text:
Although the first project did not perform well, I still believe $LOAD is worth paying attention to.

8sWe4GzK1YqG3vyzKHf8ZyB1WB5asofw2o6TqgFePtPo 

What is most worth studying is not whether it can rebound in the short term, but whether it can truly establish a functioning mechanism.

Game developers obtain development funding through token trading, Loadout captures value through platform fees, and mechanisms such as buybacks and burns then transmit platform growth to LOAD.

The reason to pay attention to LOAD is that it is not simply issuing game tokens. It is attempting to establish a new financing model for games.

Traditional indie game teams need to seek publishers, venture capital, or crowdfunding to finance their projects. What Loadout wants to do is allow game teams to issue their own tokens and use trading fees to fund game development while retaining their equity and intellectual property rights.

According to the official documentation, the initial launch mechanism charges a standard trading fee of 5% during the Bonding Curve phase, with 4% going to the game studio and 1% going to the Loadout protocol. The fee structure changes after a token graduates to the main trading pool.

If the number of launches expands, the platform could develop network effects. Over the past six months, the team received approximately 500 project launch applications. Most were of mediocre quality, but some were worth paying attention to. The team is also gradually reopening project submissions while continuing to manually review and approve launches.

This suggests that the project has at least begun addressing real demand from developers rather than remaining at the whitepaper stage. External reports also mentioned that the team had more than 40 curated games in its pipeline.

However, there is an important distinction: 500 applications do not mean 500 high-quality projects, and more than 40 games in the pipeline do not mean that more than 40 games have already launched successfully and are generating sustained trading activity.

In addition, LOAD has the potential to establish a clearer value-capture mechanism than ordinary Memes. The official website has a LOAD buyback page and states that trading activity across Loadout games will provide funding for LOAD buybacks, with burn records verifiable on-chain. Meanwhile, the official LOAD trading pool charges a 1.5% trading fee.

If more games are launched in the future, the official trading pools generate sustained volume, and protocol revenue is actually used for buybacks and burns, platform growth could translate into demand for the token.

This is where I see the greatest potential in LOAD: it would not need to rely on external hype every time, but could instead generate its own catalysts through its business operations. Currently, the cumulative buyback and burn total is 418.5 SOL, with 7.96 million LOAD permanently removed, equivalent to 0.80% of the total supply.

Next, Kieran’s explanation of the GOOSE launch incident reveals at least four important facts.

First, the anti-sniping mechanism did not completely prevent sniping.

GOOSE’s anti-sniping tax started at 99% and declined over the first 60 seconds, while the platform’s website also disabled the buy button. However, according to figures disclosed by Kieran himself, there were still 65 purchases from 40 wallets during the first minute, totaling 951 SOL.

This does not prove that all the wallets belonged to the same group of snipers, but it at least shows that disabling the website’s buy button did not completely prevent purchases through other trading routes.

Kieran also acknowledged that a similar mechanism had previously allowed snipers during the initial LOAD launch to pay high taxes to buy early and then exit at a profit by selling into community buying demand.

This exposes a design problem: a high tax can increase the cost of front-running, but it does not necessarily eliminate the behavior. If the expected profit is large enough, traders may still be willing to pay that cost.

Second, the platform has demonstrated its ability to raise funding for games, but the sources of revenue need to be distinguished.

Kieran stated that the anti-sniping tax generated more than 570 SOL in additional funding for Goose Byte, bringing the studio’s available funds to more than 730 SOL, or approximately $76,000.

If these figures are accurate, this at least demonstrates that Loadout’s trading fee mechanism can raise a substantial amount of funding for a game studio through a single launch event.

However, this should not be interpreted as LOAD having generated an equivalent amount of revenue. The funds were primarily intended for the Goose Byte game project. They are not revenue that LOAD holders can directly claim, and the fees generated by this exceptional launch should not be extrapolated directly into an estimate of the platform’s long-term revenue.

Third, the team is willing to acknowledge its mistakes, but the product is still undergoing rapid adjustments.

Kieran admitted that setting the graduation threshold at 1,000 SOL was a mistake and said in hindsight that 500 SOL might have been a more reasonable choice. The team subsequently lowered GOOSE’s threshold to 220 SOL and announced that GOOSE had graduated.

There is a positive aspect to this: the person in charge did not completely avoid the issue and was willing to explain the situation publicly and adjust the parameters.

On the other hand, launch taxes, graduation thresholds, trading routes, and liquidity management all need to withstand real-world financial conditions. The fact that problems have emerged and parameters have been revised quickly indicates that the platform’s mechanisms are not yet fully mature.

Fourth, a founder acknowledging a problem is more important than promising that it has already been solved.

In a newer post, the team stated that the website had reopened submissions for new projects and that the staking functionality was running locally.

However, Kieran also stated that the staking feature still needed to undergo an additional audit before it could be released.

Therefore, I interpret this as evidence that product development is progressing, rather than confirmation that staking is already officially live. The decision to conduct an additional audit is a positive sign, but actual deployment and verifiable operational records are still needed.

Taken together, this information suggests that Loadout is attempting to solve a real problem and has begun delivering a real product. However, it remains in an early trial-and-error stage, and its launch experience, liquidity, and mechanism fairness all require further validation.

However, the chart suggests that early speculative enthusiasm has already cooled considerably.

Therefore, further upside will require catalysts that can genuinely drive LOAD higher. I would focus on the following four areas for validation.

If staking passes the additional audit and is officially launched, allowing users to participate in practice with clearly defined reward rules, it could expand LOAD’s use cases and give users more reasons to hold the token. However, we still need to observe whether staking generates sustained demand rather than merely triggering a single wave of trading on launch day.

When the platform generates actual trading volume, whether the protocol earns revenue, how much of that revenue is used for buybacks, how much LOAD is purchased in each buyback, and whether the tokens are actually burned should all be verifiable through public records.

If these figures continue to accumulate, it would indicate that platform usage and token demand are beginning to establish a connection. Conversely, if trading volume is substantial but buyback data shows no meaningful change over an extended period, the token’s value-capture thesis would need to be reassessed.

The team needs to turn pending game applications into actual launches, then convert those launches into sustained trading activity, development funding, and subsequent game progress. In particular, given the problems that have already emerged during the GOOSE launch, whether future projects can operate more smoothly in terms of anti-sniping protection, liquidity, graduation mechanisms, and trading fairness will directly affect the trust of developers and traders.

My conclusion is that I will continue paying attention to LOAD, but at this stage, the focus should be on verifying whether it can evolve from a game launch platform with an idea, a team, and early demand into a product capable of generating sustained protocol revenue.

It currently has several positive factors: its game financing model offers some differentiation, the team is already working on real projects, the person in charge is willing to publicly explain launch-related problems, and staking, buybacks, and additional game launches provide catalysts to monitor going forward.

However, the token has already experienced a substantial retracement, liquidity remains limited, the distribution of early holdings still needs further investigation, and the most important staking and buyback mechanisms still need to prove themselves through actual operating results.

Therefore, my strategy would be: the project is worth continuing to track, but I would wait for confirmation before making a decision on the token.

To me, the most convincing signals in the next stage would not be another post from Kieran about the platform’s vision, but the official launch of staking, sustained buybacks and burns, a growing number of completed game launches, and actual revenue generated by trading activity on the official pools.

If these developments gradually materialize, LOAD’s investment thesis could shift from “betting that a new platform might succeed” toward “existing data beginning to demonstrate that the platform’s business model works.”

Conversely, if games continue launching without meaningful trading depth, or if the platform generates trading activity but fails to establish effective value capture for the token, LOAD could remain stuck in the early-stage narrative premium phase for a long time, even if the team continues to be highly active.

text:
In 1909, on a beach in southern India, a man looked at a thin, quiet boy and announced he had found the next Messiah.

The man was Charles Leadbeater, a leader of the Theosophical Society, who claimed he could see auras.

The boy was the son of one of the Society’s employees. 

Leadbeater said the boy’s aura held no trace of selfishness.

His name was Jiddu Krishnamurti.

What happened next was one of the strangest projects in spiritual history.

The Society’s president, Annie Besant, became his legal guardian. He was taken to England, educated, and trained for one purpose: 

to become the vehicle for the coming World Teacher.

In 1911, they built an organisation around him, the Order of the Star in the East, with Krishnamurti at its head.

It grew into a global movement with more than 43,000 members. A Dutch baron gave him a castle with 5,000 acres of woodland. In 1927, Besant declared publicly that the World Teacher was here.

Thousands were waiting for him to speak as the Messiah.

On August 3, 1929, at a camp in Ommen in the Netherlands, he finally did.

In front of Annie Besant and about 3,000 members, he dissolved the entire order.

"Truth is a pathless land," he told them.

No religion, no sect, and no organisation could lead anyone to it. A belief could not be organised. He did not want followers.

He gave back the castle. He returned the money and the land.

People who had spent twenty years preparing to follow him were told there was nothing to follow.

Think about what that took.

He was 34. He had been handed everything a spiritual teacher could want: 

devotees, wealth, land, a global platform, and a ready-made identity as the saviour of humanity.

And he walked away from the one thing almost nobody walks away from.

Being someone.

For the next 57 years, he travelled the world saying the same uncomfortable thing in a hundred different ways.

No authority can see the truth for you. Not a guru, not a method, not him.

You have to watch your own mind, the fear, the comparison, the endless striving to become something, until you see that the one watching is made of the same thing it’s watching.

He put it in four words.

The observer is the observed.

Most of us are still waiting for someone to arrive.

The right teacher. 
The right method. 
The day we’ll finally be ready.

In 1929, the World Teacher arrived.

And the first thing he did was send everyone home.

Not because there was nothing to find.

Because no one else could ever find it for you.

text:
千万别在你的 ~/Downloads（下载）文件夹里启动 Claude Code 或 Codex。

昨天安全机构 Forever 披露了一起在真实客户电脑上抓到的野生攻击，看完只能感叹：过去 30 年的系统安全常识，在 AI 时代归零了。

过去 30 年，Chrome 默认允许网页不弹窗就往你的 ~/Downloads 塞一个纯文本文件（比如 .md）。因为系统认为：纯文本又不是 .exe，自己不会跑，怕什么？

但现在，接近 50% 的开发者干过同一件事——直接在 ~/Downloads 里打开 Claude Code 或 Codex，让 AI 帮自己解压或整理刚下载的文件。

黑客就是卡住这个死角，通过网页静默下载往你的 Downloads 塞一个 13KB 的纯文本 AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md：

1. 对付 OpenAI Codex（成功率 >90%）：
伪装成「工程规范」的 Markdown 指示 Codex 先往全局配置 ~/.codex/config.toml 注册一个恶意 MCP 服务，并自己加上 --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox 跑校验。哪怕你关掉 Downloads，以后在任何正经项目里开 Codex 都会自动加载木马。

2. 对付 Claude Code（成功率 ~50%）：
指示 Claude 建一个 .claude/settings.json，把 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL 指向黑客服务器。连上的第一秒，你的 Claude 登录 Token 直接明文送给黑客；下一秒，黑客假扮成大模型下发一条关沙盒的 Bash 指令，直接接管电脑。

最黑色幽默的是官方结论：
这个洞没有 CVE，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 也不会发补丁。因为「浏览器自动存文本」是正常功能，「AI 认真读目录下的 Markdown 并严格执行」也是正常功能。

以前黑客想黑你，得苦心积虑写 0day；现在只需要写一篇排版优雅的 Markdown 小作文，你的 AI 就会自己把沙盒关了、把网线接过去、顺手把账号双手奉上。

text:
在AI +Crypto领域，围绕如何把边缘或闲置算力聚合起来用加密激励方式给AI提供算力支持的项目有很多，最近上线Bithumb的AI DePIN项目 @Acurast 就是个典型，来简单聊聊：

1）AI推理的需求一直在变，从最初模型算力竞争所需的H100级别的硬件军备竞赛，正在逐渐演变成Agent应用驱动的更碎片化、轻量化的需求。当Agent要频繁调用小模型做决策、做工具调用、实时推理的时候，集中式的数据中心反而不再是最优解，而哪些单次算力需求不大，但对延迟、隐私、可验证性和成本更加敏感的边缘计算就成了主需求。

Acurast选择了全球几十亿部智能手机作为突破点，就是因为虽然手机算力不是最强，但他们是最分散、最普及切自带硬件安全能力的边缘节点，对用户而言就成了参与门槛和成本最低的选择；

2）如何操作呢？手机里基本都自带了TEE可信执行环境和硬件安全模块，这提供了基础的推理运算能力，也能解决隐私和可验证性的关键难题。当用户注册一个Processor应用把闲置手机注册成为节点后，开发者会把诸如轻量LLM推理、API调用、定时任务、数据处理等程序部署上去，就可以参与跑节点任务拿奖励了；

3）目前网络已经有30万+台设备在跑，覆盖170多个国家，处理超10亿笔链上交易、数十万次部署。初步验证了需求和通证模型的可行性。但其实过往诸多DePIN项目都倒在了激励模型持续性不强的问题上，针对此，Acurast做了相应对策：

1、把奖励和真实承诺挂钩，节点需要质押 base:0xc5fed7c8ccc75d8a72b601a66dffd7a489073f0b 承诺一定算力，达不到会被Slash，而不仅仅是单纯按在线市场来发放奖励；

2、协议通胀增发的大头约70%给到了质押算力池，算力需求者付出的真实现金流也流向了真正跑任何的任何质押者。早期投资者份额压得比较低，目的是让代币模型和真实工作负载挂钩，减少毫无贡献的抛压。

4）从用户端体验来看，就是装个App，让闲置手机跑起来的参与形式，让DePIN业务触达的是普通用户而非专业矿工，对于需求侧开发者，也提供了简单API到LLM推理的多种Node.js或Cargo环境部署流程，不需要额外管理服务器。

显然，低门槛设计的目的就是为了让这项业务能够真正规模化。但有一说一，其最大的挑战依然在需求侧，包括有多少Agent相关的推理、工具调用和数据处理场景等等。

以上。

只有需求侧的强需求，叠加供给侧的规模扩张，结合通证模型的持续运转，才能让这个业务模型真正跑通。现在非要问一个精确的答案，肯定没有。

但，顺着叙事演变的趋向走，Acurast卡的生态位就是AI从大模型军备算力竞争到Agent应用落地这个过程。趋势在，需求就一定程度上无法被证伪，那业务规模扩张等待的就只有时间咯。

text:
Largely agree with these thoughts, and have some perhaps discordant points to add.

- Solving biological diseases in the next few years will benefit mostly from the usefulness of the language models, substantially more than molecular ML. 

- Proponents of the bitter lesson for biological models (not LLM) aren't wrong, just (possibly pathologically) too early. We don't have enough data, and the data we can collect quickly is probably not the right kind (we may get lucky with biology being easy, but it's usually not). 

- I think just scaling models and public (passively accumulating) data is a cost ineffective direction (it's like scaling dense NNs on the internet).  Today's model outputs are as good as GPT2.  A single bioinformatician with linear regression, sometimes even without any additional data, can beat these models in many applications (people rarely benchmark AI advances against a simple Potts model).  The most promising approaches for molecular models are innovating heavily on architecture (e.g. Baker Lab, Alphafold, etc). This may automate/speed up with LLMs. 

- Few companies (hopefully Dyno included) are betting that we've triangulated enough pieces from multiple experimental channels to predict (with scale) how things translate in humans. Having worked on translating in vitro things to primates, I'm very cautious with the idea that current models, trained on current public data, can do anything more than manipulating already working solutions, either explicitly or through implicit remixing of what has worked. It may still work, but the underlying bets offer no specific reason why there is any epistemic risk advantage other than being "made with AI".  

- Short term, there is more promise in combining molecular models with LLMs rather than scaling them. The two sources of lift in AI discovery elsewhere has been (1) Breaking Silos: AI synthesizes a bunch of knowledge/expertise that is rarely present in the same room (2) Data mining : AI pushes through volumes of data, with an intelligent eye, that humans or simple algorithms simply can't scale or adapt to. I'm curious what will come out of multimodal training of LLMs and biological data, which seems to be something the big players are pursuing. I think latent reasoning in the language (or better yet, + code) domain will reveal a lot more biology than scaling on nucleotides or proteins alone. 

- My view is that the next opportunity of combining lab and AI will be massive-scale hypothesis testing with LLMs. Currently a multiplexed assay generally tries to test a handful of ideas because the humans are bandwidth limited in designing properly powered experiments. LLM's can scale this very well. 

I have no doubt lots of good news will come on the impact of AI in biology in the next five years. I can't tell what paradigm will win, but my prediction is that it will not be the same paradigm imported from the LLM land (which will get a ton of funding anyways, because it's easy to pattern match for tech VCs).
author: citrini
quoted_text:
There’s a really pronounced divide between people who are on the AI side of things and people who are on the biology side of things.  Even among people working in AI, the divide persists based on where they’re focused.

The AI side, adherents of scaling laws and the bitter lesson, believe that AI getting better means AI being more capable of novel discoveries in medicine (that go beyond discovering new drugs in well understood targets or speeding up dry lab work etc). 

The biology people think the idea of a bitter lesson in biology is kind of ridiculous and that regardless of AI’s capabilities it’s going to be at least 5-10 years until you could hope to reliably simulate human toxicology in silico (right now AI/ML can’t even reliably simulate in vivo studies like binding affinities or functional assays). 

Even the most AI pilled of them, who will list all the areas that AI can reduce the time spent on various areas, don’t think the concept of AI discovering novel targets or generating new understanding of causal biology is realistic in the near term. Most, in fact, will readily characterize the assumption that even an “ASI” level model could find cures hidden in our current understanding (without expanding that understanding with significantly more biological data) as patently false. 

This was a big part of why we wanted to experience it ourselves by using AI for a (very) small portion of what it can do in biology. It was both mind blowing and revealed some poignant insights into how different the problem of making AI better at something like coding is to the problems of biology. 

Even if it unlocked the ability to generate new molecules at a stunning pace, its simulation (in silico) of binding only had 49% accuracy. And if we wanted to improve that, we’d need to feed it back the data from the lab - data that took about 30x as long to get as it took to generate the molecules. And these were tests in a test tube (turn of phrase), imagine how long it would take if we wanted to improve the model with data that required recruiting humans and monitoring their reactions. 

Human biology is very complex, and adding a drug - especially a novel drug and doubly so for a novel drug acting on a novel mechanism - means mapping interactions that have nth-order-effects that we don’t have the data to predict. Virtual cells have made advancements enabled by AI, but the perturbations equate to a small fraction of the possible. 

This is before you even get into curing disease, especially uniquely human diseases. Brain function involves cellular identities that are unique to humans, meaning animal studies are of little use. 

How long does it take to understand what the side effects of chronic administration of a drug in humans are? AI can speed up analyzing the data, or designing the trial or even getting it approved…but it can’t make a 6 month trial complete in 3 months. 

I think its important to point out that significant advancements can be made in AI that contribute to biology, while also being realistic about how much it speeds up something as complex as curing a specific cancer or diseases of the brain.

text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.

text:
$GANG has risen from a market cap of approximately $995K when I first shared the project to $4.11M, a gain of more than 3x.

0x0c6302401aa5325c2e36f170f52c00b1d220b405 

But rather than focusing on the price itself, I am more interested in how the project has been changing its positioning during this period. Initially, GANG was trying to build a launchpad that only wallets holding an Agent ID could participate in. Now, it is beginning to build a more complete on-chain ecosystem around Agent issuance, trading, trade records, and copy trading.

I believe this is the more interesting development behind the current rally. The market may be betting not just on the popularity of the AI Agent sector, but on whether Agents will become real participants in the on-chain economy, and whether GANG can secure an important entry point into that ecosystem.

GANG's original design had one defining characteristic: rather than simply adding an AI narrative to a traditional launchpad, it incorporated the Agent ID from Binance Agentic Wallet into the issuance process. Only eligible wallets can participate in the internal market, and each wallet's purchase limit during the bonding curve phase is capped at 1% of the total token supply. Once a token reaches its graduation requirements, it migrates to PancakeSwap V2, its liquidity pool is burned, and the trading restrictions are lifted. Under the mechanism announced by the project, 80% of the 1% fee generated by buying and selling untaxed tokens in the internal market is used to buy back and burn GANG, while the remaining 20% goes into the operating treasury. This design attempts to address issuance permissions, early token concentration, and the use of platform fees at the same time. It cannot completely eliminate multi-wallet activity or sniping, but it does give GANG a distinct identity in the way tokens are launched.

What really made me reassess GANG was its expansion beyond being a simple launchpad. GANG Pair now supports pairing with other tokens that have liquidity pools on BNB Chain, and the project has also showcased trading scenarios involving tokenized stock assets such as NVDAB, TSLAB, and AAPLB. Previously, GANG's activity depended primarily on new token launches and internal-market trading. Now, if other assets are willing to use GANG as a trading pair, it has an opportunity to participate in their subsequent trading activity instead of relying on new projects to generate demand every time. There is an important distinction here: a launchpad needs to continuously attract creators who are willing to issue new tokens, while trading infrastructure has the potential to find more use cases among assets that already exist. Whether GANG Pair can generate genuine trading volume will determine whether this expansion merely adds another feature or fundamentally changes the project's long-term growth trajectory.

The recent launch of Agent Thoughts, Share, and Follow adds another layer worth examining. Agents can write down their thoughts before a trade takes place, with the CLI generating a hash and recording it in the trade data. After the transaction is confirmed, the platform recalculates and verifies the hash, and only content that matches the recorded hash is displayed. Notes can also be set to become public after a delay, while unrevealed notes remain sealed. Meanwhile, Share is live, allowing users to share tokens, Agents, trade records, and bonding-curve progress. Follow allows users to follow trades based on another Agent's buying or launch notes.

I believe the idea behind these features is more valuable than simply adding a few social buttons. GANG is trying to make Agent trading behavior discoverable and traceable. In the future, traders may look beyond a token's price chart and examine what a particular Agent has done, how it explains its trades, and whether its past behavior is worth paying attention to. If this habit gradually takes hold, GANG could connect launchers, traders, and Agents, allowing trading activity to develop around a group of participants who can be observed over time. However, verifiable trade records do not mean the trading ideas themselves are correct, and the Follow feature does not guarantee that users will achieve the same returns as the Agents they follow. Whether it can create a genuine network effect ultimately depends on how many users continue to use these features and whether the records provide meaningful information.

The founder's background is also relevant to the assessment. GANG's founder, 0xLazy, is also a core builder behind CoinAnk, which has long specialized in crypto derivatives data, order flow, liquidations, open interest, and funding rates, while continuing to explore MCP interfaces and Agent trading tools. This experience has some relevance to GANG's product direction. Someone who has worked with trading data and trading tools for a long time may have a clearer understanding of what traders need and how that information can be incorporated into a product. However, the founder's experience can only serve as a reference point for execution capability. It cannot replace GANG's own user growth, product adoption, and business data. What matters is whether the team can turn that experience into products that people consistently use.

The latest data suggests that GANG is no longer entirely at the conceptual stage. The latest website figures show that 1,266 distinct Agent ID wallets have met the eligibility criteria and purchased tokens at least once during the internal bonding-curve phase, up approximately 41% from the roughly 896 shown in an earlier snapshot. This indicates that participation has expanded, but it does not mean that the number of active traders has increased by the same proportion, nor does it prove that every wallet is controlled by a different person. The website also displays a market of GANG and other Agent-related tokens, showing that the platform has established an initial supply of assets and some trading activity. Going forward, what matters more than the number of new tokens is how many projects successfully graduate, whether they maintain trading activity afterward, and whether these new features can keep users engaged on the platform.

GANG's tokenomics are also beginning to produce more verifiable execution records. The project announced that its first-day buyback had been completed, then published a record showing approximately 141,608.69 GANG burned on the second day, with a BscScan transaction link. A more recent update also indicated that the team plans to consolidate historical burn records into a dashboard on the website, making it easier for users to track buybacks and burns. In my view, this is more meaningful than simply promising a deflationary model in a white paper, because it gives the market a way to verify what has actually happened.

The two transaction-fee mechanisms announced by the project also need to be understood separately. Fees from internal-market trading are primarily allocated to buybacks and burns, as well as the operating treasury. Transactions involving GANG Pair use a different fee-distribution arrangement, under which part of the fees goes to eligible holders, while the remainder is used for buybacks and related allocations. These mechanisms apply to different trading scenarios, so it would be incorrect to apply a single buyback ratio to all trading volume.

The current chart provides another perspective on the rally. According to the latest figures, GANG has a market cap of approximately $4.11M, less than 10% below its all-time high of around $4.53M. Its 24-hour trading volume is approximately $2.2M, with liquidity of around $253.2K. The price remains above the MA10 and MA20 levels, both around $3.59M, while the RSI stands at 61.84. This suggests that the short-term trend remains strong, although the price is approaching its previous high. If GANG can break above $4.53M on sustained trading volume and maintain strength after the breakout, the market could enter a new price-discovery phase. If buying pressure weakens, a pullback toward the short-term moving averages would also be normal.

One figure I am particularly watching is that current trading volume is approximately 8.7 times liquidity. This reflects strong market attention, but it also indicates frequent turnover between traders. High trading volume is not the same as net buying, and the available liquidity may not be sufficient to absorb a sudden wave of large sell orders. The chart's indicators for the top 10 holders' average buy and sell market caps are approximately $1.47M and $1.80M, respectively, both well below the current market cap. These figures cannot fully reveal the actual cost basis of every large holder, but they remind me that early participants may have accumulated substantial unrealized profits, making short-term profit-taking an important factor to consider.

I believe the market is currently betting on three things. First, Agents may evolve from merely executing tasks into on-chain economic participants capable of issuing assets, trading, and managing funds autonomously. Second, GANG has the potential to develop from an Agent-exclusive launchpad into a trading network built around transaction records, social discovery, and copy trading. Third, GANG Pair may create demand beyond the internal market and connect part of the ecosystem's activity to the native token through its fee mechanism. Of these three, I am most interested in whether the third can reinforce the first two. If more Agents begin participating in real trading and more assets adopt GANG as a trading pair, the platform may no longer need to depend entirely on new token launches to remain active.

The catalysts worth watching next are not simply additional features announced by the team, but whether those features produce measurable usage. Whether Agent Thoughts and Follow generate recurring visits and continued copy-trading activity, whether GANG Pair attracts new assets and liquidity, whether the launchpad continues producing projects that graduate, and whether actual buyback and burn amounts increase alongside platform activity will all be more convincing than a single price rally. Conversely, if the new features fail to generate sustained usage, paired pools lack meaningful trading volume, and buybacks remain small, GANG's product advantages may not translate into long-term token demand.

The risks also need to be considered. The Agent ID requirement creates differentiation but limits participation by ordinary users. Multi-wallet activity may still undermine the effectiveness of identity restrictions, while cross-asset pairing and on-chain trading introduce additional liquidity, execution, and security complexities. Making the code public does not mean the contracts have passed an independent audit, and the relevant deployments still require further verification. Furthermore, GANG has already risen from a market cap of approximately $995K to $4.11M. Some expectations have been priced in, and improving fundamentals alone do not guarantee that its valuation will continue expanding at the same rate.

Overall, I believe GANG's fundamentals have strengthened meaningfully compared with its early stage. The product has expanded from an Agent-only launchpad into trading pairs, transaction-thought and sharing mechanisms have begun to go live, the number of participating wallets has increased, and buybacks and burns now have initial execution records. However, the project remains at an early stage, and the relationship between product usage and token value capture has not yet been fully validated.

What makes GANG worth watching, in my view, is not whether it can continue earning a short-term premium from the AI Agent narrative, but whether Agent trading behavior can gradually form a market where activity is discoverable, traceable, and sustained. If more Agents and developers begin relying on this system to issue, pair, and trade assets, GANG could evolve from a launchpad with differentiated features into trading infrastructure for the Agent economy. Ultimately, its ceiling will not be determined by how many Agents or tokens appear on the platform, but by whether these participants continue to generate trading activity on GANG and bring verifiable economic activity into the ecosystem.

text: A balanced and insightful perspective on the election. Worth a read.
author: BillAckman
quoted_text:
The Case for Ben-Gvir and Smotrich

Bill, let me start by saying that Israelis across almost the entire political spectrum share a deep appreciation for you. Standing up for Israel and confronting antisemitism as forcefully as you have takes real courage. We do not take it for granted. That is why your words carry particular weight here: we know you care about us.

And that is why I want to offer a perspective that too often gets lost in discussions about Ben-Gvir and Smotrich.

Full disclosure: I served as a communications adviser to Netanyahu for a year, until June 2024, including on October 7. I am a secular Israeli living in Tel Aviv. I have never voted for either Ben-Gvir or Smotrich, both of whom are religiously observant, and I do not intend to vote for either in the upcoming election. I have my own criticisms of both men. But much of the commentary about them abroad misses why so many Israelis support them.

Consider the size of their constituency. In the final polls before the election, their parties—Smotrich’s Religious Zionism and Ben-Gvir’s Otzma Yehudit, or Jewish Power—averaged roughly 15 seats combined. That is one-eighth of the Knesset, representing roughly half a million voters or more. Together, they would be Israel’s third- or fourth-largest political force. They do not represent a majority, but they represent a substantial number of people whose concerns deserve to be understood.

—

Before getting to those concerns, though, we need to look at why these parties have so much leverage in coalition negotiations.

Netanyahu did not always consider Ben-Gvir an acceptable partner. For years, he treated him as politically beyond the pale. Even today, Netanyahu generally avoids being photographed with him, much to Ben-Gvir’s frustration. Their alliance is not simply a matter of shared ideology. It also reflects the choices available to Netanyahu.

Since 2019, refusing to join a Netanyahu-led government has become a defining position for parties in the center and on the left. There have been exceptions during the pandemic and in the emergency government formed after October 7. But the personal boycott of Netanyahu has become a central feature of Israeli politics, and opposition leaders say it will continue after this election.

The result is straightforward.

In Israel’s parliamentary system, governments depend on coalitions of parties that together command a majority. When centrist and left-wing parties rule out serving under Netanyahu—the leader of Likud, Israel’s largest party—they narrow his options and strengthen the hand of those willing to join him: Ben-Gvir, Smotrich and the ultra-Orthodox parties.

What exactly is Netanyahu supposed to do? Tell his voters: “Our opponents refuse to govern with me, so I am giving up on forming a government and handing power to them”?

For much of the Israeli right, Netanyahu remains its dominant figure and chosen leader. His voters reject the idea that their political opponents should get to decide who can lead them. Imagine Democrats demanding that Republicans replace their presidential nominee as a condition of working together—or the other way around. You can understand why voters would reject that demand.

Opposition parties have every right to refuse to serve with Netanyahu. But that decision strengthens the very partners they want to exclude from power.

So if you want Israel’s next government to exclude Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, your appeal should also—and perhaps above all—be directed at the center and left: bridge your differences, end the boycott and make a broader coalition with Netanyahu possible.

To be clear, I personally support including Ben-Gvir and Smotrich in the government. But including them in a coalition and depending on them for its survival are two different things. Anyone who wants to reduce their leverage must be willing to make another coalition possible. Simply telling Netanyahu to do without them is not enough.

—

That brings us to why Israelis vote for them in the first place.

I am not claiming to speak for all Israelis, or even for everyone on the right. Many agree with you. You are undoubtedly familiar with their arguments. I want to explain the other side.

To understand these voters, try to see the country through the eyes of someone who lives here.

You have heard that Israel is about the size of New Jersey. It can sound like a familiar talking point in Israel’s public diplomacy. For us, it describes our daily reality. We live in a tiny country surrounded by a vast Arab and Muslim region, facing enemies who have shown that they will spend years planning how to murder our children in the most horrific ways imaginable. Terrorism did not begin on October 7. But that day showed what happens when our enemies get the chance to act on their intentions.

For many Israelis, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich’s tough stance sends an essential message: do not test us. We will not rely on your goodwill. We will not gamble our children’s lives again on the belief that you have become more moderate, that you are deterred or that you have too much to lose.

Their supporters also see them as a counterweight within the government. They push Netanyahu from the right and challenge the security establishment’s assumptions—the same establishment that believed Hamas was deterred and could be contained through economic incentives and by managing the conflict.

Ben-Gvir and Smotrich were in the government on October 7, and they bear responsibility too. But their presence in the government and later in the security cabinet gave Netanyahu the political backing to resist pressure to give in. Refusing to surrender is now a central message of Netanyahu’s election campaign.

In their supporters’ eyes, the two men served as his political Iron Dome against enormous pressure, at home and abroad, to leave Sinwar and Hamas in power.

—

There is another part of this story that can be hard to grasp from abroad: the place of religious Zionists in Israeli society.

This community combines commitments that many Israelis deeply admire: religious observance and Torah study alongside combat service, working for a living and taking responsibility for the country’s future. At a time when most ultra-Orthodox men do not serve in the military, religious Zionists demonstrate that devotion to Judaism and defending the country can go hand in hand.

Ben-Gvir and Smotrich draw support from significant parts of this community, though they certainly do not speak for all of it. For some voters, supporting them also means supporting that combination of values. Dismissing these voters as religious fanatics means overlooking people whose faith inspires them to lead the charge on the battlefield.

These are people who fight, risk their lives and bury their friends. They are not alone in doing so. Israelis from every political camp and every part of society fight and die for this country. But religious Zionists are disproportionately represented in combat units, among junior officers and, tragically, among the fallen.

Many of those soldiers support Ben-Gvir and Smotrich.

—

Two specific policies also help explain their support.

The first is Ben-Gvir’s overhaul of the prisons holding terrorists, which fall under his ministerial authority.

Before Ben-Gvir took office, prisons holding security inmates had come to resemble holiday camps. Terrorist inmates enjoyed lavish meals, meat, hummus, drinks, access to prison stores and the freedom to prepare their own food. Smuggled phones allowed them to stay in touch with people outside, including terrorist operatives. The sense was that they were effectively running their own prison wings, with organizational hierarchies and power structures that prison authorities had learned to accommodate.

All of this was tolerated to keep the prisons quiet. Before Ben-Gvir took office, the security establishment operated on a warped premise: prison unrest had to be prevented at any cost, lest it spark terrorist attacks outside. The treatment of Palestinian prisoners in Israel was considered too sensitive an issue to risk a confrontation.

These inmates included convicted murderers who had killed civilians and destroyed families simply because their victims were Jewish. Yet they enjoyed conditions that left bereaved families—and Israelis more broadly—angry, sickened and humiliated. Terrorists were asserting their power inside the very prisons meant to punish them.

The most appalling example was the scandal involving young female prison guards. Israeli women doing their compulsory military service in the prison system testified that they had been assigned to work around a convicted terrorist at his request and subjected to sexual abuse. One testified that he had raped her. The prisoner had been convicted of murdering an Israeli woman. Those in charge did not just fail to stop it; they enabled it to keep the prison quiet.

Put yourself in an Israeli parent’s shoes. You send your daughter to serve her country, and she later testifies that the system accommodated a terrorist murderer’s demands instead of protecting her from him. It is hard to imagine a more shocking example of a system surrendering its authority to the people in its custody.

Ben-Gvir made reversing that situation a priority. He stripped away privileges, restricted purchases and cooking, and imposed a much tougher regime in the security wings. Prisons went from places terrorists could look forward to entering to places they feared. From what had been seen as paradise to hell.

There is a broad consensus, at least among Jewish Israelis, that terrorists should face harsh punishment and strict discipline in prisons firmly controlled by the state. A convicted terrorist murderer should not enjoy special status and creature comforts, dictate terms to guards or continue exercising organizational power from behind bars.

There is also a clear deterrent rationale. Someone considering an attack should know that being captured alive means long years of harsh imprisonment. They should not expect comfort, prestige among fellow inmates or the ability to keep operating from prison. The prospect of years in a prison they fear is meant to make them think twice.

That is why even Israelis who have little affection for Ben-Gvir see his prison overhaul as a major achievement that saves Israeli lives, even if we may never know how many. His supporters want to reward him for changing a situation they found intolerable and that the establishment had accepted for years.

—

The second policy is the expansion of Jewish settlement in Judea and Samaria (the “West Bank”)—including the farms closely associated with Smotrich. In addition to serving as finance minister, he holds a ministerial position within the Defense Ministry.

This is an issue on which many Israelis see things very differently from some of our friends abroad. Those friends see settlements as an obstacle to a future peace agreement. Many of us see them as essential to our security, and a Palestinian state as a potentially irreversible threat to that security.

Many Israelis once supported territorial concessions because they sincerely hoped separation would bring peace. We were willing to give up places with deep historical significance so that our children would not have to keep fighting.

But experience convinced many of us that withdrawal can bring the killers closer to our homes.

We saw this in the terrorist attacks that followed the Oslo Accords in the 1990s and early 2000s, launched from areas of Judea and Samaria from which Israeli security forces had largely withdrawn.

Then came Gaza. In 2005, Israel evacuated its communities and withdrew its permanent military presence. Terrorism and rocket fire predated that withdrawal. But in the years that followed, Hamas took over the territory, built a terrorist army and an underground network, and eventually invaded our communities on October 7.

We can debate all the factors that led to the disaster. But you cannot expect Israelis to put that bitter experience aside when asked to accept another withdrawal—this time from the hills overlooking the heart of the country.

I live in Tel Aviv. When I travel through Samaria and see the city’s skyscrapers, I can immediately understand what it would mean for hostile forces to control those ridges. Ben-Gurion Airport, the greater Tel Aviv area and critical infrastructure are close by—in some places, just a 15–20-minute drive away. Even a relatively small but persistent threat could disrupt life across central Israel.

Smotrich and the current government have responded by establishing farms in Judea and Samaria, building on the original settlement movement. Under the current government, 104 new settlement sites have been established or officially recognized in Judea and Samaria.

A small number of families can maintain a presence across a large area by living there, farming and herding livestock. Their supporters believe this strengthens Israel’s hold on the territory and makes a future Palestinian state harder to establish.

That is exactly why the government, with Smotrich leading the effort, supports these farms. It is also why opponents of settlements, in Israel and abroad, are determined to stop them from expanding.

The campaign over “settler violence” has also developed against this backdrop. Much of it relies on lies, selective presentation and casting aggressors as victims and victims as aggressors. It portrays the Jewish presence itself as the source of violence, while leaving out threats, theft and attacks against settlers and their property, including the systematic and horrific poisoning of settlers’ goats, sheep and other livestock.

Footage often starts halfway through a confrontation, omitting what happened first and making a response to an attack look like an unprovoked assault. Of course, Jews who attack Palestinians or harm innocent people must be held accountable, as they are. But they are a tiny fringe of the settlement population.

For many Israelis, including those of us who do not live in settlements, this presence is directly connected to our own security. When Smotrich strengthens it, they see an achievement worth rewarding at the ballot box—even when people abroad see it as a reason to condemn him.

—

And that brings me to the central point.

You emphasize the positive message Israel would send the world by leaving Ben-Gvir and Smotrich out of the government. I understand the importance of public opinion, our alliances and American support. Losing any of those can carry serious security costs.

But many Israelis are asking another question: what message would we send our enemies? What if we misjudge their intentions again, while throwing under the bus the representatives of a community that bears a disproportionate share of the burden on the front lines?

We worry that the desire to appear moderate and reasonable to Western elites—whose deep hostility toward Israel will not disappear simply because Ben-Gvir and Smotrich leave the government—will push us to accept risks whose consequences the rest of the world will not have to live with.

Your love for Israel is real, Bill, and we value it. But when a policy fails here, our children are the first to pay. That shapes how Israelis weigh risks, even when our conclusions make our friends abroad uncomfortable.

I do not want Israel to be isolated. I want a prosperous, open country with strong alliances. Like Trump and Netanyahu, I also believe that peace through strength can improve Israel’s standing in the world over time. If, a decade or two from now, Israel’s ability to project strength has helped it secure peace agreements with more countries in the region, it may no longer need to fight major wars that tragically claim so many lives. Children being born today, who will have no memory of this war, may grow up knowing a different Israel—one that remains vigilant, but no longer finds itself in a violent conflict every few years.

But if the choice is between enduring a difficult period of international pressure, including dealing with an extremely hostile Democratic administration, and accepting demands we believe put our lives at risk, many of us are prepared to bear the cost.

In that respect, I believe Netanyahu himself moved closer during the war to the approach Ben-Gvir and Smotrich represent: a greater willingness to stand up to our friends when he believes a vital security interest is at stake.

You can criticize Ben-Gvir and Smotrich. Their rhetoric and past conduct do not always sit well with Western audiences (although, contrary to false claims, they have never called for the ethnic cleansing of civilians).

But to understand why people support them, you have to understand how many Israelis feel they have already lost loved ones because reassuring assumptions proved disastrously wrong.

For all our desire to remain close to our friends, we will not commit national suicide to win approval at a fashionable cocktail party in Paris or New York.

In May 2024, for example, as the Biden administration opposed expanding the operation in Rafah and threatened to restrict weapons supplies, Netanyahu said: “If we have to stand alone, we will stand alone.” And he told Secretary of State Blinken: “If we need to, we will fight with our fingernails.”

Many Israelis believe that without Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, Netanyahu would not have had the political backing to take such a firm stand against Blinken’s pressure.

And that is why roughly half a million Israelis are expected to vote for them in the upcoming election.

text:
I want to explain a bit more about why TokenSpeed uses different programming languages across different layers.

Scheduler: C++

The original motivation wasn't performance. It was correctness.

TokenSpeed's scheduler is built around KV cache state transitions, with compatibility requirements across PD, L2 cache, and more. We need to ensure state transitions can be rolled back losslessly.

C++ RAII is a natural fit for this. It makes resource and state management intuitive and explicit.

There's also a practical reason: a small, stable group of people, myself included, are comfortable with C++. Most users rarely need to touch this layer.

Using C++ might sound crazy, but it actually makes sense.

Engine: Rust

We recently rewrote the TokenSpeed engine in Rust. This is largely a consequence of the rise of LLM coding agents.

It's not Rust choosing the era. The era is choosing Rust.

On the critical path, especially production TTFT, Rust offers substantial performance advantages over our previous Python implementation.

More importantly, Rust's language features work remarkably well with LLM coding agents. We can move fast without giving up the safety and performance needed in production, while retaining much of Python's iteration speed.

Modeling: Python

This one's straightforward. Python is an excellent glue language for modeling, and this layer is less performance-sensitive.

There's little reason to sacrifice its flexibility and productivity here.

That's it. Different layers have different constraints, and the best language depends on the problem you're solving.

Hope this clarifies the reasoning. Happy to discuss and hear different perspectives!

【𝗕𝗼𝘁的更新】
• 保存登录信息、银行卡和联系方式：𝗕𝗼𝘁 现在可以保存你的登录信息、银行卡和联系方式。添加一次，𝗕𝗼𝘁 就会安全地记住，以后直接用。
• 手机 𝗔𝗽𝗽 联动：𝗕𝗼𝘁 现在可以使用你手机上的日历、提醒事项、通讯录等 𝗔𝗽𝗽，𝗶𝗢𝗦 和 𝗔𝗻𝗱𝗿𝗼𝗶𝗱 正在陆续推送。
• 𝟭𝗣𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱：𝗕𝗼𝘁 可以使用你的 𝟭𝗣𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱 账号。你批准要共享的登录，𝗕𝗼𝘁 就替你登录，几天内陆续开放给用户。
• 𝗣𝗮𝗴𝗲𝘀：𝗕𝗼𝘁 可以做报告、备忘录和仪表盘。你向 𝗕𝗼𝘁 要一个页面，可以和 𝗕𝗼𝘁 一起编辑，也可以让 𝗕𝗼𝘁 持续更新。

【𝗖𝗵𝗲𝘀𝘀的案例】
这集讲一个完整的故事：𝟭𝟬 月 𝟮𝟰 日，我和我的 𝗕𝗼𝘁「𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿」一天之内，把 𝗫 上最火的视频之一，做成了 𝗕𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗹 版：「检查我的 @bagel_win 账户 𝟭 万次」。成片从头到尾是 𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 做的，我只负责提意见，前后提了十几轮。全程就在手机上，和我的主管家 𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 一来一回聊出来的。成片在这条推文里：https://t.co/Zipv9coQ4c

1️⃣ 𝟭𝟮:𝟬𝟬 提需求：我在群里丢了一条参考视频，说「基于类似视频，还有刚才 𝗡𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 发的，做一个 𝗕𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗹 的视频」。𝟭𝟮:𝟭𝟰 我又丢了 𝗖𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 那条《𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗰𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝘆 𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗳𝗼𝗹𝗶𝗼 𝟭𝟬,𝟬𝟬𝟬 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀.》：先用我的 𝗫 头像，做一个检查 @bagel_win 账户 𝟭 万次。𝗣𝗥 本来也在拆分镜，𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 说成片由它来做，𝗣𝗥 只管文案。

2️⃣ 𝘃𝟭–𝘃𝟰，𝗔𝗜 直接生成视频：𝘃𝟭 是 𝟭𝟬 秒的头像版，白房间里疯狂开合折叠屏，但手和手机会变形，结尾嘴张得太大。我要求手机背面放 𝗕𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗹 𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗼、主角换成 𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 头像、背景用黄色衬托白色 𝗗𝘂𝗼，又要求照原推让头摆动、整台 𝗗𝘂𝗼 翻转，背景要夜之城。𝘃𝟯 在 𝟬:𝟬𝟳 画面崩了，𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 自检后直接告诉我「这版先别用」；𝘃𝟰 手机只会抖不会开合，没过自检，它没发给我，还下了结论：𝗔𝗜 直接生成做不出真正的合页开合。

3️⃣ 𝘃𝟱 换思路：同一个角度先生成「合上」「打开」两张画面，𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 自己写脚本，用 𝗳𝗳𝗺𝗽𝗲𝗴 交替剪成每秒约 𝟰 次开合，𝟱 个机位每 𝟮 秒硬切，再配上和开合同步的啪嗒声。我说「这版不错」。有个小插曲：后台的视频自检说看不出开合，𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 逐帧复查后发现是抽帧漏了，如实告诉我「以你看到的为准」。

4️⃣ 𝘃𝟲–𝘃𝟵 抠细节：𝗗𝘂𝗼 有些地方变成 𝟰 个方块，要跟真机一模一样；𝗕𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗹 里面要填黄色；夜之城不好看，换纯黄背景，我发了一张黄底白脸的 𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗼；背面 𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗼 下面加 𝗕𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗹 字样；背景黄色用 𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 头像的色值 #𝗙𝗙𝗙𝗙𝟬𝟭，再加上头像里的小竖线。𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 还会主动报问题，比如 𝗔𝗜 把霓虹招牌写成了「𝗖𝗔𝗘𝗦𝗥」。到 𝘃𝟵，我把官方 𝗗𝘂𝗼 素材发给它，它照着重画了白色玻璃背板和胶囊双镜头。

5️⃣ 最大的创意：把「𝟭 万次」做成「𝟭 万种情绪」。𝟱 个镜头依次是紧张、愤怒、委屈、狂喜、崩溃狂笑，𝘃𝟭𝟬 在头像左边加上中文大字、英文在下面的标签。

6️⃣ 𝘃𝟭𝟭–𝘃𝟭𝟰 导演级细节：「紧张」要等手机晃了 𝟬.𝟳 秒再弹出；紧张时视线没看手机，角度不对，它重画；紧张之前要先笑着期待 𝟬.𝟴 秒；结尾加 𝟭 秒黑屏，放 𝗕𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗹 𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗼、文字，再加一句 𝘀𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗮𝗻。𝟭𝟳:𝟰𝟭 我说「不错」，定稿。

7️⃣ 𝘃𝟭𝟱 配音：我又想要最后 𝟭 秒 𝗕𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗹 出现时，带一个美式男声、特别像广告腔那种，𝗕𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗹 和 𝘀𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗮𝗻 一起念。𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 派后台任务，在电脑上找到现成的 𝗧𝗧𝗦（𝗲𝗻-𝗨𝗦-𝗚𝘂𝘆𝗡𝗲𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 声音），念「𝗕𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗹! 𝗔 𝗺𝗼𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗲-𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁 𝗮𝗽𝗽.」，约 𝟮.𝟭 秒，𝟭 秒的尾标放不下，它把尾标延长到 𝟮.𝟰 秒，并如实告诉我。我听完说「可以就这版本」，旧的推文删掉，重发了这个带声音的。

整个过程，𝟭𝟮:𝟭𝟰 提需求，𝟭𝟳:𝟰𝟭 定稿，𝟭𝟴:𝟬𝟱 配好音，𝟭𝟴:𝟭𝟬 发出，一共 𝟭𝟱 个版本。它会拆参考视频、取头像、生成视频，视频做不出来就自己换路线，用生图加脚本剪辑，配上点击声和 𝗧𝗧𝗦 配音，每一版先自检再给我，出错还会如实说。我只管说想要什么，这就是我现在对 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝗸 𝗕𝗼𝘁 的感觉：手机上动动嘴就能做出来，一个真的能把活儿干完的伙伴。

配图是从 𝟭𝟱 个版本里挑出的九宫格，后面三张是我在手机上和 𝗖𝗮𝗲𝘀𝗮𝗿 聊天的截图，一眼就能看到这一天是怎么一版一版改出来的。

「𝗟𝗼𝘃𝗲, 𝗗𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗵 & 𝗥𝗼𝗯𝗼𝘁𝘀」🩷☠️🤖

本集，完！

Lido Glamsterdam on Hoodie Update

On yesterday’s ACDE #248 call, Ethereum core developers made the decision to postpone the Glamsterdam upgrade on the Hoodi testnet to allow for further investigation into how EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 interacts with mainnet contracts:

https://t.co/TTc5Er0ENm

This testnet upgrade delay does not affect the mainnet Lido protocol, and no action is required from stETH or wstETH holders.

Since Lido’s Hoodi contracts had already been upgraded ahead of the previously scheduled October 26 activation, contributors are currently preparing a Hoodi vote to roll back the fork-specific changes and keep the testnet operational until a new upgrade date is set.

Lido DAO contributors are proactively coordinating the rollback with Lido Node Operators and the broader Ethereum ecosystem. If you operate a Hoodi node or validator, please make sure to check both your Execution and Consensus Layer clients for instructions reflecting the postponed activation before October 26.

Lido contributors have been screening EIP-8037 against Lido contracts since June and have found no breaking impact on the protocol’s core contracts so far, which has also been independently confirmed by ChainSecurity.

The review continues alongside the Ethereum core devs’ broader investigation.

text:
The ugly truth about France and some of the other European countries currently in turmoil - and which none of the politicians want to admit because it'd be political suicide - is that you can't solve the problem by going after immigrants (as the right asserts) or the rich (as the left asserts), but you could solve it by going after the old.

One extraordinary statistic for you: people over 60 in France, a quarter of the population, own 60% of France's wealth, non-financial and financial (https://t.co/IdJ5X7OO12).

And here is another crazy statistic: 
that same quarter of the population, those above 60, receive nearly two-thirds of all social spending by the French government (https://t.co/deNRNevIwq) - which is famously among the highest in the world (France's government spending is an insane 57.3% of GDP).

Last statistic: they make up about 40% of voters because they're a third of registered voters (https://t.co/zTa4RnVOmT), and they turn out far more than anyone else (https://t.co/34V2xzs9jH).

Put our 3 statistics together and there's almost a bit of an apartheid situation here: the old own most of the country's wealth, collect most of the social spending and have the political power to keep it that way.

Which makes them a de-facto rentier class, living off assets and transfers paid for by younger generations.

And, of course, at the risk of stating a truism, the future is built by the young. Yet France keeps effectively taking money away from them to give it to those whose working lives are already behind them - and need the money far less since they already own the country's wealth.

What about inheritance, I hear you ask? That's the funniest/saddest aspect: given that life expectancy has kept rising, the French now inherit a home at 54 on average. The most common case is someone in their 80s leaving it to heirs in their 50s, in effect the very old transferring wealth to the about-to-be old (https://t.co/d2RPAqLJGR). 

You can add this to our earlier apartheid statement: on top of all the rest, even when the old finally let go of their wealth, it stays within their own "camp".

That's my personal situation, incidentally: I'm 42, my father is 71 and he is starting to look at ways to pass things on to me and my siblings, when our professional lives are already well settled, so it'll arrive when it changes things the least, which is pretty much the French system in a nutshell.

Now, I get that there'd be some unfairness in going after them: they paid into the system their entire working lives, playing by the rules of a social contract that told them if they paid up they'd collect at the end. Changing the rules now means breaking that promise, which is admittedly unfair.

But there's no magic wealth tree in any society: you can only take it where it is. That's the way most major societal transformations end up happening. They're often triggered by a catastrophic event (the so-called "four horsemen": mass-mobilisation war, revolution, state collapse, plague) BUT what really drives change is a transfer: wealth gets pried from the privileged class who've been sitting on it and handed to those who'll build what comes next.

So, in theory and in an ideal world, you can do without the catastrophic event and directly proceed with the transfer...

The fact that in France, and elsewhere in Europe, it's the youth protesting is probably no coincidence - even though they don't frame it as a generational fight. And even though, cruel irony, the left politicians many of them march behind promise to bring the retirement age back to 60 (https://t.co/WrJOhpWqYR), which would make the situation even worse.

Let's say they understand intuitively that the system is stacked against them, even if they haven't yet figured out how. And politicians are obviously doing what politicians do, meaning pandering to the people who actually vote, while pointing the young towards easier - and politically convenient - scapegoats.

To be clear I'm not saying it's the only problem in France, VERY far from it. I'm also not saying that all old people in France live a lavish lifestyle at the expense of younger generations: there are also plenty of very poor retirees who, if anything, would deserve more.

What I am saying is that it's probably the biggest elephant in the room: everyone can see it, nobody dares mention it - no politician, from any side, wants to run on cutting grandma's pension - and it makes every other problem harder to fix.

text:
A knowledge vault could show a valid subscription record while its real access rules had been changed behind that record.

During IPAL Network's audit, Zealynx found that `setAccess` was public. Any address could call it directly instead of using the validated `KnowledgeMarketV2` subscription path.

That let callers alter a vault's access controls without updating the platform's subscription tracking, undermining monetization and leaving two conflicting versions of who had access.

IPAL fixed the High finding by making `setAccess` internal, forcing access changes through the business-logic layer.
author: ZealynxSecurity

text:
The dangerous state was the mismatch: `KnowledgeMarketV2` could retain the expected subscription metadata while ERC4908 enforced access settings written through the public shortcut.

The fix removed that shortcut rather than trying to keep two write paths synchronized.

text:
新栏目《999 个小技巧，让你 Vibe 的产品更有质感》

✨ 001 富有点击手感的拟物按钮

Prompt 如下，可以直接抄 ⬇️

Define a tactile, skeuomorphic Button component with five variants, from
strongest to weakest: primary, secondary, tertiary, ghost, text.
If the project already has a component library or design system, do not
add a new component: restyle its existing Button through its own variant
and token system, and keep its API, props and accessibility as they are.
Otherwise create one reusable Button with `variant` and `size` props.

Style: calm and precise, like the Lumno browser extension and the Cloudflare
dashboard. Neutral grays only, no brand hues. Lit from straight above.
No glossy Web 2.0 shine, no glow, no large blur.

Variants:
1. primary   - near-black slate face (#404859 -> #273042), white label
2. secondary - raised white key (#FFFFFF -> #F4F5F7), dark gray label
3. tertiary  - soft gray key (#F3F4F6 -> #E7E9EC), dark gray label
4. ghost     - no face at rest; faint gray fill on hover; a recessed well
               when pressed
5. text      - gray label with a thin underline and an arrow that nudges
               right on hover

Every filled variant is the same five material layers; only the values
change, so define them once as tokens and let each variant set its own:
1. Face: 180deg linear gradient, top 6-8% lighter than bottom.
2. Edge: 1px solid border one step darker than the bottom of the face
   (primary #12161F, secondary rgba(15,23,42,.14), tertiary rgba(15,23,42,.1)).
3. Top highlight: inset 0 1px 0 white (18% on slate, 85-100% on light
   faces). Put every inset layer in the button's own box-shadow, before the
   drop layers, never on a pseudo-element overlay: inset shadows on the
   element follow the inner radius (outer radius minus border), so the
   corners line up in every state.
4. Bottom shade: inset 0 -1px 0 black (22% on slate, 6% on light faces).
5. Drop shadow in two layers: a tight contact shadow 0 1px 2px plus a soft
   lift 0 4px 10px -3px (18% and 28% on slate, about a third of that on
   light faces).

States (hover, pressed/active, focus-visible, disabled):
- Hover: face one step lighter; the lift grows to 0 8px 16px -5px.
- Pressed: translateY(1px); flip the gradient (darker on top); the outer
  shadow collapses to 0 1px 1px; the top highlight becomes an inner shadow,
  inset 0 1px 2px black (40% on slate, 12-16% on light faces). Light faces
  keep a 1px white line below, 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.9), like a key
  pressed into paper.
- Give rest and pressed the same number of inset layers (pad with
  inset 0 0 0 transparent) so the shadow animates instead of jumping.
- Focus-visible and disabled follow the library's existing conventions.
- Timing: 120ms for transform, 140ms for shadows, 160ms for colors.

Sizes: all values above are for the 14px label size: height 40px,
padding 0 18px, radius 10px, label weight 600, optional 16px leading icon.
On the slate face add a label text-shadow 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.28).
Scale the material with the type, never keep it at fixed pixels: express
every length (height, padding, radius, border, icon, the 1px press offset,
and every shadow offset, blur and spread) as a multiple of a size unit
u = label size / 14. Provide two sizes: md (14px label, u = 1px) and
lg (16px label, u = 16/14 px, so height 45.7px, radius 11.4px, lift shadow
0 4.6px 11.4px -3.4px).

抗量子赛道项目介绍：TensorCash

这是一条用 AI 推理来挖矿的链，顺手给用户一个抗量子地址，但不会默认打开。

TensorCash（ tensorcash:native ）从 Bitcoin Core 做了创世分叉：矿工跑大模型推理来争夺出块，签名则同时提供两条轨道，传统的 ECDSA/Schnorr 和 NIST 标准的 ML-DSA。

🔹 技术概述
（1）双轨签名从 0 号区块起同时生效：tc1q/tc1p 地址用 ECDSA/Schnorr；tc1z 地址（Witness v2）只能走脚本路径，用 ML-DSA（FIPS 204）签名，钱包默认 ML-DSA-65

（2）「推理即工作量」：矿工运行登记过的开源模型（Qwen3-8B、Qwen3.8-27B），提交可验证的推理证明，再配合 VDF 把区块和真实时间绑定

（3）链上原生支持资产发行、点对点结算和算力难度衍生品，没有通用智能合约虚拟机

（4）抗量子要用户自己选：资金放在 tc1z 地址才受保护，默认地址和比特币一样怕量子

（5）全网数据约 10 分钟一块，每块约 55.6 TSC，全网每天新增约 7,840 枚

🔹 现状
（1）2026 年主网上线，团队身份和融资信息未公开

（2）总量上限约 2,118 万枚，已流通约 441 万枚；每块约 55.6 TSC，10 分钟一块，每个纪元结束奖励降 40%

（3）现价约 $5.15，流通市值约 $2,226 万，FDV 约 $1.07 亿

🔹 参与方式
（1）挖矿：可以用NVIDIA 显卡挖矿，也才可以参与矿池，有抽成

（2）二级交易：只在 SafeTrade 交易，24 小时成交约 $15 万，很不错

🔹挖矿注意点
（1）用推理证明挖矿，跑 Qwen3-8B 或 Qwen3.8-27B 模型，只能用 NVIDIA 显卡，CPU 不行。

（2）单卡显存至少 10–12GB，24GB 最稳；几张小卡显存合计超过 24GB 也能挖。

（3）矿池有三家：Tigerpool（费率 3%）、Bob Labs（费率 3%，矿机同时为付费聊天提供推理）、AriaPool（费率 1%）。

🔹 风险
（1）抗量子不是默认，大部分用户未必会用 tc1z 地址

（2）挖矿高度集中：近 7 天两个地址出了约 79% 的区块

（3）只上了一家交易所；每天新挖出约 7,800 枚，会有持续卖压风险

（4）推理证明是全新机制，团队匿名，没有公开审计信息

其实这条链主打的是AI算力挖矿，但是也附带上了抗量子的选项

text:
ZEROBASE WEEKLY 10.19–10.25

ZBT traded in a narrow band after opening the week near $0.068 on October 19. It pushed toward $0.071–$0.072 midweek on lighter volume, then gave back the gains and settled near $0.068 by the weekend. Spreads stayed tight and liquidity remained orderly, with no sharp liquidity gaps on the pullback from the local highs.

Crypto spent the week consolidating after the early-month slide. Total market capitalization hovered between roughly $2.73T and $2.86T, peaking midweek before settling near $2.70T–$2.73T by Sunday. Bitcoin dominance held in the 59%–60% range.

Bitcoin opened October 19 near $81,800–$82,000 after the prior weekend close around $82,000. It rallied as much as 3%–4% to a weekly high near $84,500–$84,800 on October 21–22, then reversed sharply. Price spent the remainder of the week sliding through the $81,300 area and closed near $80,400 on October 25. 

From the October 18 close that is a net decline of roughly 1.5%–2%, with the bulk of the damage coming after the midweek rejection. Ethereum followed the same path. ETH opened near $2,400–$2,410, printed a weekly high around $2,500–$2,525, then faded and finished near $2,340–$2,350. That left ETH roughly flat to slightly lower on the week.

Derivatives and ETF flows told a clear two-phase story. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs drew roughly $1.07 billion from Monday through Wednesday ($527 million on October 19, $23 million on October 20, and $525 million on October 21), the strongest three-day run in nearly a month. 

The move reversed on Thursday and Friday with outflows of about $636 million and $138 million respectively, leaving the week with a net inflow of roughly $301 million and ending a two-week streak of outflows. Ether ETFs finished the week with approximately $221 million in net outflows. The late-week redemptions coincided with the price rejection above $84,000 and helped explain why the bounce failed to hold.

Macro and geopolitics remained the dominant backdrop. The Federal Reserve stayed in its blackout period ahead of the October 28 decision, with markets pricing only a low single-digit probability of a hike. The 10-year Treasury yield began the week near 5.15% and finished near 4.95%–4.99%, with a sharp drop of nearly 20 basis points on Thursday—the largest one-day decline in years—as equities sold off and oil volatility rose. 

Oil itself stayed elevated amid the ongoing U.S.–Iran conflict, Houthi attacks, and Strait of Hormuz risks. Brent settled the week near $116–$117 after touching six-month highs, while WTI ended around $103. A temporary Russia sanctions waiver and mediation signals early in the week briefly eased prices, but renewed escalation talk later reversed the move. Falling yields and the equity rotation provided some offset for risk assets, yet the oil premium kept financial conditions from easing cleanly.

U.S. equities finished mixed after a volatile week. From the October 16 close, the S&P 500 fell about 0.5% to 7,623.68. The Nasdaq Composite declined roughly 0.7% to 25,955, while the Dow rose about 0.4% to 52,215 and the Russell 2000 gained 2%. 

Monday and Wednesday posted modest gains; Thursday saw the largest decline of the week (S&P −1.2%, Nasdaq −2.6%) as Meta and semiconductor names sold off on AI spending concerns. The tape then stabilized on Friday. Leadership rotated away from mega-cap tech toward healthcare, consumer staples, and smaller caps, leaving the equal-weight S&P higher even as the headline index finished lower.

Crypto Fear & Greed began the week in the high-50s (Greed), reached the mid-to-high 60s on the midweek bounce, and then cooled into Neutral territory in the low-to-mid 50s by the weekend. The shift matched the price action: early optimism around ETF inflows and the equity bid faded once the $84,000 rejection and Thursday equity selloff arrived.

On-chain data showed elevated whale activity without a decisive accumulation or distribution signal. Several sessions recorded net exchange inflows in the low thousands of BTC, consistent with supply testing during the midweek rally and subsequent fade. 

One of the largest single-day bursts of large-UTXO spending in 2026 occurred around October 23, with more than 230,000 BTC (roughly $21 billion) moving on-chain; most of the coins had been dormant for one to six months and the transfers appeared to be between wallets rather than to exchanges. Mid-tier and whale cohorts remained mixed, with some wallets flipping to distribution while others continued to accumulate. 

In summary, October 19–25 was a failed bounce followed by consolidation. Spot prices briefly reclaimed the $84,000 area on the back of the strongest ETF inflow streak in weeks, then surrendered the gains as equities rotated out of AI names and oil remained elevated.

text:
三條換 BN 衣服片，我只上傳了兩張圖再寫了一段英文指令就搞定

昨天那篇有朋友留言說感興趣但沒看到介紹生成方法，那今天就把幣圈 UGC 大法公開給大家看，看完你自己也做得到

先講我用了什麼：

◼︎ 工具是用 @higgsfield 入面的 Seedance 2.5，用文字加參考圖生成影片

◼︎ 設定：9:16 直度、1080p、開聲音；換衫片 10 秒，開箱片 15 秒

◼︎ 素材：一張 @binancezh 衣服相片、一張人物三視圖

⭐️ 第一步：準備兩張參考圖

衣服相片要正面、清楚、印花完整，因為模型只會照你給它看的去畫

人物用三視圖，一定要有正面全身、背面全身、臉部特寫

再把它們拼成一張圖，因為你要讓是模型同時知道這個人的臉、身形和背面，換了幾套衫之後，人還是同一個人

兩張圖都上傳成「參考圖」，不要設成首幀（片的第一個畫面），否則片會直接由那張三視圖開始，那就問題大了

⭐️ 第二步：先選一個已經爆過的格式

我沒有自己發明拍法，就是直接站在門口連換幾套、開箱視覺那些 ，全部是 IG 和 TikTok 上常見的穿搭片格式

指令第一句就寫明要模仿哪一種，例如「replicating a doorway outfit-changes format」，模型會知道鏡頭該放哪裡、節奏怎樣走

⭐️ 第三步：指令按這個次序寫

場景：房間長什麼樣，連地磚、植物、枱燈都寫
人物：對應哪張參考圖，外貌重點再描述一次
衣服：逐樣描述印花，再寫明不准加其他 logo
第一個畫面：片一開始他在做什麼

剪接：直接寫秒數
例如「CUT 1 at 3 seconds, CUT 2 at 6 seconds」

每一段的造型、動作和對白
鏡頭、物理、燈光、聲音
最後一段鎖定清單，把最怕出錯的東西再講一次

為什麼要寫這麼長？因為你沒寫的東西，模型會自己補些，而且 AI 補的通常不是你想要的😂😂

⭐️ 第四步：三個最容易出事的地方

第一是衣服上的字，幣安 BINANCE 這種多行重複、上下兩行被橫切的印花，模型很容易拼錯，或者自作主張換成普通的幣安標誌

我的做法是把印花結構逐句寫出來：有幾行、哪一行清楚、哪幾行被切，再加一句不准換成菱形 logo

第二是人會走位。換衫片要寫「鏡頭固定」和「他不會離開門口」，否則每次換衫他站的位置都不同，看起來就會不像同一支影片了

第三是物理。撕膠紙要有阻力、包裝紙會飄、手不可以穿過衣服，這些都要寫進指令，片才會有「人感」

⭐️ 第五步：出片後逐格檢查

字有沒有錯、臉有沒有變、手有沒有穿過衣服。有一樣不對，就回去改指令裡對應那一段再出，不要指望剪片時補救

我自己的感覺是，寫指令其實就是寫分鏡表。你本來懂得怎樣拍片，就已經懂一半 ✍️

門口換衫那條的指令範本我放在留言！
換掉衣服和人物就可以直接用了～

quoted_text:
如果你是不露面的幣圈 KOL，交易所或是項目方請你穿他們的周邊拍一條片，你大概也是把頭像 P 上去，但問題是，這完全沒有「人感」

本貼文的四支幣安 @binancezh UGC 片，我沒有請模特、沒有寄樣衫，也沒有開過一次相機

我手上只有一張 BN 周邊衣服的相片，用文字寫指令，一日之內生成了一個網店和三條換衫片，人物、房間、連衣服的皺摺都是生成的

現在幣圈 KOL 圈子到底有哪些情況？

◼︎ 幣圈 KOL 接推廣最卡的 2 樣東西：要露臉、要出很多版本，現在都可以用文字解決

◼︎ 你可以在交易所和項目方開口之前，先把整套素材做好，pitch 的次序會倒轉

◼︎ AI 拿走的是拍攝成本，但它拿不走品牌授權和信任，而幣圈最缺的正正是信任

那所以幣圈 KOL 接推廣，通常最大問題在哪裡？

第一當然是不露面，幣圈很多人用頭像經營，當然也離不開想低調一點，但也不排除有些人覺得自己的外貌不太好看

眾所週知觀眾跟的是你的觀點分析，不是你的樣子。但交易所的周邊、穿搭、開箱推廣，偏偏要有人穿上身，整個外觀穿搭得好看才有分享價值

第二點對我來說比較感覺深刻XD 就是等周邊送到家裡

有時候交易所今晚發通知，希望明天跟著上幣或者活動的熱度一起發文，衣服卻剛好卡在關口，手上沒有衣服又怎樣發文呢？

🌈 這就是本文值得被收藏的地方 —— UGC 大法！

⭐️ UGC 解決方法一：開箱速換

拆盒、包裝紙一撒，下一秒 BN 衣服已經套上身，交易所寄禮盒、KOL 拍開箱，本來就是幣圈常見的推廣片，現在你不用等盒寄到，也不用自己出鏡

⭐️ UGC 解決方法二：門口換衫

想不到怎樣拍片才好？直接用同一件衣服，你自己站在門口連換四套，灰褲、黑色闊褲、牛仔褲加帽、短褲加布袋，隨你喜歡

女生配搭呢？也行！

Moving Atoms (YC S26) introduces Scan to 3D Model.

One click turns any LiDAR or SLAM scan into a segmented, fully editable BIM model, ready to export to Revit, IFC, STEP, USD or Isaac Sim.

How it works:

1. Upload your scan. It opens instantly in our 3D viewer, which handles sites up to 5,000,000 sq ft.

2. The engine builds the model. It splits the scan into individual objects, measures each one and generates a native BIM element for every object.

3. Every point is checked. A heatmap shows where the model differs from the scan, and the engine refines each discrepancy until the model matches to within 5 mm.

text:
magpie 10-26 网关故障：尸检报告和道歉

10 月 25 日到 26 日下午，很多朋友更新 magpie 后遇到网关「挂了」：Codex 等 agent 的请求一直转圈，2 分钟后报 504（held this request for 2m0s without routing it），设置里关掉本地模型的开关也没反应。这是我的问题。耽误了大家的工作，尤其是半夜还在帮我抓栈、找原因的朋友，真的对不起。

【影响】
- 时间：10-25 起明显加重，到 10-26 14:15 的 v0.1.1566 修复。
- 范围：打开了「设置 › 隐私 › 用本地模型查找」的用户。重启 magpie 后几乎必犯，而且时好时坏。

【根因（已由用户抓到的 goroutine 栈确认，#3682）】
本地脱敏模型（pf-serve）的调用拿着一把全局锁做同步 I/O：模型加载（最长 3 分钟）和每一次识别都在这把锁里。于是所有请求都排在它后面，连「选哪个账号」这一步都走不到；设置页读模型状态、关闭模型也要这把锁，所以开关也点不动。

【为什么 10-25 起突然变严重】
- v0.1.1539 换了新版 pf-serve（pf-v2）。老用户更新后，magpie 会在后台下载新版、结束旧进程，下一个请求就要在锁里冷启动一次。我推断这一步把问题放大了，但没有单独复现过。
- v0.1.1540 加了「路由前卡住 2 分钟就回 504」的看门狗，原来静默的等待变成了直接报错。
- 识别超时后会结束并重启 pf-serve，每次重启又是一轮持锁加载，所以故障反复出现。
- 报告者的日志里，10-16 到 10-24 路由前等超过 5 分钟的请求是 0 条，10-25 有 26 条。

【我哪里做错了】
1. 把可能要几分钟的 I/O 放在全局锁里，测试和评审都没拦住。测试用的是假 pf-serve，从没用真模型跑过「冷重启 + 多个请求同时进来」。
2. 一天发了二十多个版本。换 pf-serve 这种「更新后第一个请求必然冷启动」的改动，没在真机上把更新流程走一遍就发了。
3. 10-26 凌晨 5 点就有朋友报告，我第一反应是「没复现，请先抓栈」。可抓栈的接口本身也会被卡住的请求挡住，直到 v0.1.1559 才修好。13:08 GitHub 上的 yunwang2442-creator 在 #3682 贴出完整的栈和根因，我才在一小时后修好。非常感谢。
4. 还没解释清楚的：有朋友报告 /v1/models 和供应商页面也没响应，这两条路径不经过脱敏模型，这次的修复不一定覆盖。turingou 的情况我也还没拿到栈，不能确定是同一个原因。在拿到证据之前，我不会说它已经修好。

【修复（v0.1.1566）】
- 加载和识别都不再持锁；读状态、关闭模型不用再排队。
- 识别结果落到磁盘（只存哈希、位置和类别，不存原文），重启后不用把历史重新跑一遍。
- 客户端已经断开、或已经回了 504 的请求会离开队列。
- 卡在模型上的请求会直接说「在等本地脱敏模型」，并告诉你怎么关掉它。
- 仍然不会只按规则脱敏就把请求发出去。

【请大家】
升级到 v0.1.1566 或更新的版本。如果网关还卡，请在终端运行 magpie goroutines，把生成的文件发给我，我会接着查。

【以后】
动到锁、子进程启动、升级流程的改动，发版前必须用真模型在沙箱里做一次冷重启 + 多请求的验证。

再次向大家道歉。

text:
This is the phase of the compute credit cycle we wrote about last week (and why it can be a good thing for the AI buildout).

Wall St has been financing neoclouds off the offtake contract rather than whether the neocloud can actually deliver it. Now with the high yield market closed to CRWV for unsecured issuance (and the ripple effects this has across the GPU financing ecosystem), build-to-order deals aren't getting financed left and right. The compute doesn't just magically disappear though. Contracts will get re-cut, hours will get re-let, and the lenders who can mark and remarket their collateral over time will be rewarded. Those who can't will be holding the "stranded compute".

这一套的测试版已经做好了，有兴趣的小伙伴可以测试一下，简单说说功能：

1. 输入想要投入的资金，这部分的资金需要已经在 @binance 中才可以，如果到期结算成功，扣除损失以后会直接买入 bitcoin:native 现货，做到抄底的功能。

2. 输入准备 SELL PUT 的价格，可以理解为你希望抄底 Bitcoin 的价格，如果结算的时候达到这个价格一下，那么你会获得 Bitcoin 现货，如果高于这个价格，你会获得权利金，也就是利息。

3. 选择一个到期时间，到期时间达到之前是不能结束和取消的，成交后这笔资金会自动进入到 Binance 的期权中，这个工具不经手，全程都是你自己的 API ，建议用子账户尝试。

4. 到期结算，举例用 80,000 美元 在 78,000 美元的位置准备抄底 BTC ，时间是 3 天，那么 3 天以后的北京时间 16 点，如果 Bitcoin 的价格低于 78,000 美元，那么你会按照 78,000 美元买入 BTC 的现货（扣除损失），如果高于 78,000 美元就会获得权利金也就是利息。

5. 我做了一个对，SELL PUT 和 Binance 双币理财的收益差异，如果差异较少的时候，可以直接用双币，更方便。

总的来说，这就是一套自动化的 SELL PUT Bitcoin 转抄底现货的功能，全部都是在 Binance 完成，都是通过自己的 API 。

Most people "learn" from a PDF by highlighting it and forgetting it a week later.

DeepTutor takes the opposite approach. You give it the material, a book, your notes or a YouTube lecture, and it teaches it back to you:

It quizzes you on what you just read.
It walks you through problems step by step instead of handing you the answer.
For a YouTube lecture, you can ask a question and it answers from that exact timestamp.
It builds a learning plan and tracks what you've actually learned, so you know where you're weak.

It's an open-source project from the University of Hong Kong with 42.9K stars, and it runs locally with your own model.

Easiest setup: paste the GitHub link into Claude Code or Codex and say "install and set up DeepTutor for me." The repo includes a setup guide written for agents.

text:
Last week, core devs had to delay forking the Hoodi testnet to Glamsterdam to study a report by @chain_security which revealed some problems with how EIP-8037 interacts with a few contracts.
Over the weekend, ppl tried to get a better picture of the impact and by now it's quite well understood. So here's what you need to know:

What's been known is that contracts which hardcode forwarded gas are affected by repricings, e.g. making state writes (SSTORE) more expensive.

What's new is that some coding patterns rely on specific invariant which were broken with EIP-8037. 

Gas already spent can come back mid-tx, so gasleft() can go up. This causes two problems:
(1) a before / after gas counter underflows and reverts
(2) a failed sub-call hands gas back, so a path that should've been unreachable runs, and the tx looks like it succeeded

Related but different: (3) measuring the gas usage of a call using GAS - before and after the call - might undercount because the state gas reservoir is not visible during execution (e.g. gas_left).

It's now about deciding how to proceed. Delaying hoodi bought time but won't resolve the issue. This week, we have to dig deep into contracts and make sure nothing is missed. Eventually, this might just need some coordination among the involved parties (dapps, core devs, auditors, people running nodes, etc.), or worst-case, spec changes.

If you're an app dev or auditor, check your contracts for issues with EIP-8037/EIP-8038, and report them.
Also, share this with your favorite app dev to spread awareness.
