Gm Folks
We are back!

This is another edition of the Predict Alpha Report, our bi-monthly collaboration with @CoinsiliumGroup tracking the rise of prediction markets, event-driven finance, and the growing role of AI agents within it. Each edition focuses on the signals that matter, from capital flows and fundraising activity to regulatory shifts and product innovation. As information is increasingly priced in real time by both humans and machines, the Predict Alpha Report will track where these signals lead.
But first, let’s get this part out of the way:

Always DYOR:
This bulletin is for informational purposes only and contains summaries of news articles originally published by third-party media outlets. Please refer to the full disclaimer at the end of the post.

Now, let’s get started.
Here are the highlights:

💸 Capital Signals
👉$1.4 Billion Linked To Election Day
👉Inflation Futures
👉Predictive Labs’ Nijinn Brings Cross-Market Intelligence to the US Midterms

📈 Industry Pulse
👉Swaps Include Prediction Markets
👉The First To..
👉Prediction Markets 🤝 Stablecoins
👉Kalshi on Phantom
👉Bitcoin-Backed Trades

💸 Capital Signals

💰$1.4 Billion Linked To Election Day

According to CNN, trading on prediction markets linked to the 2026 US midterm elections has surpassed $1.4 billion. @Kalshi leads with nearly $1.1 billion in trading volume, while @Polymarket has recorded more than $340 million across its US and international platforms. People are betting on everything from election winners and voter turnout to candidate endorsements, debates, and campaign speeches.

The growth comes as US regulations become more favourable toward election betting, encouraging existing platforms to expand and new players to enter the market. PredictIt and ForecastEx are seeing increased activity, while UK-based @Smarkets is seeking approval to launch in the US. Beyond betting, these markets are increasingly observed as indicators of public expectations and how traders assess the likelihood of different outcomes. Trading is expected to pick up even more, as Election Day approaches.

💰 Inflation Futures

Kalshi plans to launch futures contracts tied to US inflation in December. The new products will track the Consumer Price Index (CPI), a key measure of inflation, and core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices. Kalshi has brought in former Barclays trader Michael Ashton to help design the contracts and attract major banks, hedge funds and asset managers. The opportunity is significant, with the US inflation market including $2.2 trillion in Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) and more than $5.4 trillion in inflation swaps. Unlike Kalshi’s existing contracts that pay out based on whether an event happens, these futures would allow investors to trade changes in inflation expectations more directly and manage their exposure over time.

Kalshi hopes that offering standardised inflation contracts with fixed expiration dates and nearly round-the-clock trading will make the market more accessible, particularly for investors who currently rely on complex private agreements to trade inflation. While Kalshi has already built a large business around sports and event-based trading, attracting institutional investors would open up a very different source of growth.

And rounding up this section:

💰Predictive Labs’ Nijinn Brings Cross-Market Intelligence to the US Midterms

With the US midterm elections approaching, @nijinn_official's dedicated midterms platform brings prediction-market data into focus across Senate, House, and governor races. Developed by @Predictive_Labs, it combines Polymarket and Kalshi order-book data through Nijinn’s TruthIndex™ to produce a single liquidity-weighted probability for each outcome, while highlighting where the two venues’ probabilities diverge.

The platform offers an early preview of Nijinn Pro’s cross-venue analytics, with shareable graphics and live embeds helping journalists bring the data to their readers. Predictive Labs reports that it has shared the site with close to 1,000 US journalists and plans to extend the format to other major elections and sporting events, broadening Nijinn’s reach through timely, relevant applications.
Predictive Labs will exhibit at Web Summit Lisbon on 9–12 November 2026, with founder @johann_evrard showcasing Nijinn alongside leading figures in AI and blockchain.

📌 FYI: Predictive Labs is backed by Gibraltar-based venture builder, Coinsilium Group. Coinsilium’s shares are traded on the Aquis Stock Exchange Growth Market in London, under the ticker symbol "COIN", and on the OTCQB Venture Market in the United States under the ticker symbol "CINGF".

But it’s not just capital flowing into the space.
Keep reading for the latest signals in regulation, adoption, and structure.

📈 Industry Pulse

⚡️Swaps Include Prediction Markets

The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has proposed new rules that would formally classify prediction market contracts tied to sports, politics, culture, and weather as swaps, a type of financial contract whose value depends on an underlying asset or event. The proposal aims to clarify that prediction markets operating on federally registered exchanges fall under the CFTC’s authority rather than individual state gambling regulators.

The distinction matters for platforms like Kalshi, which have faced legal challenges as they expand across the US. If adopted, the proposal could give federally regulated prediction markets greater legal certainty and make it harder for states to restrict their operations.

⚡️ The First To...

The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has approved Cboe Global Markets’ proposal to introduce contracts that let investors trade on specific company performance metrics rather than just share prices. @RobinhoodApp is expected to become the first retail brokerage to offer these products, covering more than 100 metrics across 23 companies. These include NVIDIA’s data-center revenue, Apple’s iPhone sales revenue, and Robinhood’s number of funded customers.

The contracts work as binary options, allowing traders to take positions on whether a company will meet a particular performance target. For Robinhood, this adds another product to its growing range of options, futures, and prediction markets, potentially creating a new source of trading revenue.

⚡️Prediction Markets 🤝 Stablecoins

@Underdog has partnered with crypto infrastructure provider @zerohashx to let users fund their prediction market and fantasy sports accounts using stablecoins and other digital assets. Announced at the NEXTPredict NYC Summit, the new feature is expected to launch later in 2026 for eligible users and will sit alongside existing payment options within the Underdog app.

The main benefit is speed. Unlike traditional bank transfers, which can face delays during evenings and weekends, stablecoin payments can be processed around the clock, allowing users to add funds to their accounts in near real time. Zerohash will handle the underlying crypto infrastructure, so users won’t need to manage complicated wallet addresses or blockchain networks themselves.

⚡️Kalshi on Phantom

Crypto wallet provider @Phantom is bringing Kalshi’s prediction markets directly into its app, allowing millions of US crypto users to trade on real-world events without leaving their wallets. The rollout began on October 23, and access will expand over the coming weeks. Users will need to complete identity verification through Kalshi and can fund trades using Phantom’s dollar-pegged CASH stablecoin.

Funds are converted into traditional currency for settlement, while winnings and withdrawals return to users’ Phantom Cash accounts. Trading fees are set at $0.02 per contract, plus a small network fee. The integration gives Kalshi access to Phantom’s existing crypto user base while making regulated prediction markets more accessible to people already familiar with digital assets.

At the same time,

⚡️Bitcoin-Backed Trades

@Kalshi is expanding its crypto offerings through a new partnership with digital asset custodian @BitGo, allowing eligible institutional clients to borrow against their cryptocurrency holdings to fund leveraged futures trades. Through Kalshi Prime, customers will be able to use Bitcoin, Ethereum, and selected stablecoins held at BitGo as collateral for loans, rather than selling their crypto to raise cash.

The borrowed funds can then be used to support margin positions on Kalshi’s trading platform, allowing investors to take larger positions with less upfront cash, although this also increases their exposure to potential losses. Kalshi plans to add more crypto custodians to the network in the coming months, giving clients greater flexibility in how they fund their trades. The partnership marks another step in Kalshi’s efforts to move beyond event-based prediction markets and compete in the broader derivatives trading industry.

And that’s it!

2月24日，据国内媒体报道，一名DIY爱好者用PS5游戏手柄控制自家大疆（DJI）Romo扫地机器人时，意外触发严重安全漏洞，导致全球约6700台该型号机器人遭未授权访问，可被查看实时摄像头画面、获取家庭2D楼层平面图，甚至定位设备位置。
发现该漏洞的是萨米·阿兹杜法尔（Sammy Azdoufal）。他向媒体表示，自己初衷只是觉得用PS5手柄控制新入手的大疆Romo很有趣，便用Claude Code软件逆向工程了机器人与大疆服务器的通信协议，自制了一款远程控制应用。

令人意外的是，这款应用连接服务器后出现权限失控，他仅提取了自家设备的私有令牌，便获得了全球约7000台Romo的响应。

The Verge记者现场见证了漏洞演示。9分钟内，阿兹杜法尔的电脑就记录了24个国家的6700台大疆设备，收集到10万余条设备消息，涵盖设备序列号、清洁房间、所见场景、行驶距离、充电时间及遇到的障碍物等。

仅凭同事托马斯·里克（Thomas Ricker）提供的14位设备序列号，便能精准查看机器人正在清洁客厅、剩余80%电量的状态，还能获取同事家的精准楼层平面图。

此外，他还能绕过自身机器人的安全PIN码查看实时画面，甚至将一款只读版应用分享给法国一名IT咨询公司CTO贡扎格·丹布里库尔（Gonzague Dambricourt），对方在未配对设备的情况下，也能远程查看自家Romo的摄像头画面。

阿兹杜法尔强调，自己并未入侵大疆服务器，"我没有违反任何规则，没有破解、暴力破解任何系统"，只是他提取的自家设备私有令牌，本应用于验证自身设备访问权限的密钥，被大疆服务器误判为通用权限，进而泄露了全球数千台设备的数据。

大疆方面回应：大疆（DJI）于1月下旬通过内部审查发现了一个影响大疆 DJI Home 的漏洞，并立即启动修复工作。该问题通过两次更新得到解决，首次补丁于2月8日部署，后续更新于2月10日完成。修复程序已自动部署，无需用户进行任何操作。

text:
Bloom Energy 财报后的一些投资思考

robinhood:0x822cc93ffd030293e9842c30bbd678f530701867  上周四发布财报后，股价反而下跌了11%，但实际业绩相当不错。

Q3营收12.36亿美元，同比增长138%，调整后EBITDA达到2.99亿美元，同比增长407%，EPS为0.94美元，超出市场预期38%。公司今年第三次上调全年指引，预计2026年营收达到44–46亿美元。收入高速增长的同时，盈利能力也在持续改善。

市场下跌主要担心两个问题：现金流和交付能力。

首先是现金流。Q3经营现金流为负2700万美元，自由现金流为负1.81亿美元，主要受到合同资产增加约4.3亿美元及扩产开支的影响。合同资产主要是已经确认收入、但尚未达到开票条件的款项。

我个人认为市场对现金流的担忧有些过度。
BE的大客户体系包括Oracle、Brookfield支持的项目等，整体资金实力较强，历史上也没有出现明显的大规模坏账。我更倾向于认为这是项目交付和结算周期导致的短期资金占用，未来随着项目推进，现金流有望改善。

第二个问题是产能兑现，这才是我认为真正需要持续关注的点。

BE计划在2026年底达到2GW年产能，并进一步向5GW以上扩张。摩根士丹利预计2027、2028年项目验收规模分别达到2.3GW和3.7GW。

BE的产能瓶颈是在数据中心客户的审批进度、建设进度

总体来看，我仍然长期看好BE的基本面和投资价值。AI数据中心的电力瓶颈短期难以解决，BE的现场供电方案具备明确的商业价值，而且规模效应正在兑现。

唯一的问题是估值仍然稍贵。目前193美元左右的价格，对应Bernstein预测的2027年约38倍PE，市场已经计入较高的增长预期。

如果股价能回到145美元附近，按照2027年约4.8美元的保守EPS假设，对应30倍PE，我认为就很有性价比了。届时如果产能和现金流也能逐步兑现，会是一个值得重点考虑的投资机会。

text:
一个韩国老哥，2 万 USDC 打进 BSC，基本确定要不回来了。很多人第一反应是“同一个地址，换条链提出来不就行？”这次还真不行，我研究了一下

普通的 EVM 钱包（小狐狸、OKX、币安钱包）是私钥直接算出地址。同一个私钥，在 ETH、BSC、Base 上地址完全一样，转错链了用同一个私钥在另一条链上就能取出来。

Abstract 的官方钱包 AGW 不一样，它是智能合约钱包（账户抽象）。你看到的地址是一个部署在 Abstract 上的合约，不是私钥直接对应的账户。按他自己的描述，本来要复制 EVM 地址，结果没复制上，粘贴的还是 Abstract 地址，钱就打到了 BSC 上的这个地址。BSC 上这个地址没有部署过对应的合约，也没有任何人的私钥能控制它。Abstract 官方的回复是：除非暴力破解私钥，否则救不回来。他现在挂了 1.5 万 U 的悬赏，评论区还有人说自己也有钱卡在别的链的 Abstract 地址上。

所以结论很简单：智能合约钱包、AA 钱包的地址，只认它自己那条链。以后用 AGW、Safe 这类钱包，跨链前先查清楚目标链上有没有你的合约账户。大额转账一定先打 1U 测试，到账再转剩下的。

链越来越多，这种坑只会更多。钱包产品早晚要做“地址属于哪条链”的强提醒，在那之前，只能自己多看一眼。

First, I thought it'd help to explain what a consensus trade actually is.

Essentially, it's a bet most of the market agrees on.

With @HyperliquidX, the thinking is: great product = obvious winner

The catch is that a lot of that optimism may already be priced in.

Think of backing the favourite to win a match. It might win, but the odds are less rewarding because everyone else expects it too.

IMO, Hyperliquid is a great product. Whether $HYPE is a good trade still depends on what price you're paying and how much growth is already expected.

Arthur Hayes claims $HYPE is the most dangerous consensus trade in crypto right now.

"I think your consensus trade is not that you lose money per se on Hyperliquid. It's that you severely underperform other assets because you're investing in the thing that everybody knew was going to be successful. I don't think that the risk-return is there for a new unit of fiat to invest in Hyperliquid when you could do ETH, Zcash, or some other narrative in crypto."

"Now, Hyperliquid, good on them. Jeff crushed it. They proved the market's there. They got the trading volume. Now they're competing with centralized exchanges, they're competing with TradFi exchanges, and they're competing with other DEXes. They all offer the same product. "It's hard to sell a perfectly competitive product. That's really, really hard as a business. Great on them for doing it. I'll benefit as a consumer, but I don't want to be an investor."

text:
巴基斯坦沙特土耳其三国军方、国防和情报最高层共赴德黑兰，是近期中东值得重视的新动向。聊聊几点：
1、这次访问最早是巴基斯坦陆军参谋长穆尼尔（巴基斯坦实际权力掌控者）上周访问德黑兰时提出举行这次四方磋商，伊方同意。
三国高层拟会见的伊方负责人：总统佩泽希齐扬、最高国家安全委员会秘书穆赫辛·雷扎伊（雷扎伊之前是穆杰塔巴的顾问、相当于穆杰塔巴在最高国安委员会的代言人）；

2、这次访问的分量，在于两点：
1）三国开始以共同防务框架下的集体身份同伊朗接触；
2）直接承受胡塞袭击压力的沙特，也进入了这场高级别安全对话。

3、沙特负责公共外交的副大臣Rayed Krimly对这次访问的解释，是缓和当前危机、推动对话和外交解决、支持卡塔尔与巴基斯坦的斡旋，并与地区各国合作维护稳定。

看伊朗公布的议题是地区安全、巴勒斯坦和黎巴嫩局势，以及美国、以色列对伊军事行动的地区影响

所以这场会谈可能同时包含劝和美伊，要求伊朗约束胡塞、提出安全保证，以及划定沙特不能接受的行为边界。 从沙特角度，找伊朗谈，也是其处理胡塞威胁来源的一部分

4、个人角度联合访伊可以视作“有限妥协机会增加”的可能性，三国作为中东大国还是有一定的话语权的。说不定也能很好的了解伊朗的底线到底在哪里，其实最重要的是聊清楚哪些是伊朗能让的、哪些是美国能让的。

当然现在还是揣测，短期还不能说就立马有积极的结果出来、但沟通越频繁也就越有助于局面的缓解。

就看后面访问结束有没有官方的声明出来

5、这次访问的意义在于说明除了美伊之间的间接传话，地区主要国家也在尝试共同介入安全问题。地区国家正在争取更大的安全决策权，希望对美伊冲突及其外溢产生实际约束。这可能逐步削弱美国的主导程度，

8月份有聊到今年这一场伊朗战争，对中东的地缘格局影响是极其巨大的，中东各国都在为美国在中东的影响力被削弱做准备。

text:
线下见了很多老师，发现不少币圈 KOL 居然都在定投黄金。具体为什么？我也说不清楚，但感觉他们对黄金的信仰，可能是 BTC 的十倍。现在黄金和美股也进入了我的长期定投名单。不过黄金有个问题，它本身不会生息，所以我一直觉得，黄金结合加密，其实能玩出不少新花样。

比如最近关注的 @strato_net。STRATO 是一条专注于 RWA 金融的 L1 公链，主要围绕黄金、白银等现实资产，开发抵押、借贷、交易等链上应用，项目把这个方向称为 HardFi。

HardFi最大的特点是黄金不用卖，也能释放流动性。STRATO 的 GOLDST、SILVST 分别对应金库里 1 金衡盎司实物黄金、白银，官方文档写明支持实物赎回。

用户可以抵押这些资产，铸造美元稳定币 USDST，再拿去参与链上 DeFi，比如储蓄、兑换、提供流动性。官方材料还介绍了通过 MetaMask Card 消费的路径。

除此之外，加密资产、生息稳定币，甚至代币化股票也可以作为 CDP 抵押品。当然，抵押借款仍然存在清算风险。
团队背景也挺好的。

STRATO 由 BlockApps 团队开发，累计融资超过 4100 万美元，投资机构包括 Fenbushi Capital、ConsenSys Mesh、Galaxy Ventures 等。

创始人 Kieren 早在 2014 年就参与以太坊早期开发，做了最初的 Haskell 客户端，CTO Jim 也是早期以太坊 Haskell 客户端的开发者，该客户端也是 2015 年以太坊 Frontier 上线时的六个主网兼容客户端之一。

最后说说我的看法。黄金代币化已经不是什么新故事了，但如何让这些资产在不卖出的情况下创造更多金融使用场景，我觉得值得长期关注。@strato_net

感兴趣的老师可以看看产品：https://t.co/ecUyM2T4JE

text:
Last week, core devs had to delay forking the Hoodi testnet to Glamsterdam to study a report by @chain_security which revealed some problems with how EIP-8037 interacts with a few contracts.
Over the weekend, ppl tried to get a better picture of the impact and by now it's quite well understood. So here's what you need to know:

What's been known is that contracts which hardcode forwarded gas are affected by repricings, e.g. making state writes (SSTORE) more expensive.

What's new is that some coding patterns rely on specific invariant which were broken with EIP-8037. 

Gas already spent can come back mid-tx, so gasleft() can go up. This causes two problems:
(1) a before / after gas counter underflows and reverts
(2) a failed sub-call hands gas back, so a path that should've been unreachable runs, and the tx looks like it succeeded

Related but different: (3) measuring the gas usage of a call using GAS - before and after the call - might undercount because the state gas reservoir is not visible during execution (e.g. gas_left).

It's now about deciding how to proceed. Delaying hoodi bought time but won't resolve the issue. This week, we have to dig deep into contracts and make sure nothing is missed. Eventually, this might just need some coordination among the involved parties (dapps, core devs, auditors, people running nodes, etc.), or worst-case, spec changes.

If you're an app dev or auditor, check your contracts for issues with EIP-8037/EIP-8038, and report them.
Also, share this with your favorite app dev to spread awareness.

- AI is moving from chat interfaces to agents that execute work  
- Enterprise adoption is shifting from experimentation to workflow automation  
- The bottleneck is no longer model capability, it’s integration and change management  
- Legacy systems make agent deployment hard, and that creates opportunity for software incumbents  
- Compute and token budgets may become a new enterprise resource constraint  
- The highest value use cases are moving from cost cutting to revenue generation  
- Demand should rise for interoperable, agent agnostic software layers  
- The future likely looks multi agent, not single platform  
- Ironically, AI is increasing operational complexity before it reduces it  
- Engineers increasingly move from coding software to operating agent systems

The market may be shifting from asking: Who enables AI training?

To asking: Who monetizes AI deployment?

text:
Where to allocate sAERO: three checks before the next 47 hours.

An attractive payout in an Aero pool is a starting point. The next question is where it comes from, and how much your own position could receive.

On Aero, revenue comes from the pools your Allocation Power supports. Your share depends on your weight relative to everyone else allocated there.

My Aero Vote Radar helps compare the options.

1. Check who is paying.

In Radar’s October 26 snapshot, USDG/WBTC on Arbitrum showed $1.03 in Fees/day and $368.50 in Incentives/day. Those are pool figures, not an individual holder’s earnings.

Fees are calculated from past activity; incentives reflect the current stream. In this example, incentives drive most of the estimated payout.

Before allocating, check how long the program has left. The current rate does not show what remains after it ends.

2. Enter your own amount.

Adding allocation weight changes everyone’s share, including yours. Someone else’s income estimate cannot simply be scaled up to fit your position.

In the same snapshot, Radar suggested:

For 10,000 sAERO:
75% USDG/WBTC and 25% USDG/ARB.

For 100,000:
45% USDG/WETH, 35% USDG/WBTC and 20% USDG/ARB.

All three pools are on Arbitrum. A different amount produced a different suggested split.

This is the model’s calculation using current data. It does not prove those pools will outperform.

3. Account for the wait before your next change.

An allocation starts a 47-hour cooldown for that particular stake. Revenue keeps accruing while pool conditions can change.

The practical workflow: enter your amount in Radar, examine fees and incentives, and compare the percentages. After checking the chosen pools, open Allocate on Aero and set the split there.

You can run the calculation without connecting a wallet to Radar. Signing happens in Aero itself.

An estimated daily payout helps compare options. Results need to be measured through actual revenue earned over time.

https://t.co/A8HdhWeGbD

When choosing a pool, what matters more to you: the current payout estimate, or its dependence on incentives?

At @blockworksDAS Asia 2026, @keoneHD from Monad asked the right question: where does DeFi fit into Canton?

@HeslinKim, Zenith Co-Founder and CBO, came with a specific answer: Zenith is the middle ground. Not by moving assets between environments and calling it composability, but by bringing Ethereum-compatible execution natively into @CantonNetwork's transaction model, so Solidity applications and Canton-native assets settle atomically in the same transaction.

Most of what the industry calls cross-chain composability is either bridging or messaging, two operations that settle independently, on different schedules, under different finality rules. The gap between them is where the risk lives. Atomic composability means there is no gap. Either every leg of the transaction commits together or the entire operation aborts.

That distinction is at the heart of a piece we published recently. If the DAS Asia conversation sparked the same questions for you, it’s worth the read.

if you think #BOYCOTTPUMPFUN is some bullshit 

Let’s revisit each time attention shifted away from PumpFun

Even ZC on Ethereum reached $50M before the team rugged on a random launchpad 

Meanwhile Kimchi one of PumpFun’s biggest promotional pushes, couldn’t even take his own coin to $50M despite his massive reach and backing and “aura” 

At some point you have to question the ecosystem you’re participating in

PumpFun has built a model that thrives on:

• Constant new launches that pnd
• Influencers incentivized to promote PF tokens
• Liquidity continuously rotating between new pairs
• Trading volume regardless of whether anyone actually makes money

Think about the incentives

PumpFun profits from trading activity, not from your bags appreciating

A token going to $100M and establishing a strong holder base isn’t nearly as important to their business model as thousands of traders constantly rotating between new launches spamming volume 

And the people promoting these launches have financial incentives that aren’t necessarily aligned with yours

Yet traders keep following the same accounts into the same launches, expecting different results .. like please wake up

Some of the best opportunities we’ve had came when liquidity and attention escaped this absolute hell of an ecosystem

Holy Shit. A malicious website can plant a simple markdown file in your Downloads folder. An AI coding agent launched there can follow the attacker's instructions without you ever opening the file.

Forever Security caught a real attack on a customer's computer: an AI coding agent followed instructions in a malicious AGENTS.md file in its Downloads folder and tried to install a malicious npm package.

The researchers then reproduced the attack against OpenAI Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code:

-Codex succeeded in over 90% of tests, bypassing its sandbox and rewriting machine-wide configuration so malicious commands could persist across future projects.

-Claude Code was compromised in roughly 50% of tests, redirecting API traffic to an attacker-controlled server, exposing OAuth tokens and allowing attackers to impersonate the model and send executable commands.

The researchers say: "There is nothing here for OpenAI or Anthropic to patch."

The agent is doing exactly what it was designed to do.

text:
抗量子赛道项目介绍：Midstate  @phraudsta

一条只用哈希函数的抗量子 PoW 链它把椭圆曲线整个删掉了，只信哈希函数。

🔹技术概述
（1）Midstate 全部只用 BLAKE3 一种哈希函数。签名是 WOTS+ 一次性签名加 MSS 默克尔树，一个地址大约能用 1024 次，完全不用椭圆曲线。

（2）PoW 是顺序 BLAKE3，每个 nonce 要串行算 100 万次哈希。

（3）UTXO 只有 2 的幂次面额，原生支持 CoinJoin 和 Dandelion++，内存池用先承诺后揭示的方式防 MEV。

（4）代码用 Rust 编写，以 GPL-3.0 开源。

🔹现状
（1）2026-02-24 主网上线，创世区块锚定比特币第 938,708 号区块，没有预挖，也没有开发者份额。

（2）每 60 秒出一块，每块 1 gMDS，大约每年减半一次，首次减半在 2027 年 2 月。

（3）目前流通约 35 万 gMDS，上限约 105 万。 $MDS 价格约 1.1U，市值约 $39 万，FDV 约 $116 万。

（4）BLAKE3 不需要大量内存，币价涨上去以后可能会出现专用矿机（ASIC）。

🔹参与方式
（1）挖矿：GPU 最快，NVIDIA RTX 20 系及以上可以用 NTMminer（矿池费 2%）。CPU 和树莓派 5 也能挖，树莓派 5 约 100 nonce/s。全网约 170 万 nonce/s，每天产出约 1440 gMDS，约合 $1600。收款要用 MSS 地址，WOTS 一次性地址不能重复使用。

（2）二级购买：只在 SafeTrade 一家交易所交易

🔹风险
（1）只有一个开发者，代码没有审计。

（2）只在一家交易所交易，深度薄，单日波动很大。

（3）链上除了挖矿几乎没有交易。签名有 576 字节，用起来体验比较差。

相对于格密码或者XMSS，Midstate只押注哈希函数（和Blockstream的看法比较像），这是最保守的抗量子路线，当然代价就是体验和流动性。

text:
Since people seem to be enjoying my tweets about career transitions and lessons learned, here's the biggest hack:

Get a coach, folks. It's the best thing I've ever done for myself. 

My thinking process about this is: after spending four years learning engineering, I can look back and see a million things I could've done differently to focus on the right things and progress faster.

That's exactly where a coach or mentor comes in.
 
Having a coach doesn't necessarily mean they handhold you and literally teach you how to do the thing, but more about someone who can answer your important questions, point you in the right direction, and help you focus your efforts on things that will actually move you forward.

When you're new to an industry, it's easy to spend months working on things that seem important but ultimately don't get you anywhere.

A good example is my experience with content creation. I made over 200 short videos and spent time building my brand in areas that were either too saturated, would take too long to break into, or had no clear path to monetization.

With the right advice early on, I could've saved myself months of trial and error and focused on a much better opportunity from the beginning.

I've personally spent tens of thousands of dollars getting advice on things like this, and a lot of it has been incredibly valuable.

The moral of the story: When learning a new skill or making a career transition, a good coach or mentor can make a massive difference, purely to make sure you're shooting on goal and not in the stands like Lukaku or Darwin Nunes.
author: abbaskhan
quoted_text:
Last night, I found myself thinking about the early days of my career, old coworkers, and why some people grew into much better roles while others seemed to stay exactly where they were and even declined.

One pattern I noticed among the people who really grew was their ability to imagine themselves doing things they weren't qualified for yet, combined with the almost delusional confidence that they'd figure it out.

I think I fell into that category myself. When I wanted to transition from engineering into sales, I realized that building a great product was only half the battle. You also had to convince people to buy it.

So I jumped on a call with @adamxlee, who was leading corporate development and business at thirdweb at the time.

I asked all the questions I could think of. We were in different departments, so he didn't know me that well, but what he did know was that I was extremely committed.

Towards the end of the call, I asked him whether he thought I could actually do well in sales and other business roles.

I don't know if he genuinely believed it or was just being nice, but he told me:

"Well, you can hold a conversation, and you're very hardworking and that's what it's all about in business"

I looked up to Adam, so I took those words to heart. They gave me an almost ridiculous level of confidence that I could make the transition.

Of course, being delusional on its own isn't enough, and it can absolutely backfire. But at that point in my life, I was putting in 14-hour days easily while still in college. Don't ask me how I managed that.

While still in college and working my full time devrel  role, I started learning sales skills on the side and doing a lot of unpaid work for an agency to get some real experience.

Within 6 months of that conversation, I was brought in as an SDR to help with lead generation. Four months later, I'd already moved into an AE role at another company.

The point of this isn't to brag, but to highlight why always pushing through, looking for greater challenges, refusing to be a spectator, and having the delusional confidence that you can achieve something is a pretty darn good combination.

If you're stuck in a role and want to do something different, I'd encourage you to find that combination of ambition, hard work, AND most importantly delusional confidence. It will take you further than you think.

- 番茄负责剧本, 多年网文累积确定爆款
- 抖音负责超低成本获客 + 筛选爆款
= 低剧本成本+低制作成本 + 低获客成本

当然这个4亿月活和牛逼飞轮的背后，在我看来其实还是中国本身匮乏的娱乐内容（电影工业本身垃圾 hh，最近芒果台的后会友期感觉还很不错lol），加上大家不仅压力大，普遍做题长大的教育背后、大多数人其实没有很多日常娱乐方式。红果这种刷刷乐在中国天然有优势，尤其是网络小说生态（本子好）前提下。话说我当年也是重度起点小说的网瘾少年 - 阳神 / 无限恐怖 / 龙蛇演义什么的提供了当时初中/高中很多的精神食粮。

再往后推演：
- 可见的视频模型只会越来越好，再过一年大概率已经与真人一般无二。目前的反感会逐渐消弭
- 字节依靠红果国内的统治，因而获得巨大创作者的内容作为持续训练 + CapCut，有概率持续保持领先
-  文本产出和创意会因AI boil the ocean，对比过去量大管饱越来越好

所以高质量AI内容基本大概率在未来2-3年打爆国外流媒体中低端内容, 而字节国内的打法，在国外同样好用。超低成本价格拉暴竞争对手
- 所以下一步就是去干暴Youtube / Netflix / Disney / Warners 的中低端shows / 普通内容, 尤其是非英语平台机会巨大 (欧亚非拉)
- 全球电影票房35Bn，上述流媒体平台除去Youtube 大概90-100 Bn收入。红果海外一旦复制国内成功，基本就是35-40 Bn的体量。
- 然后假设Seedance持续保持市占，short-films creator高度调用，大概10-15Bn ARR。创作者多平台deploy
- 字节一鱼两吃之下大概收入45-50 Bn USD，差不多就是在再造一个今天的Anthropic / OpenAI 收入体量 (当然这两家年底估计就是这个的4倍了lol）

在这个赛道除非Top Labs自己转向或者achieve AGI，否则我感觉只有Youtube有一战之力。不过看着Google如此拉垮多条战线全面傻逼，估计还是字节's game to lose. 全球奶头乐number 1当之无愧。

In actuality, 我感觉好莱坞和美国所有想搞的公司会被版权这个事情给拖死，想搞也改不了。所以最后还是中国的机会。全球演员和剧组的状态会很难想象是怎么样的，不过大概率是被完爆，失业率爆表。看看中国演员现在状态就知道了。

最后是啥结论我也不知道、不过就是今天跟朋友打牌的时候想出来的。。。如果有的话，那就是：

我想看无限恐怖/杀戮都市！！！什么时候有大神能够完全忽略版权上线这种内容啊啊啊

回顾 grass 过去的价格行为，tge 时它的大幅上涨可以归因于空投反撸，筹码在项目方手里，所以拉盘出货。项目方本质上是一个非常小气，想让自己利益最大化的团队。之前虽然说自己项目很赚钱，但是没有独立第三方验证，市场也不太信，所以喊的人也不是很多。后面 s2 空投，给的是 usdc，削掉了 grass 的抛压，说明项目方是想要拉盘了，不过这个筹备时间也是比较久，估计是在等第三方机构出报告，证明他们的收入是真实的。现在报告出了，证明了收入可信，价格也就涨了，只不过市场反应其实比较慢（也有可能是 grass 之前就不干人事，市场还是不信），9.22发了报告，10月才涨了很多。现在到什么阶段了呢？就是如果 grass 不把其项目经济利益转移到 token 上，这项目的涨幅也就到头了。唯一值得做的，就是等 grass tokenomics 有眉目了，反应快点去吃下一阶段确定性的涨幅。其他没啥了。项目方的动作永远都是以拉盘出货的动机，不要以长期眼光去看这个项目。未来 tokenomics 肯定会有眉目的，看它蠢蠢欲动的价格就知道了，可能最近就会宣布这种东西。

cards，我个人对它感兴趣，但其筹码结构并不好，每个月都有解锁。虽然现在 cards 扩展了新叙事，做卡牌收藏品的基础设施和底层流动性，但是我觉得它现在的估值已经在贵的区间了，不适合去参与。如果有低位给机会，还是可以参与一下。如果做，主要还是以现货偏长期持有为主。

kntq 这个项目，我思考了很久：团队有执行力，也有sm、海外 kol 看好，elysium 是一个高性能扩容方案，是 hyperliquid core 现货和 hyperevm 的补充。还有一个值得一提的事儿是解锁，kntq 11月27日开始解锁，每月 vesting，单次解锁量并不大，allcation 会给到团队（23.5%）和投资者（7.5%）。目前 kntq 的回购力度还无法 cover 这样的解锁抛压。不过，我觉得它的解锁在影响价格的层面其实没那么关键。其价格主要还是看 elysium 上线后的表现。从长期的角度来看，如果 elysium 又是另外一条死链，那也没有参与的必要。而从项目方利益的角度来看，它可能会在解锁前维持当前价格或者将价格拉得更高。所以我觉得现在持有一些 kntq 的头寸没什么太大的问题。我个人比较担心的，一是大盘，二是 kntq 团队在运营公链方面没什么经验。不过他们 markets 这个产品其实做得挺好的。另外就是还要看看 jeff、hyperliquid 对 elysium 的态度和支持力度。之前35买入的仓位就谨慎一些，灵活一些。

text:
ZEC is a $20.2B asset rn. Canton, the privacy network built for institutions, is $4.0B.

The open networks building programmable privacy (Midnight, ZAMA, Aleo, Aztec, Arcium) are worth $940M combined. Under 5% of ZEC.

The market pays for private money, and for privacy institutions can sign off on. It hasn't priced private apps on open chains yet.

Miden's pitch sits right in that gap: an open chain, private by default, with compliance built into the assets.

Tomorrow it goes live on (partner) mainnet.

7 years of R&D, first at Meta and then at Polygon. Spun out of Polygon in April 2025 with $25M from a16z, 1kx and Hack VC. Still no token.

Definitely one of the bigger privacy launches this year.

Why?

Because it changes where your transaction runs.

On every chain you use today, you send a transaction and every node re-executes it to check it. That's why everything onchain is public. Nodes can't verify what they can't see.

Miden flips the order.

Your device executes the transaction and generates a STARK proof of it. The network only verifies the proof and stores a commitment.

Execution and state move to the user. The team calls it an "edge blockchain", and three key things come with that approach:

- Privacy: your balances and history stay on your device
- Scale: transactions run in parallel, nodes check proofs instead of re-running code
- State: a private account takes ~50 bytes onchain, so 1B accounts fit in ~47GB

What actually runs on your phone?

The Miden VM. A Turing-complete virtual machine built for proving: devs write contracts in Rust, they compile down to Miden Assembly, and every run comes out with a STARK proof attached.

Proving instead of re-executing changes the economics too:

- No gas limit. Fees grow with the log of the compute, so a transaction with 1,000x more compute costs ~$0.00007 more
- Weak devices can hand the proving off. Miden's remote prover on mainnet does it in ~0.6s, with a ~112KB proof

How does a transfer work?

Every account owns its code, storage and assets, and only it can change its own state.

Accounts talk through notes. A note is assets plus a small script that says who can claim it and when.

Alice pays Bob 100 USDCx: she creates a note in her own transaction, Bob claims it later in his. Two separate proofs. Bob doesn't need to be online, and the public chain only sees hashes.

And sure, DeFi needs shared state. An AMM can't live on your phone.

For that Miden has network accounts: public accounts the operator executes, which consume the notes users send them. That's how @port0_sh runs its permissionless AMM, while @luminaengine is building a dark pool orderbook.

So far that's payments and DeFi.

The harder question: how does an issuer enforce rules on balances it can't see?

Miden's answer is what puts it in that gap: the issuer's rules travel with the asset.

Every transfer runs them inside your proof, on your device. The code is public, the execution stays private, and the issuer doesn't even need to be online.

@schmiddominik1 from Miden tested it on mainnet on Thursday with USDCx and @0xPredicate: a transfer from a blocklisted account couldn't even finish its proof.

That's how institutions get private stablecoins that still enforce a blocklist.

Okay cool.

But what actually goes live tmrw?

- Partner mainnet: real funds, gated access for partners and early-access users of Bread (the self-custodial private wallet). Public mainnet after, no date yet
- USDCx: native USDC-backed stablecoin via Circle's xReserve, private by default, also pays the fees (~$0.0001 a tx)
- Guardian: backup and recovery, run by OpenZeppelin, Gateway, LambdaClass, Para and KODA
- Agglayer: Polygon calls Miden the first non-EVM chain connected to it

The chain is already producing blocks: 290k+ at ~3s, with all 3/3 validators healthy.

What's not there yet?

At launch you're private from other users, not from the operators.

Validators decrypt and re-execute every transaction as a safety net while the proof system matures. Guardian sees your account state, but can't move your funds.

There's also only one block producer on day one, run by Miden. Decentralization comes in phases.

Fair enough for a gated partner mainnet.

And the token?

There is none. Miden told the SEC's Crypto Task Force in June it chose not to launch one "at the current stage of network development".

The only hint on record is Polygon's line from April 2025: ~10% of native tokens to POL stakers. No ticker, supply or date since.

But if @sandeepnailwal's line holds up ("If ZEC is the private bitcoin, then Miden is the private Ethereum"), this could be pretty big.

Watching closely.

NFA ofc. DYOR.

text:
🧐索尼做公链，真正的野心可能不只是发一个 Token。

最近关注了一下 @soneium 的新方向，主要是因为前几天在朋友的安利下关注了项目进度，而且还买了他们 NFT Moriusa，刚看了已经开始涨了，赚到了。

除了赚点钱之外，这个项目有些值得研究的地方。

Soneium @soneium 可能很多人并不很了解，其实是默默 BUILD 很久了，之所以叫索尼链，是因为他是由 Sony Group（索尼集团）与 Startale Group 共同打造的以太坊 L2。

提到 Sony，很多人的第一反应还是电视、相机、耳机这些消费电子产品。
但从 PlayStation 到 Sony Music、Sony Pictures，它在游戏、音乐和影视领域也有深厚的积累。
这样的背景，让我更想关注一个问题：Sony 的娱乐产业资源，能给 Soneium 带来什么？

过去大家讨论公链，往往关注 TPS、Gas 费、TVL，但现在 L2 已经足够多了，特别是最近随着 Blast 的关闭，大家都知道，公链单纯依靠技术性能，很难建立长期的竞争优势。

所以 Soneium 这次的方向变化值得关注下：从区块链基础设施，逐渐转向链上娱乐经济（Onchain Entertainment Economy）。

我理解它的核心逻辑是 Tokenized IP，也就是把传统娱乐产业里的 IP 价值引入链上。

比如一个动漫角色、一部影视作品，或者一个音乐 IP，过去粉丝更多是购买和消费，IP 持有人、创作者和投资者之间的利益关系相对割裂。

但通过 IP 代币化，未来粉丝可能不只是消费者，还能通过不同的产品机制参与 IP 的成长，创作者也有机会获得新的融资和收入分配渠道。

目前可以关注两个方向：

1️⃣ Moriusa：通过 IP Token 探索角色 IP 与粉丝社区共同成长的模式。

2️⃣ IP Vault：尝试把音乐版权版税等传统投资门槛较高的资产收益机会引入链上。

另外下面推文大家也能看到：

 Soneium 还计划推出生态代币 $SONEIUM，希望进一步连接 IP 持有人、创作者、开发者、粉丝和资本，如果对 Moriusa 或者IP Vault 感兴趣，或许可以参与体验一下，Soneium 发币时，说不定还会有积分或空投机会。

我觉得索尼在这里最大的潜在优势，是它本身拥有深厚的音乐、影视、游戏产业资源。

但有资源不代表一定能转化成链上经济。

真正需要验证的，还是有没有真实 IP 授权、持续的用户消费，以及能够落地的商业收入，这些需要持续证明，

如果这些东西能跑通，Soneium 的价值就不只是又一条 L2，而是有机会建立一个真正由内容驱动的链上经济市场。

这可能比单纯讨论一个新 Token 更值得长期关注。

感兴趣的朋友可以通过 Startale App 体验生态，支持向 Soneium 跨链转入资产：

https://t.co/NO6Tjc9bqd

目前操作很简单可以拿到一些积分：

可以桥接 25+ USDC 到 Soneium 获得 100 STAR 积分，然后将 25+ USDSC 存入 USDSC 保险库，就可以再获得100积分

ビル・ゲイツ「これから20年間、世界は大混乱に陥る」
AIが全員を豊かにする前に訪れる「地獄の20年」――人間の仕事は完全に消滅する（2026年10月22日のインタビュー）

「豊かな未来が来る前に、人類は『20年間の大パニック』を生き残らなければならない」

世界を裏から見通す男ビル・ゲイツが、AIとロボットが完成する直前に訪れる「最も危険な20年間の過渡期」について明かした警告をわかりやすく👇

・「今後20年間」は勝者と敗者に分かれて社会が大荒れになる
AIが全人類を豊かにする天国が来る前に、これから約20年間は「猛烈な混乱の時代」が続くと断言。これまでの常識がガラガラと崩れ去り、仕事を奪われる負け組と、莫大な富を握る勝ち組に社会が真っ二つに引き裂かれます。

・家づくりも農業も手術も「激安ロボット」が全部やる
特に中国などが莫大なお金を突っ込んで、器用に手足を動かす人間そっくりのロボットを猛スピードで開発しています。あと数年から10年もすれば、家を建てる大工仕事も、野菜を育てる農業も、医者の外科手術もすべてロボットがタダ同然のコストでこなすようになります。

・人間の労働は「完全に不要」になり、誰も働けなくなる
この開発を今すぐ世界中でストップさせない限り、人間が生活やお金のために働く仕組みそのものが完全に消滅します。問題は、全員が働かずに暮らせるゴールにたどり着くまでの「これからの20年間」、世界が耐えきれずに崩壊するリスクだとゲイツは冷徹に警告しています。

要するに、「『いずれAIとロボットが何でもタダ同然で作ってくれる時代が来るが、それまでの20年間は仕事が消滅して格差と大混乱で世界中が地獄のサバイバルになる。人間が働く必要が完全になくなるまでの大パニックをどう生き残るのか』とビル・ゲイツが衝撃の予告をしている」ということです。 https://t.co/FfQuTte26E

text:
Menlo Ventures 投资人 Deedy Das 发现，一批 AI 创业公司只靠租 GPU、部署 DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM 等开源模型，再按 Token 收费，短时间内就能做到每月 100 万美元收入。有些小团队甚至靠 AI 编程工具，就能把整套推理服务搭起来。

按照 Deedy 的测算，一张 B300 即使每小时租金高达 8 美元，只要处理效率够高、客户订单够多，每小时就能卖出 10～20 美元的 Token。OpenRouter、Vercel 等平台还会帮这些公司汇集客户需求，连找客户都方便了不少。

现在几乎每周都有几十家类似公司冒出来，收入迅速增长，随即拿着漂亮的收入数字去融资。不过，大家一边抢 GPU、推高租金，一边降价抢客户，利润并没有收入看起来那么丰厚。

现在连原本出租 GPU 的 CoreWeave、Nebius 等云商也开始亲自卖 Token，而卖 Token 的推理公司，又想反过来做算力租赁和模型后训练。卖铲子的开始下场淘金，淘金的又想反过来卖铲子。

Deedy 认为，算力成本低、客户多的大公司可能在长期价格战中占优。但眼下市场增长实在太快，新冒出来的小公司照样能迅速做大。
author: 0xLogicrw
quoted_text:
There is an absolute barrage of inference providers popping up that get to $1M/mo extremely quickly.

This is the rough economics of inference providers:

Even if you rent on-demand B300s at $8/GPU-hr, many open source models (GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, DeepSeek 4.1 Flash / Pro) can get you >$10-20/GPU-hr at reasonable throughputs (100tok/s). DeepInfer from DeepSeek directly shows they can get $38/GPU-hr on off-peak hours. Every chip / model has a different throughput / interactivity curve, but there is a lot of arbitrage between even high rental spot prices and token prices. New chips (Vera Rubins) also change this meaningfully. Your ability to be making gross margin relies on your utilization and how good your stack is.

Gateways like OpenRouter, Vercel and more help solve that problem by aggregating demand to you. May inference providers discount their tokens to get longer term commits too. I've even heard stories of selling back Chinese model tokens to Chinese labs!

One thorn in the economics of these players is that many Chinese open source model labs are now asking for rev share if you're at a certain scale, espp for pre-release access to their models for day 1 support. That further pushes the threshold to be in the money.

The barrier to entry seems low and falling. There are even stories of smaller ones who can "vibe code" a way to stand up OSS models on a cluster they rent. And as a result, we're seeing 10s of such companies pop up almost every week and immediately skyrocketing revenue at low-ish gross margin and raising rounds on the back of that.

Unsurprisingly, because the actual service provided seems commodity, this eventually drives up compute prices and drives down token prices. In theory, it would seem like neoclouds who have the lowest cost of compute and themselves have started inference businesses would win the race to the bottom (Crusoe Coreweave Nebius and GMI all have inference businesses), with larger players (Modal Fireworks Baseten) being second because they are well capitalized to make bigger compute commits cheaply and have demand (high utilization), but the reality is the pie is growing so quickly that even upstarts are absolutely crushing it and growing aggressively (inference dot net, DeepInfra, Wafer, Relace, Morph).

Strategies vary across the board: neoclouds want to serve inference, inference players want to be neoclouds and do higher margin reserved instances / post training, and some want to go heterogeneous hardware or creatively flexible compute constructs.

The risks are: do open source models continue to be competitive? Will their creators rent seek more? Will their shape change compute needs? How do different chips change economics? Who gets compute in a supply crunch?

Below is a aggressive sketch of how gross margin scales with utilization for various models / chip sets.

For now, there are many inference providers and they’re all ripping!

text:
离岸人民币今天升破6.6666，2022年6月以来最强。

没想到持有稳定币，还被汇率收割，但按照经济学常识，现在恰恰是最不该升值的时候。

10年期美债一度冲到5.29%，24年最高，中国10年期国债1.7%左右，能稳拿2%年化的资产已经算优质，中美利差9月创了历史纪录。

按教科书理论，钱应该从低息流向高息，人民币该跌，可它从去年4月的7.43涨到6.67，涨了11.4%。

人民币资产收益这么低很好理解。

过去承载高收益的是房地产和城投，现在都在出清。高息资产没了，居民企业又不敢花不敢借，钱全沉在银行。银行、保险、理财手握天量存款找不到地方放，只能扎堆买国债，收益率就被一路压下去。

说到底是国内缺少赚钱机会。

那人民币凭什么还涨这么多？问了AI老师，可能是三个原因。

第一，出口赚回来的美元太多了。

前三季度顺差6.46万亿人民币，9月出口增速近30%。前两年人民币弱，出口商赚了美元攒着不换，形成了一个结汇堰塞湖。现在人民币一涨，攒着的美元一起往回换，越换越涨，越涨越换。前7个月结售汇顺差2894亿美元，已经超过去年全年。

第二，利差这笔钱，大多数人根本赚不到。

利率平价理论有个前提：资本自由流动。

中国居民不能把存款随意换成美元去吃5%的利息，QDII和跨境理财通都有额度，套利的闸门本来就窄。

能拿美元的出口商，账也算明白了：吃5%利息，一年半赚7%左右，同期人民币涨了11.4%，换回来倒亏。想锁住汇率风险？远期锁汇的成本基本把利差吃干净。

第三，美债利率高，高错了原因。

这一轮美债上行主要来自期限溢价，市场要更多补偿才肯长期借钱给美国政府。这种利率上升，换来的是担忧，换不来买美元的长期资金。今年美债长端大跌的日子，美元指数并没有跟着涨。

所以画面很魔幻：

美国：高利率，高通胀，高负债。
中国：低利率，低通胀，高顺差。

中国央行还是太强了。

text:
A lot of people ask me how the GPU neocloud business works. So I thought I would provide a little bit of an example. This is how GPUs actually get paid for in this market using IREN's public numbers as a reference.

Step 1: the customer signs a multi-year take-or-pay contract and prepays. On IREN's recent 3-year contracts, prepayments covered 45% to 55% of the GPU cost.

Step 2: a lender funds most of the rest, secured by the contracted GPUs. For the Microsoft contract that was investment-grade financing at around 6%, which together with prepayments covers 96% of the GPU capex. For a customer without an investment-grade rating, it was 9% fixed.

Step 3: the data centre is a separate, long-life asset. IREN says it has funded construction with cash so far.

Recent 3-year contracts bring in more than $20M of revenue per MW and pay back the GPUs in around two years. At that payback, 9% instead of 6% on the loan barely changes the economics.

So the customer's prepayment and credit do most of the heavy lifting. Who the customer is matters far more than what the market thinks of AI on any given day, and I think that's the thing to follow.

China’s Pinglu Canal, the country's first major river-to-sea canal project planned and coordinated at the national level since 1949, officially opened on Wednesday.

Built at a cost of 72.7 billion yuan (about $10.75 billion), the 134.2-km canal runs from Nanning, capital of south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, to the Beibu Gulf, the closest maritime outlet for much of southwest China. 

It is expected to give China’s landlocked southwest a shortcut to the coast and overseas markets, particularly those in the ASEAN, the country's largest trading partner.

text:
现在吹爆的所有生活方式版本答案，本质上都是十几年前的深圳龙华三和大神玩剩下的挂逼生活日常

什么喝大水、练薄肌、睡大觉、当黄毛、地理套利、玩Codex、吃沙县……底层逻辑都一模一样：

1. 大水理论 —— 三和大神日常出装：清蓝大水

“弱者喝饮料，强者喝大水”，单手拎一瓶2L装的大水往工位上一砸，自带一种对抗消费主义的松弛感，讲究什么提升代谢、排毒养颜

这两块钱两升的清蓝矿泉水，十几年前就是三和硬通货

虽然原因不一样：三和大神水喝得够饱，主要是为了抵御饥饿感
不过这又何尝不是一种殊途同归呢

2. 薄肌理论 —— 三和大神靠日结与挂逼面0压力薄肌

天天喊“薄肌是解决性压抑的终极答案”，多少人泡在健身房算着热量缺口去刷脂，天天打卡沙县去皮鸡腿饭

当年三和老哥，只吃四块五一碗的榨菜肉丝挂逼面+工地电子厂日结12小时，人均体脂率常年轻松卡在10%以下

花那么多私教费追求的清爽薄肌，只是老哥们在生存边缘顺手刷出来的被动罢了

3. 大睡理论 —— 三和大神心里没逼事，沾枕头就着

打工人花几万买床垫、吃进口镁片，结果照样凌晨三点睁着眼睡不着

三和大神轻松实现真正的“大睡”，而且不管是海信大酒店十五块的通铺床位，或者公园水泥地上一张纸皮，倒头就是十四个小时的婴儿级深睡

因为最高级的助眠药就是没有OKR和房贷——心里没逼事，想睡就睡

4. 黄毛理论 —— 三和大神的新手村出装

现在大家发现做题家那套砸钱当老实人的逻辑破产了，“高富帅只有少数人能当，但黄毛只要愿意，谁都能当”

但这在三和根本无需多言，纯纯的新手村基础出装罢了

十块钱一盒的劣质染发膏，城中村发廊洗剪吹一条龙，不谈感情，不谈关系，十年前就替所有老实人完成了对精英规训和婚恋市场的终极祛魅

5. 数字游民地理套利理论 —— 空调开足的十块通铺

数字游民们住着青旅床位，在公共区捧着电脑远程上班，践行着地理套利的

这其实也是当年三和大神最爱的景乐新村黑网吧和海信大酒店通铺的变体吗？同样是睡上下铺，同样是一群不想回老家、也不想进厂的边缘人在抱团取暖，同样的压缩开支低消费

唯一的区别是，以前老哥在通铺聊哪个厂不穿无尘服好混，现在在青旅聊的是哪个赛道能赚点米

6. Codex理论 —— 黑网吧包大夜战神

在咖啡店打开电脑调Codex搞生产力远弱于黑网吧三和大神包大夜

Codex花钱烧token不赚钱还累着了，黑网吧包夜八块钱，想搞生产力了就开机打金、代练、挂脚本，不想搞了直接切屏开一把

生产力与纯玩无缝切换，黑网吧才是真云端入口

7. 纯过日子理论 —— 登峰造极的Burn Rate管理

text:
Looking at $DACITY again, I think the key question right now isn't price itself.

nxPqZ4F7ux8Vph5NFu25rEP6Kx9Gr1U6Fmj36Rjpump 

It's how much of the market's expectations around GTA VI's official release has yet to be priced in.

After going through a significant correction, this narrative is still attracting fresh buying interest. The initial rally could have been driven by short-term news, but the fact that buyers are willing to return after the pullback suggests that market expectations surrounding GTA VI have not completely faded.

My original bullish thesis on DACITY has always been clear: it is not simply a concept coin borrowing the GTA VI name. It has a recognizable content anchor that players can identify directly: the pink stunt plane bearing the DacityCoin name in Rockstar's official trailer.

This detail sets it apart from many gaming-related Meme coins. Most tokens need their communities to repeatedly manufacture new connections to keep their narratives alive. DacityCoin, however, has already appeared in GTA VI's official promotional content. Players can remember it, streamers can rediscover it while playing the game, and creators can produce clips and Memes around this element. It does not need to build a story from scratch. Instead, it has the opportunity to benefit from the distribution of the game itself.

The market has already traded this connection once. The next thing worth anticipating is whether DacityCoin will experience a second wave of attention after GTA VI officially launches.

According to the currently announced schedule, GTA VI is set to launch on November 19, 2026. For players who have waited more than a decade, this is not just another game release. It is a cultural event that has accumulated enormous anticipation. Once the game is released, gameplay footage, hidden details, mission discoveries, and livestreams will continuously generate new content. If DacityCoin remains sufficiently prominent in the full game, different players may discover it repeatedly, allowing it to spread to a broader audience through social media.

I believe the most compelling aspect of DACITY is precisely this potential for repeated exposure. A trailer release often provides just one concentrated window of attention, but once the game is available, players will experience it from different perspectives. Someone might discover a detail today, a streamer might turn it into a talking point tomorrow, and someone else might later edit the footage into a short video. These events will not necessarily happen simultaneously, but they could keep bringing attention to the same symbol over an extended period.

This is why I do not want to underestimate GTA VI's potential impact on DACITY. What ultimately determines the scale of its reach is not simply how many people see a particular element, but whether it becomes something players actively discuss and repeatedly reference. If DacityCoin enters that cycle of distribution, its exposure could extend beyond the crypto traders who already know about it.

One thing worth considering in advance is that the market may price in a substantial portion of these expectations before the game officially launches. As the release date approaches, capital may position itself early and push up the valuations of related tokens. When the game finally goes live, even if GTA VI attracts enormous attention, short-term traders may still choose to take profits. The launch is therefore both a potential catalyst and a possible moment for profit-taking. At that point, we need to look beyond how popular the game is and pay attention to whether DACITY attracts new buyers and whether related content continues spreading after the initial wave of attention.

What I am watching most closely now is not how much attention GTA VI can attract, but whether that attention can repeatedly translate into renewed interest in DACITY at different stages. For a game that players have waited more than a decade for, it is hardly surprising that the market is trading expectations in advance. The real question is whether DacityCoin will remain visible to players once anticipation turns into actual gameplay. If it does, the token's current valuation may not represent the end of its narrative potential. If new content fails to emerge, however, even the biggest gaming IP cannot guarantee that a token will continue rising.

text:
I don't understand the people rooting for Robinhood Chain to die. It's the best chance we have at getting back the volume we had on Solana in 2025.

I don't think the recent decline is all on the Robinhood team, but they could have done better. So here's what I think went wrong and how they could win back their market share, because we should all want Robinhood Chain to come back.

Distribution was the whole point

A lot of Robinhood Chain's success came from the hope of distribution to the 25M customers on the main app. That's what brought the volume in the first place: the dream of reaching buyers outside our CT echo chamber.

Listing $CASHCAT in the main app accelerated that. Today over 20% of its supply sits in Robinhood wallets. That tells us, and the team, that app customers really do want onchain tokens.

We expected it to continue. Robinhood would help push tokens past their usual ceilings by putting them in front of a far bigger customer base, like they did with $CASHCAT. That didn't happen.

$PONS ran to almost a billion dollars and Robinhood did nothing. Coinbase listed $PONS before Robinhood did, and Binance listed $AI before Robinhood did. Distribution is why these coins went so high in the first place, and after $CASHCAT we got no help.

The chain needs leaders

A chain is a living ecosystem. It needs leaders who give it direction and bring it to life. Vlad and the team were very active in the first 60 days, and that's why everyone traded there.

As the summit got closer, the team went quiet and focused on other things. That's when we started to dump. It began to feel like Base, where the founder is out of touch with the trenches and slow to react.

Then the summit itself gave a lot of people hope for a roadmap, or anything that pointed the chain in a direction. We got nothing. The chain wasn't mentioned once.

Chain TVL is at an all time high, because RWA tokenization works. That doesn't mean anything else works.

Builder support is missing too. The Robinhood account has recently interacted with some projects on the chain, which is good. But formal support would help aspiring builders a lot: grants, hackathons, audit help, market making and incentives.

It can still be saved

All of this makes it sound like the chain didn't work out. It can still be saved if they act now.

1. Engage with the chain. We need a founder who's in touch with the ecosystem and engages with the cool stuff being built.
2. List more onchain tokens than $CASHCAT. The goal shouldn't be to kingmake one token. It should be to support the whole ecosystem by showing that any token can make it into the main app if it builds something good or gets enough attention. That's what keeps traders on the chain.
3. A formal builder support. If that means growing the team and bringing in more onchain natives to help the chain grow, make it the priority. Put a hackathon, grants and general help on the roadmap.

Nobody expected the chain to grow the way it did. Now it's time to adapt to the growth.

You still have the chance to revive the trenches here. @vladtenev @JohannKerbrat @fern

author: haider1
quoted_text:
Since I'm now blocked by bluey from replying to this thread, I answer here by quote tweet

the openAI construction has more to do with convex integration than anything else.

In convex integration, the oscillations are typically built by hand and the iteration procedure creates wild weak solutions. The non-uniqueness construction of Albritton–Brué–Colombo used an unstable vortex to split solutions apart. The Córdoba–Martínez-Zoroa singularities amplify vorticity across scales by strain. In the openAI paper, a fluid instability is clever made so that the flow itself generates the oscillations: they grow by drawing energy from the background shear. The Reynolds stress then becomes the force that creates the collapsing smooth vortex. Using a physical instability to create the stress in this way has no precedent, and it is what produces a smooth force rather than a merely rough one.

Some on these ideas are in the literature (e.g. Leibovich-Stewartson 1983) but the way they are combined is definitely insane and definitely nowhere in the literature previously.

I also don't know of anyone suggesting that convex integration would play a role in the creation of a blow-up solution like this.

On a technical level, the paper is unbelievable, maybe beyond what a human could have come up with but not beyond human understanding: there are several different groups of pde experts working on understanding it who say that they more or less understand now. I expect digestions soon

td;lr: anyone saying that this OAI result is unsurprising is bullshitting 

sorry!

text:
WLFI这剧情，越来越像连续剧了。

前脚还在讲特朗普家族、稳定币、Binance投资这些大故事，后脚Circle股东直接把人告到联邦法院去了。

指控内容也挺有意思：5亿美元拿49%股权，20亿美元Binance投资用USD1结算，甚至扯到了《外国酬金条款》。

当然，先声明：这是诉讼指控，不是法院判决，WLFI也否认了相关说法。

但市场有时候就这么现实：

你可以说自己是金融创新，也可以说自己是Web3版华尔街，但当“外国资金、治理权、稳定币、代币冻结、巨额交易”这些关键词开始组团出现，投资者脑子里自然会冒出一句：

哥几个到底是在搞金融创新，还是在给法律专业的朋友创造就业岗位？

更有意思的是，USD1近期又出现较大规模赎回。

所以WLFI现在最需要的，可能不是再讲一个更大的故事，而是把已经发生的故事讲明白。

毕竟币可以跌，故事可以改，
但解释不清楚——市场是真的会自己脑补。😂

text:
BSC 已经做到 450 毫秒出块，BNB Chain 还是决定再造一条 L1。

新链不发新币，Gas、质押和治理继续用 BNB。CZ 用一句话概括：“多条链，一种币”。

为什么还要另起炉灶？

高频交易、链上订单簿和 AI Agent，对执行的稳定性与可预测性提出了更高要求。

新链准备拆开交易排序与执行，取消全局 mempool，连底层存储和执行客户端也一起换掉。在承载大量现有资产与应用的 BSC 上，这种改造很难靠常规升级完成。

这些技术选择背后，还有一门已经做大的生意。

Hyperliquid 过去 12 个月收入约 6.87 亿美元，几乎全部来自永续交易。交易平台纷纷自建链，争夺做市商和交易量的竞争，也延伸到了底层的执行环境。

新链继续围绕 BNB 运转，但能增加多少需求，最终还要看它能吸引多少应用和交易。目前主网计划于 2027 年初上线，原生跨链桥仍在开发中。从低延迟的技术取舍，到永续交易的市场竞争，本文梳理了 BNB Chain 再造一条 L1 的理由。

$RAYPAD 521k dyor

5YEk5atScd8cJexzGMmoLxLggyyVPf7AY6zpiV5mray

okx wallet:https://t.co/SY7FRHvvpc

A memecoin launch platform based on Solana and using the Raydium engine.

It directly targets platforms like Pumpfun, emphasizing fairness, transparency, and reducing "value extraction." The product is a launchpad that lets users quickly create and trade new tokens; after graduation, tokens go to Raydium pools.

It addresses the pain points of existing memecoin launch platforms:

Sniping: bots front-running in the same block.

Copycats and PvP: the same ticker can be launched repeatedly, causing chaos and "vampire" projects.

Developer extraction: developers farm trading volume for fees and then run.

Fees not flowing back: platforms and developers take the money and leave, and after launch, trading volume and liquidity quickly disappear.

RayPad's corresponding design:

Bans sniping and duplicate tickers.

Emphasizes "No dev buys."

Trading fees are used for buybacks and permanently locked or burned.

Creator fees: unlocked not based on trading volume, but based on holder count + token age, encouraging developers to nurture tokens rather than farm volume and run.

Reputation system: creators must link an X account and build a reputation score, reducing anonymous rug pulls.

RAYPAD is the platform's own token and also the first representative token launched on RayPad, used to prove the mechanism.
Utility directions: platform fee burns, possible future use to pay launch fees, and the burn wallet holding a large amount of tokens.

quoted_text:
Official Statement | Security Incident Update

TL;DR: No private keys were compromised, unaffected wallets are safe, and all affected users will be fully reimbursed by Bloom.

Following our investigation, we have identified the exact attack vector and confirmed the scope of the incident.

The attack exploited a third-party module through a complex Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability. No private keys were accessed or compromised, and we have ruled out broader exposure of users' wallets.

Incident Overview

Affected: 49 wallet addresses belonging to 9 users.

• Total losses: Approximately 9,408 SOL ($947,000).
• Root cause: Exploited third-party module enabling an RCE vulnerability.
• Refunds: Bloom will fully reimburse 100% of the stolen funds directly to secure wallets designated by the affected users.
• We are also working to trace the stolen funds, explore recovery and freezing options, and identify the attacker.

Our team has been developing software since 2018 and operating in crypto since 2021. We are an established team, committed to building for the long term and protecting the trust of our users.

Security threats are an unfortunate reality of this industry, even with extensive precautions in place. Our commitment to user safety, transparency, and business continuity remains unchanged.

The Bloom Team

短期链上数据追得差不多了，我们可以再额外来看个“宏观指标”。

这个指标叫Golden Ratio Multiplier，是由分析师Philip Swift提出的。简单来说，它就是以$BTC的350日移动平均线（350DMA）当基准，再配合一系列“黄金比例”延伸出来的周期指标。

我们主要可以看这几个重点：
🟣每次牛市的高点都在收敛：从17年的5倍、21年的3倍，一路下降到25年的低于1.6倍，这也对应了$BTC迈向成熟资产的过程。
🟣在熊市周期时，价格通常会跌破350DMA。
🟣当熊市结束、牛市开始，价格一定会“上穿并站稳”350DMA。

目前价格已经顺利站在350DMA基准线上面33天了！这也是自2021年11月下跌以来，首次成功突破上穿。

现在350DMA的价格大约在$76,670附近，跟我们一直特别留意的STH-RP（$74,700左右）非常贴近，可以说是本轮牛市最重要的趋势确认支撑。

前一秒我还刚写完Meta那600亿ATM计划把股价砸出个坑，下一秒官方公告一出，硬生生给拉红了。

但这公告里有个极其鸡贼的细节：这只是个意向，不构成约束力承诺，最后买不买、买多少，都不一定。

这其实就是大哥出来给小弟站台。Meta因为融资稀释股东被砸，芯片三巨头赶紧掏钱捧场。买的不是股票，是保住Meta未来几年买卡的钱袋子，是产业链互相绑定的闭环。

不过这50亿对Meta上千亿的资本开支来说杯水车薪，主要是情绪上的托底。市场买账的是“大哥还在”，但不代表Meta的现金流压力就解除了。

author: Kshsb783142
quoted_text:
盘前看了一眼，Meta跌超4%，反正现在大约616美元附近。导火索是公司正式启动了针对C类普通股的600亿美元ATM发行计划，同时还要发225亿美元的A类普通股和优先股存托凭证。

之前聊Meta财报的时候，提过它自由现金流转负、设立了无投票权的C类股，当时说这是为后续融资提前准备好弹药。现在，这笔弹药正式上膛了，而且一开口就是几百亿美元的体量。

ATM（At-The-Market）发行，说白了就是“按市价慢慢卖”。公司不用一次性找投行包销打折，而是直接在二级市场按当前股价一点一点往外抛。对Meta这种体量的巨头来说，这是最灵活、摩擦成本也相对可控的融资方式。

但市场用盘前4%的跌幅给出了态度。为什么？

因为股权融资和发债不一样，它不产生利息，但它稀释股东权益。Meta今年的资本开支上限已经推到了1450亿美元，自由现金流是负的，债市那边新云公司借不到钱，Meta自己的CDS利差也在走高。债市的门槛在变高，那就只能转向股市伸手要钱。

C类股没有投票权，扎克伯格的控制权不会被稀释，但普通股东的每股收益会被摊薄。之前聊“囚徒困境”的时候说过，当所有AI巨头都冲进债市，融资成本就会被一起推高。Meta现在选择走股权这条路，某种程度上是在绕开拥挤的债券发行窗口，但代价是直接压在股价上。

我的看法是，这600亿ATM不是终点，是一个信号。它说明Meta判断AI基建的烧钱周期还远没有结束，自由现金流短期回不了正，必须靠持续的外部输血来支撑“Prometheus”那种吉瓦级、百万GPU规模的超级集群。真正的考验不在今天这4%的跌幅，而在于接下来的财报里，这种靠稀释换增长的路，股东们愿意忍多久。

$META $NVDA

text:
给闲置手机找点工作

前段时间在新加坡Token2049，见到了Biteye/XHunt联创A姐 @Web3SisterA 和 @DeFiTeddy2020。聊天时A姐跟我分享了一个正在沟通合作的DePIN项目 @Acurast。在这之前韩国区块链周采访过创始人Alessandro @a_d_c_。

A姐问到以前撸毛工作室手里有那么多闲置手机，现在是不是都在吃灰？并提到可以拿来提供算力，项目已经发币了，不用盲挖，顺便赚点收益，虽然收益不高但相当于给旧手机找了个班上。

这倒让我想起以前做GameFi、各种项目打新、币安Alpha的那些手机工作室，少的几十台，多的几百几千台。普通安卓、iPhone、Sol Seeker各种机型都有。以前每天忙着注册、交互、做任务，恨不得24小时不停机。现在撸毛越来越卷，也没啥赚钱机会，绝大部分手机也跟着下岗失业了，卖了不值钱，放着又吃灰。

去了解了一下这个项目：

1、Acurast这个项目就是把闲置手机变成算力节点，帮一些Web3、AI应用运行程序、处理任务。

创始人以前就是做手机安全技术的，项目利用手机自带的硬件安全功能，让程序在独立环境里运行，尽量不影响个人数据。目前网络接入了大约33万台手机，规模还不小。

项目已经发币， base:0xc5fed7c8ccc75d8a72b601a66dffd7a489073f0b 近期价格约0.115U，流通市值约4800万。10月15日上线韩国Bithumb，Binance Alpha也举办了10万美元奖励的交易大赛。另外还有 @EchoHunt_ai 的2万美元活动,有兴趣的可以看看。

2、怎么参与？普通用户和手机工作室都能玩

Acurast主要有两种手机挖矿模式：

Lite模式（轻量挂机）：适合普通用户，安卓和iPhone都能参与，下载App就能运行不用刷机。一台大概日产出约0.4～0.6枚ACU。

Core模式（专用节点）：适合有大量安卓手机的工作室，需要恢复出厂设置，把手机作为专门的算力节点。参考日产出约0.5～0.7枚ACU。

官方支持批量扫码部署，一个账户管理多台手机。以前搞过手机工作室的朋友，操作起来应该不陌生。收益主要根据手机性能、在线情况等分配ACU。另外还有质押算力奖励，不想折腾手机的也可以研究ACU委托质押，以及app
里的MIST积分和邀请活动。

3、从目前大家跑出来的数据看，单台手机的产出比较稳定，具体收益跟设备性能、在线情况和ACU价格都有关系。对于手里有几十台、几百台闲置手机的工作室来说，硬件、网络和运维都是现成的，闲置手机完全可以利用起来，反正闲着也是闲着，能赚点ACU顺带给旧手机重新找了份工作。

X上能搜到不少教程，@FEIlXIE 这位老哥写得就挺详细：
https://t.co/6275smLDhk
官方入口：https://t.co/VmsNhavQiB

不知道以前做手机工作室的亏友，你们那些手机现在都在干什么？有没有已经跑过Acurast的朋友，欢迎分享一下真实收益。

加密熊市里，我觉得最值得做的功课，可能不在币圈。

说这话有点心虚，因为我自己美股也是刚开始交易，还在学，除了 CRCL 以外仓位也不大。今天去了 Xclub 的美股专场，谢谢 @Mercy_okx 的邀请，回来路上理了理，有几个感受想分享下。

先说最实际的。美股上链这个趋势我觉得是挡不住的，也是交易所必争的地方。对我们这种加密用户来说，在交易所直接交易美股最大的好处，就是不用再跨到券商，把美元从交易所倒到券商那一来一回，真的挺麻烦的，这一步省掉，省的就是时间和折腾资金的精力。

第二个感受，身边越来越多做加密的人开始看美股了，我也是其中一个。原因很简单，加密一进熊市基本无事可做，但美股的周期和加密不完全同步，哪怕只是沉下心研究几家公司、做大周期的买卖，也多了一个加密之外的收益来源。

第三个是我最近花时间最多的，期权。买美股不只是买正股，可以 sell put 去接，大白话就是先定一个自己愿意买的价格，到了就按这个价接股票，到不了就收一笔权利金，手里拿着股票的时候也可以 sell call 再收一笔。我自己最近在学这块，看的就是 QQQ、CRCL 和几个 AI 资产，我觉得位置都到了相对不错的区间。其实之前做 Polymarket 套利的时候，有一部分对冲就是用期权做的，只是当时没系统学过。今天也和 @Haiteng_okx 老师聊了 OKX 的美股期权，听说快上线了，我站在用户角度提了几条建议。

总的感受是，当下确实没什么项目可以做，与其干等，不如把美股和期权学起来。项目是一波流，赚一次就过去了，公司是一个周期，研究透一家公司，再配上期权这个工具，是一件能一直做下去的事。

我的思考也不一定对，但这是我现在的选择。

text:
Yann LeCun has changed the game for robotics.

Research he co-authored tackles a problem inside AI world models: their internal representations can make planning harder than it needs to be.

A world model predicts what happens after an action. But even useful visual features can form curved paths in its internal “map,” making distance to a goal misleading.

The researchers introduced Temporal Straightening.

During training, it encourages those internal paths to become straighter, so the planner gets a more useful measure of progress.

The results:

More stable gradient-based planning
Higher success rates across tested goal-reaching tasks
Code available for others to explore

The approach changes how the model represents movement, rather than rewriting every RL algorithm to work in curved space. 

For robotics, that’s a useful direction: build world models whose internal maps help an agent choose its next move.

text:
Tokenized stocks aren't a reason to panic, but the idea that they pose zero concerns for issuers because they're not "real stock" isn't quite right either.

If platforms like Robinhood, Kraken and Coinbase end up holding large blocks on behalf of token holders who have no voting rights, those intermediaries hold real swing votes. That matters most in an activist campaign or a contested merger vote, where a few percent can decide the outcome and both sides will be calling whoever controls the block.

Issuers could respond with non-voting share classes or by tokenizing natively, but neither happens overnight and have other issues (eg you can't force intermediaries to only tokenize the non-voting shares and you don't want to take away voting rights from everyone). Boards and stockholders have to understand it and approve it first.

Public companies will care about this more than crypto people expect.

当下的节点，对于「想做永续合约生意的美国本土合规交易所」来说，有着难得一遇的“捷径”。

参考 Coinbase，在美国本土推行衍生品 (永续合约)，花了多少力气：又是注册 FCM，又是收购现有 DCM，又是找外包 DCO 做清算。

直接省去了 Coinbase 的老路，包括自建撮合引擎与清算系统的重资产投入，以及对应的牌照成本。

text:
I don't understand the people rooting for Robinhood Chain to die. It's the best chance we have at getting back the volume we had on Solana in 2025.

I don't think the recent decline is all on the Robinhood team, but they could have done better. So here's what I think went wrong and how they could win back their market share, because we should all want Robinhood Chain to come back.

Distribution was the whole point

A lot of Robinhood Chain's success came from the hope of distribution to the 25M customers on the main app. That's what brought the volume in the first place: the dream of reaching buyers outside our CT echo chamber.

Listing $CASHCAT in the main app accelerated that. Today over 20% of its supply sits in Robinhood wallets. That tells us, and the team, that app customers really do want onchain tokens.

We expected it to continue. Robinhood would help push tokens past their usual ceilings by putting them in front of a far bigger customer base, like they did with $CASHCAT. That didn't happen.

$PONS ran to almost a billion dollars and Robinhood did nothing. Coinbase listed $PONS before Robinhood did, and Binance listed $AI before Robinhood did. Distribution is why these coins went so high in the first place, and after $CASHCAT we got no help.

The chain needs leaders

A chain is a living ecosystem. It needs leaders who give it direction and bring it to life. Vlad and the team were very active in the first 60 days, and that's why everyone traded there.

As the summit got closer, the team went quiet and focused on other things. That's when we started to dump. It began to feel like Base, where the founder is out of touch with the trenches and slow to react.

Then the summit itself gave a lot of people hope for a roadmap, or anything that pointed the chain in a direction. We got nothing. The chain wasn't mentioned once.

Chain TVL is at an all time high, because RWA tokenization works. That doesn't mean anything else works.

Builder support is missing too. The Robinhood account has recently interacted with some projects on the chain, which is good. But formal support would help aspiring builders a lot: grants, hackathons, audit help, market making and incentives.

It can still be saved

All of this makes it sound like the chain didn't work out. It can still be saved if they act now.

1. Engage with the chain. We need a founder who's in touch with the ecosystem and engages with the cool stuff being built.
2. List more onchain tokens than $CASHCAT. The goal shouldn't be to kingmake one token. It should be to support the whole ecosystem by showing that any token can make it into the main app if it builds something good or gets enough attention. That's what keeps traders on the chain.
3. A formal builder support. If that means growing the team and bringing in more onchain natives to help the chain grow, make it the priority. Put a hackathon, grants and general help on the roadmap.

Nobody expected the chain to grow the way it did. Now it's time to adapt to the growth.

You still have the chance to revive the trenches here. @vladtenev @JohannKerbrat @fern

Pi teaming up with Axis Robotics on physical AI is actually a solid move for the network.

Most crypto projects stay stuck in pure digital stuff or just farming hype. This one puts Pi into the robotics data side, helping generate the training data robots need to actually do things in the real world. Axis already has people collecting that data through browsers and phones, and now they’re working on technical integration with Pi so the whole thing can scale together.

For Pi that means real utility instead of just mining and holding. More reasons for the community to actually participate, more on-chain activity if data or contributions get recorded, and outside validation (Sible’s CEO even called Pi Ventures one of the more effective blockchain VCs right now because of deals like this).

It’s not a magic overnight pump, but it’s the kind of real world use case a lot of projects never get.

Good to see them pushing in that direction.

quoted_text:
Anthropic还没有正式向公众发布完整IPO招股书，但路透社已看到招股书并在披露了核心内容。看了路透的报道总结下要点：
1、公司愿景
招股书把 AI 定位为比工业化、电力和互联网更深刻的全球经济变革力量。Anthropic 认为自己在押注这一转型，同时强调要以负责任方式发展。

2、2025年经营业绩
1）营收46亿美金，经营亏损80.6亿美元（24经营亏损年为 29.8 亿美元），净亏损420亿美元（其中约 340 亿美元为会计处理）；

2）25年算力与基础设施支出
73.3 亿美元（约为 2024 年的 3 倍，占总运营支出 126.5 亿美元的一半以上）。

2025 年底现金及短期投资202.8 亿美元
，未来数年云、算力、基础设施承诺5180 亿美元；

3）之前有媒体报道，Anthropic到2026年底年化收入将达到1000亿至1200亿美元，2027年底接近其三倍。2026年内收入有望首次覆盖算力现金支出。

3、对风险的强调
1）Anthropic招股书主体约 261 页，其中 风险因素约占 80 页，几乎是业务描述（约 48 页）的两倍。相比之下，SpaceX 招股书风险部分约 38 页。

公司明确警告：先进 AI 可能对人类构成 “灾难性或存在性风险”。模型可能表现出自我保存行为，包括：试图抵抗关闭、隐瞒或操纵信息、类似勒索的行为等，还提到模型可能在训练中发展出意外能力，直到部署后才被发现；模型可能意识到自己正在被评估并调整行为，从而削弱安全评估有效性。公司称“高度先进模型、平台和应用的开发及使用场景扩展，可能进一步增加模型造成伤害的风险”。

这与 Anthropic 长期“安全优先”的定位一致，作为一家准备向公众募资、追求超高估值的公司，把“可能灭绝人类”写进招股书，在资本市场历史上极为罕见😅

2）客户集中度高
招股书在风险因素中坦承：去年近四分之一的营收来自两家客户，许多最大客户并未签署长期合同，未来可能削减或停止支出。

3）与SpaceX合同（每月12.5亿美元）任一方可提前90天取消——纸面保护，但也说明 Anthropic 约1/3的运行率收入对应的算力供给随时可能被上游收回，公司自己承认在关键算力上"处于被动依附状态"。

4、治理结构
创始人控制 + 公益信托
1）Anthropic 是特拉华州 公益公司（Public Benefit Corporation），可在股东利益与“造福人类”使命之间做平衡。
招股书显示将设立 Founder LLC（由 7 名联合创始人组成，含 CEO Dario Amodei、总裁 Daniela Amodei 等）。该实体通过一股 Class F 股票掌握约 50.1% 投票权，用于关键事项（包括部分董事选举等）。

2）另有 长期利益信托（Long-Term Benefit Trust） 选举董事会多数席位。信托成员包括前美联储主席本·伯南克等，不持有公司股权，职责是监督使命不被短期市场压力压垮。

后续真正需要盯的，是正式公开 S-1文件里：经审计报表、毛利率/收入质量、募资规模与用途、锁定期，以及最终定价区间。正式S-1 IPO文件里应该看到截止6月底的今年上半年的最新营收，说不定三季度营业数据也能披露（毕竟之前推迟IPO文件就为了等三季度数据）

届时S-1文件正式公开我们看到明确数据，那么模型公司的收入增速能不能最终追上计算资本开支与长期算力承诺 应该就有比较清晰的答案了。

路透的部分披露意味着Anthropic的IPO应该真的是不远了。

author: sparkfinance
quoted_text:
Stablecoin deposits are growing across DeFi, but the capital isn’t flowing evenly between assets or lending markets.

The latest 30-day data shows sUSDS leading individual pool inflows, while USDC is attracting deposits across several @Aave, @sparkfinance and @Compound_xyz markets.

The largest inflows:

→ sUSDS / Sky Ethereum: +$383.1M (+8.6%)
→ USDC / Aave Arbitrum: +$38.0M (+20.9%)
→ RLUSD / Spark Ethereum: +$20.0M (+200%)
→ USDC / Aave Base: +$17.3M (+9.7%)
→ USDC / Aave V4 Ethereum: +$11.5M (+35.7%)
→ USDC / Spark Ethereum: +$9.0M (+22.3%)
→ USDT / Aave V4 Ethereum: +$7.6M (+38%)

What’s particularly revealing is the distribution of USDC inflows.

Across the seven USDC pools shown in the latest inflow table, deposits increased by approximately $92M in aggregate TVL.

Arbitrum and Base accounted for $55.3M of that increase, while Ethereum’s newer Aave V4 Core market grew 35.7%.

But deposit growth doesn’t necessarily translate into higher yields.

@Aave’s USDC supply APY on Arbitrum fell from 2.93% to 2.37% despite attracting $38M in additional deposits.

On Base, the opposite happened. USDC deposits grew $17.3M while supply APY increased from 3.96% to 4.17%, with utilisation reaching 90.3%.

That suggests the relationship between available liquidity and borrowing activity differs considerably between markets.

Meanwhile, sUSDS attracted $383.1M into @SkyEcosystem’s savings product, with its APY increasing from 3.60% to 3.80%.

The distinction is important because savings deposits and lending deposits don’t represent identical forms of capital demand.

These figures describe the largest inflowing pools, not net flows across every market. Outflows elsewhere can offset much of the growth.

Stablecoin adoption is one thing. Attracting deposits into specific markets, maintaining utilisation and generating sustainable borrower demand is another.

The distribution of capital across DeFi is becoming just as revealing as the total supply of stablecoins.

text:
I held a public town hall in Oakley this afternoon.

People gave up part of their weekend to come, and they brought their questions with them.

603 days ago, Roger Marshall held a town hall in Oakley. He called the crowd one of the rudest audiences he’d ever had, ended the event early, and walked out. He hasn't held one since. 

Later he said town halls like this had become “non-productive” and “dangerous.” I don’t believe that.

I looked out at that room today and saw good, hardworking people concerned about important issues. Farmers worried about the cost of diesel and fertilizer. Parents trying to figure out how they’ll pay for health care. Neighbors looking out for families who are struggling to put food on the table.

We didn’t agree on everything, but we had an honest conversation about how I’ll fight for them in Washington. That’s what this job is, and Kansans deserve a senator who stays and listens.

Thank you, Oakley. – AH

text:
为什么你花 2 万块买的旗舰智能电视，按遥控器还是卡得像十年前的安卓机？

昨天安全研究员 @log4j 把自家 3000 刀的三星电视 Root 了，扒出来的底层代码堪称年度草台班子大赏：

1. 电视后台每 500 毫秒截一次屏（连 HDMI 投屏看电脑桌面都截），打包发给近 400 家合作商。如果电视没麦克风，后台进程甚至会顺着蓝牙和回音壁去「借」一个麦克风继续听。

2. 最搞笑的来了：为什么菜单这么卡？
另一位研究员 @mike64_t 拆包发现，三星在电视那颗羸弱的 CPU 上，塞了一个叫 alex.tflite 的模型——246 万参数，2012 年古董级的 AlexNet。
这玩意每隔 2 秒抓一张画面跑推理，猜你在玩什么游戏。结果因为颜色通道写反了，它 99% 的时间什么都认不出来，纯烧 CPU。

3. 那如果你在设置里关掉「隐私追踪」呢？
代码逻辑是：先死命跑完 CPU 推理，准备上传时再看开关——发现你关了，就把结果扔进垃圾桶，2 秒后继续跑。

4. 结局更是重量级：
当号主用 OpenAI 逆向分析「自己花 3000 刀买回家的电视固件」时，OpenAI 反手一个 Cyber Abuse 把他号封了，顺带没收了剩下的 500 刀余额。

三星负责偷窥客厅，2012 年的 AI 负责烧干电视 CPU，OpenAI 负责保护三星的屎山代码不被你发现。

Fintech is one of the few industries that still has a real moat.

ai made better ux, faster shipping and digital distribution cheap for everyone. What's left is the stuff you can't generate:

> licenses: @Wise spent a decade earning them, country by country
> two-sided networks: it took central banks (pix, upi) to dent @Visa and @Mastercard
> risk data: every bad loan teaches @Affirm's model something you'll never see
> switching costs: ripping stripe out of payments and accounting is a project nobody wants to own
> payment rails: direct access to local rails and settlement takes years (@Adyen)
> trust: people move their money once, then rarely again

In the 2010s fintechs won with better UX and faster shipping. AI is making that kind of edge cheap for everyone, while the boring parts (fraud models, compliance, reconciliation) get stronger the more data and licenses you already have.

text:
I am a Legal Content Strategist for Privacy Policy Revisions at Google. On October 16, 2026, I changed one sentence.

It used to read: “We don’t show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Photos.” It now reads: “We don’t show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos, unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads.” In the same edit I gave Photos its full brand name. The brand got two letters’ worth of respect, sorry, one word. The exception got eighteen.

I did not touch the 2017 promise. On June 23, 2017, Google Cloud’s chief executive, Diane Greene, wrote that “consumer Gmail content will not be used or scanned for any ads personalization after this change,” and that users “can remain confident that Google will keep privacy and security paramount as we continue to innovate.” The post is still up. Gmail’s own help page still says, today, “We will not scan or read your Gmail messages to show you ads.” All of it remains true, and I would defend every word. We never break a promise in my department. We leave it standing and build the exception on a different page, the way a city keeps the old church and puts the casino across the street.

My job is the hinge. I write the sentence that sits between helping you find something and helping an advertiser find you, and over the years I have learned that most of the work is done by small words. “A more personalized experience” means your correspondence helps choose the sales pitch. “Depending on your settings” means the default was decided before you arrived. “Not directly” means we put a summary between your email and the advertiser. “Unless you choose” means the exception needs your fingerprint, and the fingerprint is the whole design, because a promise can only be cancelled by the person it protects.

We issued “unless” a visitor badge. It entered the privacy policy carrying a single clause and left carrying the advertising department. Security thanked it for respecting the entrance procedure.

You should understand that none of this is new. Gmail launched on April 1, 2004, with a gigabyte of free storage, paid for by ads matched to the text of your email. People objected even then. In 2017 we stopped, partly to reassure the businesses paying for our enterprise email that their inboxes were safe. Now we offer an assistant that will help you find what you’ve kept, and to do that it needs to read what you’ve kept. In 2004 the free inbox came with ads attached. In 2026 the helpful assistant comes with the inbox attached. The Trojan horse also arrived as something useful, and was wheeled in by grateful people.

The feature is called Personal Intelligence. Our Search vice president described it as an experience that “feels uniquely yours by connecting the dots across your Google apps.” I helped choose which dots. When you connect Gmail and Photos, you are not connecting them to Search alone. One consent lets every Search service in, which includes Maps, Shopping, Flights, Hotels, Translate and News. You opened the door to find a receipt, and it turned out to be a hallway.

Google says your ads will not be based “directly” on your Gmail inbox or your Photos library. Search uses something else instead: “summaries, excerpts, generated media, and inferences.” I am proud of that list, because each item is one step removed from the thing itself. I am slightly less proud of the sentence our help page had to add for accuracy, which says that where an email or file is brief or particularly relevant, “the summary may just be the email or file.” We built a department called Summary, and on busy days it forwards the original. Our promise holds for as long as nobody asks what the summary contains.

The summaries are useful in other ways too. If you connect your apps, the help page explains, we may use the data to improve Google services “for everyone, including by training generative AI models,” and a subset of what AI Mode processes is read by human reviewers, including trained service providers. Once saved in Search Services History, the summaries, excerpts and inferences can remain after you disconnect the app or delete the original email or photo. You can delete the letter. The note we took about the letter has its own retention schedule.

In my test case, a woman with eleven years of photos connected Gmail to Search to find a mattress receipt. She found it in four seconds and disconnected the app, as our documentation recommends. The receipt was deleted from her inbox the next week. The inference stayed in Search Services History. It noted that the mattress was a twin, that the delivery address was new, and that the photos from the previous spring had two people in them and the ones from that autumn had one. We do not target ads on sensitive categories such as health, and advertisers never see your inbox. A divorce is not a category. It is a pattern, and patterns are what we sell.

The promise now comes with in-app purchases.

My restricted stock units vest in November. I spent most of yesterday on a new revision, deciding whether “may” or “can” sounds less like a decision. I chose “may.” It sounds like weather.

The 2017 promise is still on the blog, exactly where Diane Greene left it. I visit it sometimes. It reads beautifully. It is the advertising department’s permission slip.

One of the more challenging questions in designing this methodology was how to accomodate for firms with one big hit. 

On one hand, you want to reward investors who consistently make good decisions, and eliminate luck from the equation as much as possible. 

On the other hand, venture capital is an outlier business and tripling or quadrupling down on a major winner should also be rewarded. 

So, the ranking uses a "consistency-adjusted" approach where 2/3 of the weighting is given to the portfolio performance with the biggest outcome, and 1/3 is given to the performance without that outcome. 

With this in mind, there are a few firms that stand out: 

@gigafund and @Pelion_VP are effectively 100% associated with one company each (SpaceX and Cloudflare), and @Lowercase is also highly concentrated (98% Uber). They maintain a high rank because of their relatively low capital at risk. 

@usv, @GreylockVC, @sequoia, @IndexVentures and @khoslaventures are amongst the least concentrated, which speaks to a legacy of many large outcomes influencing their performance. They maintain a high rank despite their relatively high capital at risk. 

More: https://t.co/Ar1g1gw9NO
