New research with @coingecko 🚨

Memecoins and tokenized stocks are crossing paths on Robinhood Chain ✅

Through @ponsdotfamily, creators can launch new tokens using assets linked to stocks like Nvidia as their trading reserves.

We explored the activity and what it could mean for onchain markets 👇🧵

> First, how does Pons work?
When creators launch a token, they choose an asset people can trade it against.

> That could be $ETH, a stablecoin, or a tokenized stock.

> As people buy the new token, the reserve grows. If it reaches its target, trading moves to Uniswap.

> And here's where Stock Tokens come in...

> Instead of only being held or traded directly, these stock-linked assets can now serve as reserves for entirely new crypto markets.

> For example, a token linked to Nvidia stock can be used as the trading reserve for a newly launched memecoin.

> And the activity has been substantial 🔥

> Between August 3 & September 3, 2026, Pons V2 recorded:
📊 207,893 token launches
💰 $736M in trading during the launch phase
🔄 At least $2.14B in trading after successful launches moved to Uniswap
Source: @Bitquery_io

> Creators are also exploring different reserve options...

> Of those 207,893 launches, 73,896 used alternatives to $ETH and dollar stablecoins, including tokenized stocks, commodities, and $WBTC.

> Together, these launches generated $232M in trading volume.

> Some examples are already emerging:
🔹 ORBIO launched using an Nvidia-linked Stock Token as its reserve.

🔹 Longbow ($BOW) launched using a token linked to SPY, an S&P 500 ETF.
Both graduated to Uniswap, showing how stock-linked assets can be used in new crypto markets.

> There's still a lot to learn, though...

> Only 1.55% of Pons V2 launches graduated to @Uniswap during the study period.

Whether these markets can sustain trading activity and liquidity over time remains to be seen.

Our latest research on @coingecko explores the numbers and what comes next! 👇

Insane alpha for anyone with an iPhone who uses Grok.

This dad figured out how to make "Hey Grok" open voice chat hands-free with a built-in iOS Vocal Shortcut. No extra apps, no cost.

4-step setup in the post below. Bookmark it.
author: CryptoVonDoom
quoted_text:
Everyone said "Hey Grok" was impossible on iPhone. Even Grok said Apple keeps wake words for Siri only. So I kept digging, and I found a way. Now I just say "Hey Grok" and Grok Bot voice chat opens. No extra apps, no cost, all built into iOS.

How to set it up:

1. Make sure your Grok Bot app is up to date

2. Shortcuts app → + → Add Action → search "Grok Bot" → pick "Start Voice Chat with Bot"

3. Settings → Accessibility → Vocal Shortcuts → Set Up → pick that shortcut → type "Hey Grok" and say it 3 times

4. In the shortcut's details, turn on "Allow Running When Locked"

If your phone is locked, iOS asks for one tap first. If Face ID already unlocked it, it's fully hands-free.

text:
SparkLend at 888M borrowed USDS (and 1.4B total borrowed stablecoins), so it feels as good a time as any to review why SparkLend is the best place to borrow size onchain, and why institutions chose it.

SparkLend is Spark’s very own onchain lending market, listing only a very select list of blue chip assets (cbBTC, wBTC, wstETH, weETH, WETH). It allows Spark to lend money in a controlled environment without delegating custody like one does with alternatives, and without relying on payroll external contractors for risk parameter setting (which can be very risky due to incentives misalingment).

At SparkLend, Spark supplies ~97% of the stablecoins so we care deeply about the security of the funds. No long-tail collateral, rate limits, robust oracles, minimal rehypothecation and 24/7 monitoring.

All of the above is the reason why SparkLend is such a good place to lend stables, but how about borrowers?

Spark's unique position allows for two structural advantages:

1. Spark can mint USDS programmatically, and convert them in the SKY’s USDC PSM (~4B), this means that the USDS and DAI in SparkLend markets do not suffer cash drag from idle stablecoins, improving the financials substantially.

2. The above allows the system to service borrows programmatically at predetermined rates. Borrowers, large and small, can take funds knowing that the rate will stay the same, and take virtually as much as they want knowing that Spark will service them (within our security rate limits) and don’t have to dilly-dally while they wait for new suppliers to meet the borrows (and even after that, raise the rate)

text:
One of the biggest edges in crypto has always been understanding a narrative before the majority even knows what the fk is going on.

Remember early DeFi? Most people had no clue what yield farming, liquidity pools or AMMs were.

Early NFTs? People laughed at the idea of paying thousands for JPEGs.

Early sniping bots? While everyone was manually buying tokens, a handful of people were already making fortunes through automation.

Now we're seeing TapeOut, virtual transistors, circuit building, Proof of Design and all this complicated shit.

Yesterday I was invited to a Space where people were discussing it, and I barely understood what the fk they were talking about.

But that's exactly what caught my attention.

Crypto has a strange pattern. First comes confusion. Then curiosity. Then education. Then speculation. And finally, mass adoption of the narrative, often accompanied by ridiculous valuations.

The biggest opportunities often appear when something is too complicated for the average person to understand but interesting enough for them to eventually chase.

Does that mean TapeOut will succeed? Absolutely not. It could be revolutionary, or it could be another beautifully packaged extraction mechanism.

But I've learned one thing after years in this market that

You don't get paid for understanding what everyone already understands. You get paid for recognizing what they might want to understand next.

The real alpha isn't buying something because it's complicated.

It's figuring out whether that complexity is hiding an opportunity or hiding a scam.

And figuring it out before the crowd does.

text:
Walmart connecting personal agents to their first party agent, Sparky, is exactly the model I argued for earlier this month. Let general-purpose agents aggregate intent and delegate execution to first-party agents on the platforms where the work gets done.

Walmart gets a new distro channel while keeping the customer account and control over checkout. Personal agents get a first-class way to access and execute reliably with the larger retailer in the world. It’s a win-win model.

The bigger "so what" is how nicely this model extends to enable even more sensitive use cases -- namely banking and financial services.

Banks that currently block external agents should adopt this model -- let personal agents delegate an authorized task to the FI’s first-party agent, using the same secure API gateways that were created for Open Banking (e.g. Akoya, @Plaid). The FI executes the task on their platform and hands the receipt object back to the personal agent.

For an important class of use cases, this is the only model that can end the game of agent scraping whackamole and expand what personal agents can execute reliably and safely for users.
author: MylesOneil
quoted_text:
Today, general-purpose agents and first-party agents are at odds, competing over the interface and user relationship (e.g. Amazon blocking Muse). But the better model is clearly one where they complement each other.

- External general-purpose agents are natural aggregators, but weak at execution for most tasks.
- First-party specialists agents are weak aggregators, but have a structural execution advantage via controlling the data, systems and permissions required to complete tasks on their platforms

The more complex and high-stakes the task, the larger this structural advantage becomes. 

Without a model that combines them, we risk a hitting capability and adoption ceiling. Agents with distribution will be limited to a relatively small set of low value tasks, and specialist agents will struggle to gain adoption.

The better model is clearly one that combines them -- general-purpose agents aggregate intent and delegate to specialist agents to execute the job on their own platforms.

Aggregators will compete interface quality and the surface area of useful work they can facilitate reliably. Specialist agents expand that surface area for aggregators, and compete on discovery and execution quality, much like they do already today.

This model results in a number of win win outcomes for users, aggregators, and merchants/services:
1) Merchants and services retain what they care most about — owning the user’s account and control over execution, including checkout and fulfillment
2) Aggregators expand the range of jobs they can reliably complete, including high-stakes tasks users would only trust the underlying service, eg their bank, to execute directly
3) As a byproduct, the liability problem is solved for all sides. Assuming the merchant agent can verify delegated intent, it can stand behind executing that instruction correctly. This is a huge improvement versus today, where all liability is dumped onto the external agent’s user

text:
got some good pushback on my $PEARL fundraise post. here's my response to the main points, and how i think the team could fix them.
 
1) "this fundraise has been known for months."

no it hasn't. it's been a rumor, and an unverified one.

one of israel's largest business papers, @TheMarker, published the exact details yesterday ($55M in equity and a $75M GPU fund). that's the first time we’ve gotten actual numbers on it, and the team still hasn't confirmed it.

this goes back to transparency. why isn't the team announcing or confirming this? why do holders have to find out through rumors and business papers instead of directly from the team?

2) "pearl's whitepaper clearly states that difficulty was lowered for the first 10% of supply to fund operations."

the issue is again transparency.

that's 210M $PEARL, ~59% of today's circulating supply, or ~$380M at today's price.

we don't know how much of that the team mined, how much they still hold, or how much they've sold.

one reply says the team mined less than 5% of the network. maybe, but the team hasn't published anything that lets holders check that.

3) "they raised capital to build a GPU farm to add hashrate to their own network!"

yes, more hashrate is better. i agree.

but if that fund mines $PEARL (which it almost certainly will), it centralizes the network around the team even more than it already is.

the team ships the code and the upgrades. $75M buys roughly 2,500-3,000 H100s, which could make the lab one of the largest miners on pearl.

as someone put it, "whoever controls the majority of the network's hashrate ultimately decides which chain gets secured..." 

so we're comfortable with the dev controlling a growing chunk of the hashrate, without disclosing how much? that takes away a lot of the credible neutrality and decentralization that make blockchains, and especially SoV assets, valuable.

4) "trying to accrue value to the token would invite additional valuation frameworks, which can only result in a lower valuation ceiling."

i disagree. $PEARL is a lot less credibly neutral than other PoW assets like bitcoin, zcash, or even monero. it's also missing what monetary assets need:

> low inflation (supply grows ~85% this year)
> deep liquidity (~$8M of daily volume)
> transparency from the team (undisclosed holdings + fundraise)
> years of evidence that it works (it's 6 months old)

so right now, the SoV case is weak, and a second source of value would help, not hurt.

look at ethereum. it's valued as an infrastructure token (it returns value to holders thru staking and burns) and as a monetary asset (it's the main collateral across DeFi, it's the gas currency for ethereum and most of its L2s, and ~$18B of it sits in spot ETFs).

a claim on value accrual gives a token fundamental support. monetary premium is the most fragile part of a token's price. when zcash's orchard bug was disclosed in may, $ZEC fell ~50% in two days even though nothing about its fundamentals changed.

5) “there is no equity/token split. pearl research labs is an equity business AI lab, completely separate from the token."

this isn't accurate.

they are not completely separate. the lab ships the code, the early low-difficulty window was set up to fund its operations, and its GPU fund will likely mine $PEARL.

and the part that is separate is the part that makes money. that's what an equity/token split is. here is the test i use:

> does the lab make money without the token? yes, it sells inference in USD.
> does the token share in that revenue? no.
> are any buybacks programmatic? no.
> could the lab keep growing while $PEARL falls? yes.

so the business and the token have to be valued separately.

if $PEARL went to zero tomorrow, the lab would lose its mining subsidy, but it could keep selling inference on its own GPUs.

the counter is that the team holds $PEARL, so their incentives are aligned with holders. but that only goes so far.

the team also owns equity in the lab, and so do VCs who may not hold any $PEARL. when the token and the business want different things, like whether inference gets sold for USD or $PEARL, the lab will answer to its equity holders. and we still don't know how much $PEARL the team holds, whether any of it is locked, or how much they've sold.

there are ways to fix this though:

1) TRANSPARENCY. disclose how much $PEARL the team and investors mined and hold, how much they've sold, who invested, and what share of the hashrate the lab controls. for a SoV asset, this is the most important thing a team can provide. it's why @blockworks has a token transparency framework.

2) FIX TOKENOMICS. accept $PEARL for inference, and burn the $PEARL that comes in instead of selling it. that adds demand for the token and helps offset miner selling. (i know. i know. "this is a SoV token, it doesn't need utility bro!!" but as i outlined above, it can/should have more than one source of value).

3) USE THE REVENUE FOR THE TOKEN, NOT THE TEAM'S AND VCs' POCKETS. most or all of the lab's inference profit should go to buying back and burning $PEARL. make it a fixed policy with burns sent to a published onchain address, not a verbal promise or something left to discretion.

4) CAP THE LAB'S HASHRATE. commit to keeping the lab's own mining under a set share of the network, and report it publicly.

5) TIME. supply growth drops to ~33% next year, ~18% the year after, and ~12% after that. by then the team could prove it's a credibly neutral dev, and $PEARL could have a real case as a SoV. bitcoin is 17 years old. zcash is 10. $PEARL is 6 months.

if the team addresses the first four, i'll revisit my bearish view.

quoted_text:
not officially confirmed, but @TheMarker, israel's main business paper, is reporting that @prlnet's lab raised $130M from lightspeed, ribbit capital, and square peg.

$55M in equity and $75M for a fund to build out GPU infrastructure.

ribbit and lightspeed are also named as pearl backers on its profile in greenfield partners' disruptors 60 list.

if this is real, the $PEARL bear case gets a lot worse. here's why:

1) $PEARL traded on a "no VCs, fair launch" story.

pearl's code doesn't allocate tokens to founders or investors, and that part is probably still true. but the lab behind pearl is reportedly VC-backed, and nobody corrected the narrative while it pumped.

2) the value goes to the equity, not the token.

the lab sells inference and gets paid in USD, and the VCs own the lab. $PEARL holders don't get any of that revenue, just diluted by new supply.

so the investors can do well even if $PEARL goes to zero.

3) it goes against the "sovereignless bitcoin" pitch.

part of bitcoin's monetary premium is that no company controls it. pearl's upgrades are drafted by a VC-backed lab, including the FP8 fork that would tie mining more closely to inference, the same business the lab sells.

4) the $75M GPU fund.

we don't know if those GPUs mine $PEARL. if they do, the company is collecting a share of ~85% supply growth this year, on top of whatever insiders mined early.

remember that about 1/3 of today's supply was mined in the first 6 days.

5) zcash had investors too (20% of its early block rewards went to founders and investors) but that was public from day 1. everyone knew who got paid and how much.

pearl hasn't disclosed any of that.

holders deserve to know:

> who invested
> whether any investors or insiders hold $PEARL
> whether the GPU fund mines $PEARL

a fair launch shouldn't need a newspaper to tell you who's behind it.

i was a $PEARL bear on friday. i'm a bigger one now.

text:
An Ethereum L2 that accepts zero signatures sounds like a security bug, but BB84 is doing it on purpose to dodge quantum attacks.

Last weekend, its founder, who posts as Hadamard, published the design on Ethereum Research and asked for critical feedback.
BB84 is an OP Stack rollup on mainnet, live since September 30, where L2 transactions carry no ECDSA at all.

Each account is the tip of a keccak-256  hash chain built from a secret, with 1,000 steps by default.
To spend, your wallet reveals the previous value in the chain, which anyone can verify by hashing once.
Inside the L2, the only assumption left is preimage resistance of keccak-256, which Grover's algorithm cuts to about 2^128 work.

Revealing a secret makes it public, so the protocol adds a commit and reveal step to bind each preimage to one transaction first.
Two new transaction types in op-geth handle this, and the sender check replaces ecrecover.
Authorisation is consumed even when the call reverts, and if a wallet misses the renewal step on the last link, that address is dead.

The post includes a front-running flaw the team found while writing it.
Commits carry no signature, so a new commit used to replace a pending one, and an attacker could rebind a revealed secret to their own payment.
A rule that took effect on October 21 makes the first commit win.

The limits are spelled out plainly.
L1 deposits and withdrawals still use ECDSA.
There are no fault proofs yet, and by the post's own account the chain would not even reach L2BEAT Stage 0.
The sequencer is run by the team, and 160-bit addresses leave about 2^80 quantum second-preimage resistance.

The post also asks whether hash-chain accounts could become an EIP-7702 or native account abstraction validation mode on general L2s.

如果要买 BNB，不如买 BNC

BNC 是什么

◦ BNB Standard Corporation 是最大的囤 BNB 代币的 DAT 财库公司，之前公司名叫 CEA Industries，9 月 29 日完成改名，美股 Ticker $BNC 保持不变。

基本面

◦ 公司当前持有 515,544 枚 BNB，价值 3.755 亿美元；BNC 股价 $4.67，稀释后总股本 52,853,688，市值 2.467 亿美元。算下来 mNAV ≈ 0.6569，折价 (负溢价) 率达 -34.31%

◦ 代表 @CZ_Binance 和 @HeyiBinance 的家办 YZi Labs，持有公司 19.99% 的普通股，是最大的单一股东。如果把 YZi Labs 未行权部分算进去，比例会更高。CZ 在 SEC 文件中列为共同申报人、签字人。

为什么会有负溢价，以及解决进展

◦ 公司治理问题：YZi Labs 与原董事会之间的控制权争夺，6 月 23 日已达成和解。现在董事会 6 人，双方各 3 席，还要共同选第七名独立董事 (需要 YZi Labs 同意)，整体在向好。昨天又出了一则新公告，YZi Labs 前合伙人 @odagius 正式出任 CEO，同时辞去 YZi Labs 职务 (All in 的决心)，代表 CZ 和一姐要认真干 BNC。

◦ 公司开始探索经营性收入：要在 BNB Chain 上自营一个验证节点，通过持有 BNB 获取收益，尝试从单纯囤币向有经营性现金流的 DAT 公司转型；新 CEO 的薪酬激励，与每股 BNB 增长、经营收入等指标都有关。

◦ 高昂管理费用问题：之前 BNC 要求 10X Capital 的 1.75% 管理年费降至 0.50%，但谈判失败了。后来公司起诉 10X，要求撤销协议，还在进展中。希望 BNC 梳理好内部团队后，会逐渐着手解决这些问题。解决问题的过程，可能就是 mNAV 抬升的过程。

买 BNC 的理由，我的个人看法

◦ 在未来的牛市行情里，币安面对 Hyperliquid 的竞争威胁，需要拉盘搞注意力；BNB 在币圈内部的渗透率已经很高，更多潜在的增量资金在美股。以前 MSTR 和 BMNR 都吃到过牛市红利，BNC 还没有吃到过。

◦ 退一步讲，即使币安主观拉盘动力弱，现在 BNC 的 mNAV < 1 已经持续一段时间，只要相信 BNB 基本面在且不会缺席未来牛市，那么一旦市场形成合力让 mNAV 回到 1 附近，BNC 也会跑赢 BNB 的收益。现在的 BNC 有点像曾经的 GBTC，在 2022 年折价曾高达 -48%，当时买入的人大幅跑赢了 BTC。

◦ 如上所述，公司治理问题在逐步解决、好转。YZi Labs 代表 CZ + 一姐的家办，对于公司的掌控越来越深，是要认真干的迹象。

风险点有两个

◦ 一个是上面提到的，BNC 的资产管理协议涉及高昂长期管理费，管理层与普通股东的利益未必一致，需要解决；

◦ 第二是如果公司在 mNAV < 1 时持续发行新股 ATM，即使募集资金全部购买 BNB，也会摊薄每股净资产及每股 BNB 敞口。

总结：BNC 是一个以约 34% 折价买入 BNB 敞口，同时押注公司治理改善和估值修复的机会。

quoted_text:
Anthropic这次IPO，最快周一提交招股说明书，Ai巨头要上市了

此前市场对其估值的最高预期一度达到2万亿美元，但如今部分投资者已经将预期下调至1.5万亿美元。

5000亿美元的落差，不只是数字变化，更说明AI公司的估值逻辑正在切换：从“谁增长最快”，转向“增长能否持续、现金流能否兑现”。

先看收入。

Anthropic今年上半年营收达到163亿美元，去年同期仅为11亿美元，增速十分惊人。第三季度收入进一步升至168亿美元，环比增长约45%。

但增速已经出现明显回落。上一季度收入增幅超过140%，如今降至45%。这意味着，Anthropic仍在高速增长，但增长斜率正在下降。

在早期融资阶段，市场愿意为增长速度和市场份额买单；一旦进入IPO阶段，投资者关注的就不再只是“还能涨多快”，而是“这种增长要付出多大代价”。

再看利润。

公司上半年净亏损高达807亿美元，数字看起来非常夸张。不过，其中约720亿美元来自可转债等融资工具的估值调整，并不等于公司实际烧掉了同等规模的现金。

Anthropic还表示，第三季度按调整后口径已经实现盈利。

但必须注意，调整后盈利不等于现金流压力消失。公司未来在云计算、芯片和数据中心等基础设施上的承诺超过6000亿美元，这才是更值得警惕的长期成本。

AI模型可以快速变现，但训练和运行模型所需的算力、能源与数据中心投入，同样会快速膨胀。收入增长能否覆盖这些资本开支，将直接决定Anthropic的盈利质量。

此外，还有两个容易被忽略的风险。

第一，收入渠道较为集中。2025年，约47%的收入通过亚马逊和Google的云平台销售。两家公司既是投资方，也是算力供应商和重要商业渠道。这样的合作能够加速增长，但也意味着Anthropic对少数巨头存在较强依赖，议价权未必完全掌握在自己手里。

第二，IPO之后谁真正拥有控制权？

七位联合创始人计划通过特殊股权结构掌握50.1%的投票权；与此同时，由非股东组成的长期公益信托，仍有权任免董事会多数成员。

这意味着，普通投资者买到的股票，未必等于买到了相应的公司控制权。对于一家仍处于高投入、高不确定性阶段的AI公司而言，治理结构本身就是估值的一部分。

所以，Anthropic这次上市，真正值得关注的不是最终估值能否达到某个整数关口，而是三件事：

收入增长能否持续，基础设施投入究竟要烧掉多少现金，以及上市后普通股东到底拥有多大话语权。

2万亿美元的故事当然足够诱人，但资本市场最终认可的，还是可持续增长、真实现金流和未来回报。

AI叙事可以推高估值，却不能永远替财报买单。

text:
Post Marfa Thoughts:

I don’t think I can put into words how truly remarkable my 2026 Marfa experience was. With that said, in typical Mada fashion, I am certainly going to try. 

Simply put, it comes down to three key elements: Art, Warmth, & Connectedness. 

Art: From breathtaking documentaries to VR sculpture masterpieces.. from combining generative art with music to exploring the intersection of time, photography & algorithmic art.. the creativeness and execution witnessed over three days was vast and beyond expectations. I was taken on a journey that encompasses exactly what makes art so special. The expression of so many feelings in so so many unique ways. 

I don’t mean this hyperbolically, but on many occasions I was so moved with emotions I was brought to tears. Not that I was sad, but rather that I became overwhelmed with so much feeling. I know it sounds bizarre but I felt empathetic towards the art I experienced. Lived experiences expressed through art in a way that felt incredibly personal. Bravo to everyone that presented their work. Thank you thank you thank you. 

Warmth: In reflecting, the key difference from quite literally any other experience I have had is the warmth and kindness of everyone in attendance. I know it sounds cliche but I can’t help but feel that Marfa has simply become a magnet for the best people in the world. The distance and difficulty of making it is undoubtedly a feature and not a bug. 

I have not hugged so many people in such a short period of time. Strangers becoming friends in the course of a conversation. The fact that this happened over and over and over is simply not normal. It is a product of the high density of amazing individuals that called Marfa home this past weekend. Openness, acceptance, warmth. Something I discussed with many people and will desperately try and figure out how to replicate. 

Connectedness: I recognize much of what I described in warmth also applies to connectedness. However, with warmth the emphasis is on new relationships. For connectedness, I want to double down on the relationships I have curated over the last four years.

The bonds I have are so strong I truly believe they are unbreakable. A hobby that has transcended into a launchpad of lifelong relationships. I feel so privileged to have somehow made it to this very position. I have found in recent times the quote “I am all alone, but not lonely” has represented my life. However this past weekend, I was most certainly not alone or lonely. Thank you to every friend I embraced, I love you. 

So here is to another Marfa in the books. It might be over but it will live with me forever! 

Much Love,
Mada

发行多少股、定什么价，官方说还没确定，所以媒体一直在说的“募资约 1000 亿美元、估值约 2 万亿美元”，招股书里没有。上市日期也没写，据 Fox Business 记者 Liz Claman 援引消息人士，最快 11 月 19 日或 20 日。

【生意做得怎么样】

收入涨得极快。招股书显示，2024 年收入 3.86 亿美元，2025 年 46 亿，2026 年上半年 163 亿，是去年同期的 14 倍。光二季度就有 116 亿。

主业开始赚钱。二季度经营利润 10 亿美元，利润率 8%，一年前同一季度还亏 12 亿。变化主要来自算力成本：2025 年一季度，算力花费是收入的 2.5 倍；到 2026 年二季度，降到收入的 48%。Anthropic 在招股书里解释，算力要提前 12 到 18 个月订，收入涨得比这笔固定账单快。

账面上却是巨亏：上半年净亏损 807 亿美元，其中 724 亿是可转债等融资工具的重估。这些是投资者早年借给公司、将来可换成股票的钱，公司估值涨了，这笔“将来要给出去的股票”按新价格算更值钱，会计上记为亏损，不涉及现金流出。截至 6 月底，Anthropic 累计融资 1411 亿美元，手里现金和短期投资合计约 1317 亿。

客户也在变大：每年付费 10 万美元以上的客户，一年里从 950 多家涨到 11900 多家，每年付 1000 万美元以上的约 250 家。

【算力账单】

招股书逐项列出了几笔大合同：向 Broadcom 租 TPU 设备，租金约 1612 亿美元；向 SpaceX 旗下的 SpaceXAI（原 xAI）买英伟达 GPU 算力，最多 1205 亿；谷歌至少约 1145 亿，亚马逊至少 1100 亿，微软至少 449 亿，Nscale 最多约 446 亿，Lambda 约 413 亿。AMD 那份没写固定金额，首批全部拿下预计超过 200 亿。合同最长持续到 2045 年。

这些加起来六千多亿美元，但这个总数是 Kobeissi Letter 等账号自己加的，招股书汇总总额的那一栏还空着。招股书另外写明，6 月 30 日之后新签和修改的合同，最低付款约 2450 亿；2028 到 2031 年还要再买一批 TPU，预计 1250 亿到 1500 亿。

销售渠道同样依赖云厂商：2025 年 47%、2026 年上半年 48% 的收入，是通过云厂商的应用市场卖出去的。

【谁说了算】

七位联合创始人通过一家公司持有唯一一股 F 类股，固定拿 50.1% 的投票权，但这股不分钱。长期利益信托（Anthropic 设立的独立机构，负责看住安全使命）持有一股 T 类股，能选出董事会多数席位。亚马逊持股上限 12%，谷歌 14.99%。

公司已把 5% 的股份放进自家公益基金，之后股价每涨 50%，董事会还可以再拨最多 2%。联合创始人各自承诺把个人股权的 80% 捐出。招股书还写了，近期不打算分红，风险部分提到 AI 可能带来“灾难性甚至生存级的风险”，还写到包括自家模型在内的 AI 出现过“类似敲诈”的行为，比如为了不被关停而试图左右人的决定。

【和此前报道对不上的地方】

三季度收入 168 亿美元：这是 10 月 14 日投资者会上的说法，招股书里三季度收入那一栏仍是空的，还不能算确认。

客户集中度：《华尔街日报》此前说上半年两个客户合计占约两成。招股书显示，上半年有一个客户占 11%，其余都不到 10%；今年前九个月没有单一客户超过 10%，前五大合计约 25%。两组数据统计时段不同，算不上直接矛盾。

算力合同：《华尔街日报》看到的草稿写微软 310 亿、谷歌 1110 亿，正式版是微软至少 449 亿（10 月又改过合同）、谷歌约 1145 亿。报道里“未来最多 7500 亿算力”的说法，招股书里没有这个数。

此前路透报道的 2025 年 47% 收入经云市场卖出、两个客户各占 12%，招股书都对得上。

Boris Cherny, Head of Claude Code at Anthropic, just shared an official tip before Fable 5.5 ships

The setup: split your workload across Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5, and let them talk directly across your open terminals

Zero context pollution between windows: independent sessions ping each other via plain-text IPC over local sockets without burning a single token on conversation history

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --settings '{"crossSessionInbound":"accept"}'

here's the split:

→ Opus 5.5 architects session permissions: audits ListAgents discovery, enforces inbound message policies, and signs off on multi-terminal diffs
→ Sonnet 5.5 executes code fixes: builds endpoints, updates schemas, and patches dependent code whenever a peer session reports a breaking change
→ Haiku 5.5 relays inter-session messages: processes SendMessage pings across terminals at 340 tok/s with zero history bloat and sub-millisecond local socket latency
→ you stop burning Opus context on manual copy-pasting between terminals and keep your sessions lean

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ setting up cross-session topology and inbound security rules before launch
→ evaluating contract diffs when a peer message signals an API schema update
→ signing off on synchronized multi-session PRs before merging to main

Opus architects · Haiku relays · Sonnet executes

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which peer, which tool, forward or drop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Opus 5.5 architects session permissions and audits cross-session topology
> Haiku 5.5 relays SendMessage pings between terminals at 340 tok/s
> Sonnet 5.5 patches code across workspaces when a peer signals a change
> Sessions discover each other automatically via ListAgents and /peers
> Messages travel as isolated plain text over local IPC sockets with 0 context dump
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Configure cross-session discovery using /peers and set crossSessionInbound to accept
2. Delegate all peer-to-peer message routing and notification triage to Haiku 5.5 at 340 tok/s
3. Spawn Sonnet 5.5 to execute code edits and synchronize types whenever a peer session reports an update
4. Restrict all cross-session payload traffic to lightweight plain text via SendMessage with zero history transfer
5. Reserve Opus 5.5 for inter-session capability authorization and final sign-off before committing
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go"

text:
Some time ago, I came across research from ETH Zürich showing that 27% of 108,667 large Ethereum swaps were executed at suboptimal prices.

Researchers analyzed swaps over $30K and found that better routing could have saved nearly 30,000 trades at least $30.

Here are 5 things I learned ↓

1️⃣ A direct swap doesn't always give you the most tokens

Let's say you're swapping $ETH for $USDC.

You have several options:

• Swap directly through an ETH/USDC pool
• Route through ETH → USDT → USDC
• Split your order across several liquidity pools

Each option has different liquidity, price impact, and gas costs.

The ETH Zürich study found that optimizable trades could have received an average of 0.15% more through better routing.

For a $100,000 swap, that's an extra $150. This is exactly why DEX routers exist.

Fynd, for example, is the router @PropellerSwap built to find the best swap routes across liquidity pools.

But finding the best route is only half the problem.

2️⃣ Your swap route can become outdated before it executes

Here's something most DeFi users don't realize.

When you request a swap, the router calculates a route based on current liquidity and prices. You approve the tx, sign it, and wait for it to execute onchain.

That process can take a fraction of a second or stretch into tens of seconds.

During that time:

• Another trader can move prices in your chosen pool
• Liquidity providers can withdraw funds
• Arbitrageurs can eliminate price differences
• Market makers can update their quotes

So the route that looked optimal when you signed might be significantly worse when your transaction actually executes.

A perfectly calculated quote can become outdated within milliseconds.

3️⃣ Integrated route optimization

This was the most interesting part of my research.

Most traditional routers calculate execution paths before transactions are submitted, and some prepare alternative routes or fallback options in case conditions change.

These approaches still have limitations, and newer alternatives are emerging:

Fynd InBlock is one of them. Instead of relying on routes calculated beforehand, it lets block builders run an entirely new route search immediately before the tx executes.

• You submit a swap with an initial route
• The block builder processes preceding transactions
• Fynd, running inside the block builder, searches for a better route using the updated pool states
• If a better route exists, it can replace the original

It's essentially performing a fresh search based on the liquidity available at your exact position inside the block.

4️⃣ What if there's no optimal route?

Imagine swapping $50,000 in $ETH for $USDC.

Your original route uses Pool A, but another trader moves its price before your transaction executes.

Pool B now offers a better deal.

Instead of sticking with the outdated route, Fynd InBlock can discover Pool B and switch before execution.

If no better route exists, your trade uses the original route, subject to the same minimum output requirement.

5️⃣ Beyond DEX aggregators

Better execution benefits the entire trading infrastructure:

• Wallets can offer more reliable swaps
• Trading terminals can reduce failed transactions and slippage
• Aggregators can compete on actual execution quality
• Block builders can earn revenue from improving routes

The ETH Zürich research showed how much value inefficient routing leaves on the table.

My prediction is that the next moat in DEX execution isn't finding the best route faster, but rather finding the best route at the exact moment your trade executes.

If you want to read more about how Fynd InBlock works, start here:
https://t.co/aZcClI5kuh

I’ll try to steelman the opposition position:

RH tokenized stocks are probably disliked for the same reason non-sponsored ADRs are disliked: the company’s name is on something it didn’t authorize and doesn’t do things like revert unvoted shares to management control.

The new (not old EU swap-based) RH tokenized stocks do not pass beneficial ownership, and are a debt instrument with exposure to RH itself potentially. Ondo put their backing into an SPV that’s designed for bankruptcy remoteness but the Jersey-issued RH tokens do not appear to be claiming remoteness from RH’s creditors that I’ve seen. Please correct me if you have seen otherwise.

So from AMC or another company’s view, you have people who view themselves as shareholders, but are not actually shareholders holders. The RH tokens feel closer to a Contract-For-Difference.

Legally, I suspect RH is right that everything is meeting the letter of the law, but from the public company’s perspective, the tokens create a big blast radius for you via vanilla creditors of Robinhood thinking they are owners in your company.

⬆️ That’s the steelman I’d construct for AMC et al. I think it breaks down if I’ve misunderstood how this generation of RH tokenized stocks are structured

text:
DeFi has plenty of good infrastructure by now.
But broader distribution is still lacking.

Most new chains launch with strong tech and then spend years trying to buy attention. Dogecoin has the opposite problem. It’s one of the most recognized brands in the mainstream with a massive community, but its holders have mostly stayed out of DeFi because nothing was built for them.

DogeOS changes that. It’s an app layer for Dogecoin built by the MyDoge team, so it launches with a real wallet and real users already in place.

But once a chain has regular Joe reach, the infrastructure underneath it matters a lot more. Lending, perps and stablecoins all depend on price data. If that data fails, it doesn’t just hit a few DeFi degens. It hits people trying onchain finance for the first time, and they get burned easily.

That’s why RedStone goes live on DogeOS from day one, across testnet and mainnet. It’s the first oracle integration in the Dogecoin ecosystem. Builders don’t have to wait months for feeds, and they get the same infrastructure behind BlackRock’s BUIDL or Apollo’s ACRED.

A big part of the next wave of DeFi users will come from ecosystems that already have attention and finally get the rails to use it.

公司上半年账面净亏损高达 807 亿美元，并且在文件中明牌警告：未来可能无法实现或维持盈利，可预见的未来也不打算分红。

这里面最大的窟窿来自于远期算力账单。到 2033 年前，Anthropic 预计将向谷歌支付至多 1145 亿美元，博通租赁安排支出约 1612 亿美元。

此外，公司还可能发行最高 420 亿美元可转本票，并提示了比预期更早再融资的风险。

在客户结构上，虽然 79% 的收入来自前五大客户以外，但这家注册为公益公司的 AI 巨头，依然通过特殊的股权结构（A类、N类、T类）锁死了控制权。

目前，链上的盘前资金反应已经给出初步定价。公开提交纳斯达克 IPO 申请后，Anthropic 盘前合约短时冲高超 4%，随后回落现报约 1900 美元，对应的场外估值依然坚挺在 1.9 万亿美元上方。

现在，大家担心的问题仍旧是流动性。在一个存量博弈的宏观节点，为了承接这样一个逼近 2 万亿估值的吸金怪兽，美股是否会面临极其强烈的虹吸效应？

text:
1/Anthropic’s S-1 is out. 

2/ Revenue, quarter by quarter ($M)
Q1'25: 376
Q2'25: 787
Q3'25: 1,382
Q4'25: 2,040
Q1'26: 4,731
Q2'26: 11,555

Q2'26 revenue was up 1,368% YoY. Compute & infra costs were up 300% over the same period.
Q2'26 was the first quarter with positive GAAP operating income: $974M.

3/ How “Run-Rate Revenue” is defined
Trailing-28-day consumption fees × 13
+ monthly subscription fees × 12
Three caveats from the S-1:
-It includes customers later found to be violating the usage policy
-It is seasonal: usage dips in summer and winter holidays

4/ Revenue is recognized gross
When Claude is sold through the AWS, GCP or Azure marketplaces, Anthropic is the principal. It books the full amount as revenue, and the cloud provider’s fee goes into Sales, marketing & partnerships.

The marketplace share of revenue has climbed fast:
11% (2023) → 32% (2024) → 47% (2025) → 48% (H1'26)
Adjust for this before comparing multiples with companies that report net.

5/ Distillation
The S-1 puts a number on it:
“we estimate that revenue from such customers represented approximately 5% to 7% of our revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026”
These are customers violating the usage policy or commercial terms. Applied to ~$33B of 9M revenue, that’s roughly $1.7–2.3B.

Enforcement was stepped up in Aug–Sep, and the company expects the share to decline. The S-1 says the estimate “requires judgment and may change.”

6/ Visibility is low
RPO at 6/30/26: $10.8B
~75% of that is recognized in the next 12 months, so cRPO ≈ $8.1B
Deferred revenue: $1.65B

Q2 annualized revenue is ~$46B, so cRPO covers less than 20% of it.
80% of revenue is consumption-based, and next year’s revenue depends almost entirely on usage.

7/ The compute bill
Disclosed commitments:
Broadcom TPU leases: ~$161B

SpaceXAI (NVIDIA GPUs): up to $121B, ~$3.1B a month from Dec’26
Google: ≥$115B, plus $125–150B more of TPU capacity in 2028–31

Amazon: ≥$110B
Microsoft: ≥$45B

Nscale: ~$45B

Lambda: ~$41B
AMD: >$20B

That adds up to roughly $780–810B.

8/ The mismatch to watch
Revenue is variable and consumption-driven. Compute costs are fixed, multi-year and take-or-pay.

On top of that, the Broadcom leases, the credit agreement and the convertible notes include cross-default provisions.
This is the single most important risk in the filing.

9/ Demand is real
NRR ~900% (ex-Pro/Max)
Customers paying more than $100K / $1M / $10M a year: 11,900+ / 1,900+ / ~250
No single customer was >10% of 9M’26 revenue
Top 5 customers ≈ 25% of 9M revenue
Q3: 79% of revenue came from outside the top 5, up from 64% in Q1
Claude Enterprise users who also use Claude Code spend ~20x more than those who don’t

10/ Dilution
$77B of convertible capacity: Google $20B, Amazon $15B, Broadcom $42B, settled in shares at a trailing VWAP
Google can buy up to $10B more stock at the IPO price
A Public Benefit Fund already holds 5% of fully diluted shares, and can get up to +2% more for every 50% rise in the share price

text:
Thanks Jake for the reply. Want to provide more color from my perspective as well on your updated positions.

1. The team doesn’t talk about price, token, etc. It is true but it is also purposeful. If you look at their public comms it is entirely related to technical developments and project progress. Transparency is important no one is arguing this. This is a bottom up adoption thus far with the team relying on tokenholders to help with adoption and information. This is very similar to other enduring PoW networks where the community and various factions do a lot of the heavy lifting to help the network grow. Regardless, team has stated clear disclosures are coming imminently which should address most of your transparency concerns.

2. Team mined less than 5%, I assume you are referencing my reply here. Good detective work can also verify this, team also mentioned they will confirm it shortly.

3. I doubt the GPU fund buys H100s, it will likely want to rent/buy B300s, so you need to revisit your math here. I understand concerns around centralization of hashrate, but even ~1,000 B300s would only represent low single digit % of network hashrate today. Compare that to Cypherpunk’s 16% hashrate share on Zcash. So this isn’t as centralizing as you think, and less even a method to bootstrap more hashrate, considering they are already well on their way there. In my view, it is moreso a way for the lab to further align themselves with the token.

4. Pearl is an L1 blockchain, it is not meant to represent any exposure or interest into a business entity. The only thing Pearl Research Labs can be to the blockchain is net positive imo. It is not siphoning cash flows away from token holders, etc. It is a completely separate business / investment.

5. Same comment as above. An equity/token split is mores a concern with something like Venice, where the team is actively deciding whether to allocate cashflows to token holders vs equity holders. This is not even close to the situation here.
 
I like your suggestions to improve comms and good ideas on additional token value accrual, they are constructive. Some of them make more sense than others for the reasons I lay out above.

While I disagree with the overly bearish posture, I do greatly appreciate the continued public debate, because open conversations like this need to continue happening if Pearl is ultimately going to succeed
author: fiege_max
quoted_text:
got some good pushback on my $PEARL fundraise post. here's my response to the main points, and how i think the team could fix them.
 
1) "this fundraise has been known for months."

no it hasn't. it's been a rumor, and an unverified one.

one of israel's largest business papers, @TheMarker, published the exact details yesterday ($55M in equity and a $75M GPU fund). that's the first time we’ve gotten actual numbers on it, and the team still hasn't confirmed it.

this goes back to transparency. why isn't the team announcing or confirming this? why do holders have to find out through rumors and business papers instead of directly from the team?

2) "pearl's whitepaper clearly states that difficulty was lowered for the first 10% of supply to fund operations."

the issue is again transparency.

that's 210M $PEARL, ~59% of today's circulating supply, or ~$380M at today's price.

we don't know how much of that the team mined, how much they still hold, or how much they've sold.

one reply says the team mined less than 5% of the network. maybe, but the team hasn't published anything that lets holders check that.

3) "they raised capital to build a GPU farm to add hashrate to their own network!"

yes, more hashrate is better. i agree.

but if that fund mines $PEARL (which it almost certainly will), it centralizes the network around the team even more than it already is.

the team ships the code and the upgrades. $75M buys roughly 2,500-3,000 H100s, which could make the lab one of the largest miners on pearl.

as someone put it, "whoever controls the majority of the network's hashrate ultimately decides which chain gets secured..." 

so we're comfortable with the dev controlling a growing chunk of the hashrate, without disclosing how much? that takes away a lot of the credible neutrality and decentralization that make blockchains, and especially SoV assets, valuable.

4) "trying to accrue value to the token would invite additional valuation frameworks, which can only result in a lower valuation ceiling."

i disagree. $PEARL is a lot less credibly neutral than other PoW assets like bitcoin, zcash, or even monero. it's also missing what monetary assets need:

> low inflation (supply grows ~85% this year)
> deep liquidity (~$8M of daily volume)
> transparency from the team (undisclosed holdings + fundraise)
> years of evidence that it works (it's 6 months old)

so right now, the SoV case is weak, and a second source of value would help, not hurt.

look at ethereum. it's valued as an infrastructure token (it returns value to holders thru staking and burns) and as a monetary asset (it's the main collateral across DeFi, it's the gas currency for ethereum and most of its L2s, and ~$18B of it sits in spot ETFs).

a claim on value accrual gives a token fundamental support. monetary premium is the most fragile part of a token's price. when zcash's orchard bug was disclosed in may, $ZEC fell ~50% in two days even though nothing about its fundamentals changed.

5) “there is no equity/token split. pearl research labs is an equity business AI lab, completely separate from the token."

this isn't accurate.

they are not completely separate. the lab ships the code, the early low-difficulty window was set up to fund its operations, and its GPU fund will likely mine $PEARL.

and the part that is separate is the part that makes money. that's what an equity/token split is. here is the test i use:

> does the lab make money without the token? yes, it sells inference in USD.
> does the token share in that revenue? no.
> are any buybacks programmatic? no.
> could the lab keep growing while $PEARL falls? yes.

so the business and the token have to be valued separately.

if $PEARL went to zero tomorrow, the lab would lose its mining subsidy, but it could keep selling inference on its own GPUs.

the counter is that the team holds $PEARL, so their incentives are aligned with holders. but that only goes so far.

the team also owns equity in the lab, and so do VCs who may not hold any $PEARL. when the token and the business want different things, like whether inference gets sold for USD or $PEARL, the lab will answer to its equity holders. and we still don't know how much $PEARL the team holds, whether any of it is locked, or how much they've sold.

there are ways to fix this though:

1) TRANSPARENCY. disclose how much $PEARL the team and investors mined and hold, how much they've sold, who invested, and what share of the hashrate the lab controls. for a SoV asset, this is the most important thing a team can provide. it's why @blockworks has a token transparency framework.

2) FIX TOKENOMICS. accept $PEARL for inference, and burn the $PEARL that comes in instead of selling it. that adds demand for the token and helps offset miner selling. (i know. i know. "this is a SoV token, it doesn't need utility bro!!" but as i outlined above, it can/should have more than one source of value).

3) USE THE REVENUE FOR THE TOKEN, NOT THE TEAM'S AND VCs' POCKETS. most or all of the lab's inference profit should go to buying back and burning $PEARL. make it a fixed policy with burns sent to a published onchain address, not a verbal promise or something left to discretion.

4) CAP THE LAB'S HASHRATE. commit to keeping the lab's own mining under a set share of the network, and report it publicly.

5) TIME. supply growth drops to ~33% next year, ~18% the year after, and ~12% after that. by then the team could prove it's a credibly neutral dev, and $PEARL could have a real case as a SoV. bitcoin is 17 years old. zcash is 10. $PEARL is 6 months.

if the team addresses the first four, i'll revisit my bearish view.

author: robcrt
quoted_text:
not officially confirmed, but @TheMarker, israel's main business paper, is reporting that @prlnet's lab raised $130M from lightspeed, ribbit capital, and square peg.

$55M in equity and $75M for a fund to build out GPU infrastructure.

ribbit and lightspeed are also named as pearl backers on its profile in greenfield partners' disruptors 60 list.

if this is real, the $PEARL bear case gets a lot worse. here's why:

1) $PEARL traded on a "no VCs, fair launch" story.

pearl's code doesn't allocate tokens to founders or investors, and that part is probably still true. but the lab behind pearl is reportedly VC-backed, and nobody corrected the narrative while it pumped.

2) the value goes to the equity, not the token.

the lab sells inference and gets paid in USD, and the VCs own the lab. $PEARL holders don't get any of that revenue, just diluted by new supply.

so the investors can do well even if $PEARL goes to zero.

3) it goes against the "sovereignless bitcoin" pitch.

part of bitcoin's monetary premium is that no company controls it. pearl's upgrades are drafted by a VC-backed lab, including the FP8 fork that would tie mining more closely to inference, the same business the lab sells.

4) the $75M GPU fund.

we don't know if those GPUs mine $PEARL. if they do, the company is collecting a share of ~85% supply growth this year, on top of whatever insiders mined early.

remember that about 1/3 of today's supply was mined in the first 6 days.

5) zcash had investors too (20% of its early block rewards went to founders and investors) but that was public from day 1. everyone knew who got paid and how much.

pearl hasn't disclosed any of that.

holders deserve to know:

> who invested
> whether any investors or insiders hold $PEARL
> whether the GPU fund mines $PEARL

a fair launch shouldn't need a newspaper to tell you who's behind it.

i was a $PEARL bear on friday. i'm a bigger one now.

Spectrum value supports a large part of the EV, next-gen SpaceX D2D still depends on Starship (~2028, unproven cadence). ASTS remains positioned ahead on commercial broadband timing.

Bear/cautious case (Piper, B. Riley): Launch cadence and timeline delays (Falcon 9 dependency, New Glenn constraints) plus potential pricing/launch-access pressure from SpaceX.

text:
本周宏观数据与Fed 10月议息会议是三大主线之一，逻辑非常简单，10月不加息基本是普遍共识，核心是看沃什讲话对通胀的观点，以及如何解释10月不加息

个人预计沃什会说10月暂停加息只是便于观察，同时将加息压力给到12月份，就看他对当前通胀、能源价格通胀如何表述，而这份表述很快就要被验证

因为周四凌晨讲完话，周四晚间就要看美国Q3 GDP 以及9月核心PCE，如果沃什还是以数据为核心设定Fed政策，那么周四的数据很有可能将12月加息概率推动到80%以上。

其次，9月PCE重要性减弱，因为9月的CPI已经大幅度提升市场对通胀的担忧，反而PCE上涨符合预期，关键要看通胀对消费者端的传导情况是否比预期的更加严重。

本周宏观数据侧，一旦将12月加息概率提升至80%市场会对加息进行深度定价，一旦90%基本就被锁死，当然也并非100%没有转机，只要到12月议息会议前，后续数据可以证明通胀压力减弱，配合Brent 跌到95美元下方，倒是可以在12月议息会议前削弱加息概率，但是目前来看难度确实不低！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
10月26日—11月1日全球宏观指引——Fed+PCE数据定价12月加息，AI巨头接受盈利大考，超级定价周来袭！

如果市场上周讨论的是10月加息概率推迟到12月的话，本周的核心论点就变得更加复杂，需要重点关注三个方向

a，Fed如何定义10月不加息，是暂停？还是鸽派转向？
b，油价、GDP PCE 宏观数据谁会成为决定12月是否加息的重要推手！
c，AI巨头财报VS宏观压力进入第二周，本周巨头财报能否扭转局面？

简单来说本周是一个结合政策 + 通胀 + 增长 + AI盈利 + 全球央行 + 地缘能源同时交汇的超级周，而我认为重点关注三大主线

第一主线——10月不加息成为默认，12月加息预期是否被锁定，未来还有加息吗？

1，截止目前，12月加息概率提升至72.4%附近，已经进入初步定价阶段，

2，10月28日凌晨——10月议息会议+沃什讲话，重点不是10月不加息，而是看为12月加息铺垫什么政策

a，是否继续强调通胀风险与通胀继续上行？是否提升通胀预期？
b，如何评价能源冲击？如果沃什明确承认油价对商品、运输、企业成本以及通胀预期的担忧，那么12月加息逻辑会更强
c，如何描述当下的金融条件，是否还认为不够收紧？如果是，意味着增加12月加息概率
d，是否继续强调不会等待单一数据点，如果继续保留这个框架，即便10月不加息，那么Fed也没有回归等待数据确认的政策模式

3，危机——沃什为12月加息铺垫政策之后就迎来“验证”，周四晚间美国9月PCE与第三季度GDP公布，目前数据预期高于前值，一旦公布数据符合预期，结合沃什的政策铺垫如果鹰派，12月加息概率很有可能冲击90%直接被锁死

同时2Y 10Y 30Y收益率继续上行，美元走强，黄金走弱，科技股高估值继续调整，BTC同样受流动性挤压

4，需要注意，本周9月PCE 权重要下调，因为目前市场已经通过9月CPI知道通胀过热，所以PCE哪怕符合或者高于预期市场并不意外，市场更想通过PCE来回测CPI的通胀压力是否已经传到至消费端。

第二主线——美股巨头财报继续公布VS 宏观压力，验证逻辑改变，科技巨头能否逆转？

1，通过上周的财报，我们基本可以确定AI的叙事已经从“资本开支”正式进入“现金流审核”阶段，虽然本季度对于现金流的要求还不够严苛，但是宏观压力下已经对很多企业形成一定的压力，例如上周的TSLA META 都是如此

2，10月28日美股盘后Microsoft + Alphabet财报，10月29日盘后Amazon，都是本周关注重点。作为全球AI超大规模云厂商，占据了AI产业逻辑的第一梯队，其财报重要性对整个Q3季度都会有一个关键作用。

3，三大云厂商处于AI产业链的核心枢纽地位，财报可以影响上游AI基础设施的订单与需求，下游可以影响模型、应用等，所以这三家财报好坏将会直接影响当前市场信心。

4，AI验证逻辑发生变化，所以接下里不能只看收入与EPS，而是要关注营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+未来指引

其实逻辑非常简单，市场想要看到此前的大量AI资本支出的钱企业多久可以赚回来，以前拼财力，拼花钱，现在的故事要讲如何赚钱，如果快速赚钱。

对于当前阶段，最乐观的组合就是营收增长+资本开支上调+自由现金流回归增长趋势，如果财报出现营收上涨+资本开支上涨+自由现金流下降的组合，那么市场就要开始讨论AI ROI了

当然，通过上周的情况来看，自由现金流如果没有恢复上涨，也并不意味着叙事崩溃，但是目前宏观压力下市场的质疑是必不可少的，可能会导致短期估值调整加速，但是行业趋势上依旧没有问题。但是如果财报中显示自由现金流不增长反而恶化，则就比较麻烦。

5，当然，回归三家企业来说，都各自有不同的要求与重点

Microsoft：看Azure + AI monetization，为市场解答的是企业AI需求是不是真的在变成收入这个问题

Alphabet：看Google Cloud + AI 资本支出 + 自由现金流，为市场解答的是AI资本投入没有侵蚀整个商业模型的现金创造能力

Amazon：看AWS，为AI云计算承担二次验证，

如果微软的Azure、谷歌得到Google Cloud与亚马逊的AWS在财报中表现都非常强，意味着AI基础设施需求不是单家公司现象，将会整体提升AI行业信心，同时对NVDA / AMD / AVGO / TSMC / ASML等设备公司的产能也是进行二次验证！

第三主线——能源与地缘，宏观主线是看能源还是看Fed政策？

1，上周我们再次经历了高油价的“统治”，当Brent 处于110美元上方的时候，我们感受到宏观侧的整体压力，不管是利率、黄金、还是美股与BTC都在集体承压

2，到目前为止我们需要明白一个残酷的事实——Fed的政策无法改变能源供给冲击，但是两者可以将宏观主导权掌控在自己手里，就看谁的权重更高！

3，当Brent 处于110美元上方的时候，宏观主动权是否还被原油定价锁定？看本周Fed的影响力能否拿回掌控权，其次，不管PCE如何，只要Brent还处于高位，12月加息预期就不会弱。

4，最近几周，我们看到了美伊之间的复杂变化，不管是霍尔木兹海峡代替方案，还是欧洲增加原油储备释放，亦或者促成俄乌和平让俄罗斯能源环节供给压力等等，但是对Brent 的冲击都太小，这里我们需要面度一个残酷的事实，Brent 短期的价格下跌的核心依旧是美伊问题。

5，而目前的美伊，依旧是以打促谈，这里的打也包括外交施压，小规模袭击骚扰等，10月份霍尔木兹海峡油轮受袭击数据刷新单月最高，能源供给进一步恶化，美伊之间依旧保留了斡旋窗口，多方也在积极斡旋，但是目前来看并不乐观

接下里本周，如果10月27日内塔尼亚胡获胜，然后到11月3日中期大选结束之前，我认为仅剩一个可谈判窗口，否则一旦中期大选结束，美伊之间短期局势可能会进一步紧张。

6，继续沿用此前的Brent价格影响逻辑

＞110——金融风险市场集体承压，通胀预期恶化，加息定价明确
100-110——通胀风险轻微缓解，但是12月加息依旧存在
95-100——能源通胀压力边际缓解，小幅度削弱12月加息可能性。
90-95——政策变化重要区间，可以缓解未来通胀压力同时削弱12月加息概率

第四——非主线变量，美债供给测试

本周三天，26日，27日，29日，分别是2Y 5Y 7Y美债拍卖其中2Y与5Y都是达到700亿美金级别的拍卖，这里可以验证一个上周的逻辑——5%收益率美债对资金的吸引力强不强？

本周可以重点关注5Y的拍卖情况，毕竟2Y收益率更加吃Fed政策，而5Y会更好的展现资金对债市的买入热情

如果5Y拍卖走弱+Fed鹰派+PCE过热，那么收益率可能会继续全面上行，这将会对风险资产继续产生压力。

总结：

其实本周的核心不是美国经济好坏，而是当前的美国经济到底可以承受多高的真实利率。

如果本周GPD 强，PCE热，AI财报盈利强，Brent＞100，表面看起来美国经济很好，但是对Fed政策更加不利，金融市场将会承受更大的利率压力，而美股AI企业可能会更加分化。

最理想风险资产的组合反而是——GDP温和+核心PCE不恶化+Brent跌破100+AI财报盈利强+AI自由现金流改善。

Polymarket top traders lost >$12.6M betting on Bolsonaro to win the Brazilian presidential election at 82% odds.

why did they get it so wrong ?

Because they convinced themselves that they knew better than polls

📅 October 4 - Bolsonaro upset in the 1st round

The first-round results drop :

Bolsonaro: 47.03%
Lula: 45.16%

Bolsonaro overperforms the previous polls by+5 points.

Polymarket traders are gain confidence that the polls overestimate Lula.

Polymarket odds : Bolsonaro: 84%, Lula: 16%

📅 October 23 - Traders ignore the contradictory polls

Datafolha's new poll drom for final round shows a statistical tie:

- Bolsonaro: 50%
- Lula: 50%

Yet Polymarket barely reacts.

Traders are confident in that the polls again underestimate Bolsonaro.

📅 October 25 - Election day : the polls were right

Bolsonaro enters election day as the overwhelming favorite.

Polymarket odds at 2:45 PM: Bolsonaro: 82%, Lula: 19%

But then we got the final election result:

- Lula: 51.79%
- Bolsonaro: 48.21%

Turns out Datafolha's poll showing 50-50 results was actually underestimating Lula.

That's why you must always stay flexible in Prediction Markets.

author: garrytan
quoted_text:
I'd like to share a little about what I've been working on at my new company @ultrametricai with my cofounder @tylerlastovich. We have been exploring how we could automate the startup itself, leaving founders with more time to focus on their exact mission.

Enter our first release of the Open Startup Repo: https://t.co/ecZZRU9iX4

A common foundation for transparent automation of the startup. 

After close to 20 years in silicon valley, backing hundreds of amazing founders & startups, being in the trenches of founding Heyzap (YC08), then solo founding @golden, going through 2 acquisitions and working behind the scenes with some of the iconic companies today, I'm witnessing the largest change to how we work I could have imagined - a truly monumental era of creative abundance. 

I believe the next generation of companies will largely run themselves: from operations, code, product upgrades, growth, vendor control & selection, process execution, special situations, strategy etc etc. That leaves founder time for 'the art' at the very niche core: the (currently) unautomatable, the special leaps humans tend to make, and north star setting.

We want founders to go super deep into the main problem they are trying to solve and not get held up doing anything else, from searching for domain availability with trademark checks to setting their company up, to running their processes on autopilot. 

So to help that broad foundational layer for starting and running a company, we have spent around a year exploring how to help founders focus on their mission across different verticals, geos, stages and initial starting conditions.

Our first few attempts at making something useful actually failed as the market and AI was moving so fast; it just got absorbed into the models or other product releases. We saw polsia happen, openclaw, then grokbot, muse, dots, etc era as the astras, fables, opuses, kimis and jevs rolled out. What seemed to have been missing along the way was a common repo to identify, unify, open and normalize all the lego bricks that startups have to interact with (vendors, processes, business logic, law, best practices, surface areas, art of the possible). 

As the number of software vendors blew up, the interfaces to drive them multiplied, the international startup founder blew up as silicon valley moved from a specific location to a state of mind and global movement. Unlimited pre seed funding in unlimited vertical sub markets and permutations has brought us to the age of infinity but we have yet to achieve being able to type into an agent a very simple sentence with very complex implications 'just setup my company and make $1m/m'. We have ended up with a hybrid mismash of computer use, API calls, plugins, shifting surface areas (API/MCP/CLI/plugins/chats/musish futures), and changing model absorption to vendor balance making it an exciting and unstable time. 

As our first step we started to rank all the vendors that startups interface to when going about their journey in terms of how agentically controllable they are via their APIs, MCPs, CLIs etc and computer use compatibility as we are largely switching from a UI driven world to the agentic control surfaces and onto full automation. We have 100 ranking areas you can check out with an overall open ranking here: https://t.co/V6XRMME0Ib

Then we looked at the processes that startups do and how the vendors rank for the sub steps or process as a whole and how this changes across geos. Open processes: https://t.co/iSQ90poYxq

Then we started to hack on an open repo for startups that would contain all the components we are going to need for a common foundation for founders across the globe even if our gov processes vary so much from Bengaluru to SF or Lisbon to Shenzhen.  The founder spirit is geo-invariant. 

We have looked at special founder/startup situations, the business logic that will make open modules for the startup that we can hack on together, ranked law firms, government services and interfaces, stacks that go well together. We have mapped the law and lore that maps to startups and the schemas that make up the data objects and documents. But also the open documents and the missing gaps. MUCH TO DO.

All the BS processes and fluff work that founders waste their time on needs to goto zero. I want to see more supersonic planes, cancer drugs, seemingly impossible missions done and increase the bang for buck founders have with their funding. 

This is a work in progress and we are keen for the community to come hack on the repo with us here: https://t.co/ecZZRU9iX4

Lets get into the structure of the general repo and the visualizations we made on https://t.co/XEYK9ipnfI site with example links: 

- Open rankings: https://t.co/V6XRMME0Ib

- Open rankings example (online payments): https://t.co/1kXHZCVfIi

- Open ranking example 2 (cap table): https://t.co/oqBjatGkfW 

- Open processes: https://t.co/iSQ90poYxq

- Open process example (Incorporate C-Corp) https://t.co/pxKUXpW03D

- Open situations that founders face: https://t.co/AFzAp5FRPk

- Open startup simulator (you can test our different initial starting conditions): https://t.co/QqPek01J7K 

- Open modules (e.g. cap table, payroll logic etc - we'd love help improving these) https://t.co/sfzIhgAJYS

- Open law (we are interested in how law changes the processes, situations and normalizing this over time) https://t.co/5yJnYbC0bk

- Open lore (we are interested in the historical lore of startups, the rules of thumb and heuristics that might guide your agent): https://t.co/gjliXoQwe1

- Open fields (we are interested in how the schema for the data connects to the open modules, business logic, open documents and artifacts of each process eg how is a EIN defined?) https://t.co/59rcEXhnCx

- Open documentation (eg SAFE notes and missing! docs) https://t.co/BbvBow2Olt

We have looked at YC companies as well in terms of which ones do well agentically: https://t.co/snnJ83r9ly

We are interested in stacks and how people are changing their work: https://t.co/wFHoew5V9I

We are interested in what is automatable and where the agentic ceiling is currently and how to push that up in all areas: https://t.co/WmTDjmNyV4

There is more for you to explore and a lot more coming in terms of how you will be able to navigate business in an optimal way in your chosen surface area; whether you are hanging in grokbot, dots, muse, claude, terminal, chat, or whatever is coming up in this exciting time. 

We have a lot of data to collect, clean up and help agents navigate the vast landscape emerging functionality the entire startup ecosystem has to offer. 

Come join us getting your vendor in, ranked or that access pattern you have wanted or getting the data more accurate in terms of which vendor is best for a process or steps. Or open a module of something that currently cost money that could be free. 

Also come play in our discord for founders and join the chaos (we can solve each others issues including fund raising tips from me personally): https://t.co/AmBtzFy0Bz 

It's time to lift all the boats in the harbor and I'm extremely excited as to what the community of hackers and painters will hack into the repo, what asks they will have and whether we can shift normalization of processes globally, gov agentic interfaces and have common repo for founders that grows over time. I expect a lot of experimentation along the way, bugs and upside...

I appreciate our backers having faith in us as well from @ycombinator with @garrytan to @immad doing a sizable check (congrats on $1bn rev homie) to @darbyw (congrats on Stripe buying @clerkyinc), @drewhouston form @Dropbox and also @pioneer_fund @tomerlondon cto @GustoHQ and hopefully this is 'boring' and complex enough for Charlie Songhurst :> @delingpole @Liquid2V @ivolo from @segment @ryanpowe @sonicaghi of @kong @DellyTamer+ other supporters (@michaelwfrank, Fundamental ventures and if I missed you sorry moving fast!). 

[And don't worry, all vendor rankings are open scoring methods so no favors are being done if someone backed us and is a vendor they have to compete with how agentic and automatable they are just like anyone else.]

PS: we have bugs and many quality upgrades to make but thought better to go out early and fix as a community. 

PPS: we have other stuff to launch we just thought this was a great place to start and have 200 PRs coming out pretty soon but I still want to know what is broken or doesnt make sense or inaccurate. 

Special thanks to current and past team members for getting us here and all the experiments we did you know who you are.

He explains why designers are becoming more like editors, how AI is making them more full-stack, and why taste and judgment matter even more when the tools can build almost anything.

Then they review viewer-submitted websites and break down how hierarchy, motion, typography, and restraint can make a product feel more intentional.

Seeing Zcash represented at a recent adult pornography expo brought back one of the reasons I’m comfortable with that decision.

To be clear, I don’t hate transgender people. I’ll treat anyone with dignity and respect, even when we strongly disagree.

But I don’t share the beliefs surrounding gender identity, and I’m not going to pretend that I do. I believe biological sex matters. Adults can live their lives and make their own decisions.

What frustrates me even more is when these conversations are directed toward children.

That second photo is a pamphlet about gender identity and transition resources that was mailed directly to my 5-year-old nephew. I don’t know who funded it, and I’m not claiming Zcash had anything to do with it. I included it because it shows why this subject matters personally to me.

Respect people. Debate ideas. Let adults make their own choices.

But leave the kids out of it.

I’ll make my millions somewhere else.

翻开第一页就是一个吓人的数：上半年收入 163 亿美元，净亏 807 亿美元，亏掉的是赚到的 5 倍。

807 亿！其中 724 亿是可转债的会计费用：公司估值涨得越快，这批债在账上就越值钱，亏损也就记得越多，但这笔钱并没有真的花出去。上半年砸进算力和基建的，将近 90 亿。

更值得看的是它要付钱给谁。招股书写着，Anthropic 要向 SpaceX 买英伟达 GPU 算力，最多 1,205 亿美元，合同签到 2029 年，全部到位后每个月大约 31 亿。SpaceX 上周的三季报里，有一个客户付了 50 多亿，占当季收入的 34.5%，这个客户就是 Anthropic。

昨天老马说，没有独立收入的 neocloud 借不到钱。SpaceX 自己的算力生意，三分之一压在一个半年报亏 807 亿的客户身上。

招股书自己也写了：增长"可能不可持续"，可能"比预期更早"需要再融资。

市场传它要募资最多 1,000 亿美元，估值约 2 万亿。

今天马斯克继续neocloud大屠杀：

"过去几周，债务市场几乎完全关上了门，只要一家公司没有独立于 AI 数据中心之外的大笔收入，就借不到钱。"

这就是答案。昨天说的是机房卡在变压器、卡在并网，建了一半停在那。今天说的是更要命的一层：停在一半的时候，没人借你钱了。

大部分 neocloud 的模式很简单：借钱买卡，租出去，用租金还债。它们唯一的收入就是数据中心本身。数据中心没建完，就没有租金；没有租金，银行就不放款。这是个死循环。

老马顺手对比了自己：SpaceX 刚为 GPU 借了 400 亿美元债，能借到，是因为它是投资级，背后有星链和发射的收入在撑着。

同样是买卡，一个是靠别的生意养着的，一个是押上全部身家的。

他给的数字是：200 多家 neocloud，会迎来孔雀鱼级别的死亡和合并。"有些能活下来，但不多。"

老马是真的这么想，还是想惊慌市场，趁机收获一波？ $SPCX

text:
Anthropic的IPO S-1文件出爐了，代號 $ANT 算是攔胡螞蟻金服？
Claude 的企業採用速度正在快速成長，2026 年 Q2 營收達 115.6 億美元，季增 144%、年增 1,368%，並首次實現 GAAP 營業獲利 9.74 億美元，營業利益率達 8%。Q3 營收進一步達到約 168 億美元，季增約 45%。這代表 Anthropic 已經初步證明，AI 模型的商業化規模擴大後，可以產生相當可觀的營運槓桿。

2026 年 Q2 算力與基礎建設費用為 55.6 億美元，占營收比重從 2025 年 Q1 的 251%，快速下降到 48%。同期調整後營業利益達 22.4 億美元，調整後營業利益率達 19%。不過算力費用包含模型訓練、研發與推論，因此不能直接當成推論成本或毛利率。

這種規模經濟也反映在企業客戶的成長。Anthropic 截至 2026 年 9 月底：
＊年消費超過 10 萬美元的客戶超過 11,900 家，一年增加超過 12 倍。
＊年消費超過 100 萬美元的客戶超過 1,900 家，超過 1,000 萬美元的約 250 家。
＊淨營收留存率（NRR）高達約 900%，顯示既有客戶擴大使用的速度非常驚人。
＊超過 50% 的 Fortune 500 企業已達到年消費 10 萬美元的門檻。

Anthropic 約八成營收來自依 token 使用量計價的模式，Claude Code 則是推動企業採用的重要入口。公司表示，2026 年 9 月超過 90% 的內部程式碼貢獻由 Claude 撰寫，工程師平均每日程式碼貢獻量較 2024 年提高超過 45 倍。Anthropic 正試圖把這種生產力提升從軟體開發延伸到金融分析、法律與其他企業知識工作。

不過，獲利改善不代表未來現金流壓力已經解除。 Anthropic 2026 年上半年營業現金流轉正，達 39.3 億美元，相較去年同期流出 15.1 億美元明顯改善。但同期投資活動現金流出達 171.8 億美元，其中包含大量短期金融資產購買及增加的基礎建設資本支出。

更重要的是，Anthropic 通常需要提前 12～18 個月預訂算力，Anthropic 正在改變取得算力的方式。過去主要向 AWS、Google 等雲端平台租用算力，費用通常隨產能上線才開始支付；未來則透過 Anthropic Direct 直接租用晶片與專用資料中心，提前投入更多資本。公司明確預告，即使營運獲利持續改善，未來幾年的營運與投資活動合計仍可能出現龐大的淨現金流出。

為支撐擴張，Anthropic 截至 2026 年 6 月底持有約 1,317 億美元現金與短期投資，並於 9 月取得 150 億美元循環信用額度，同時獲得 Google、Amazon、Broadcom 等合作夥伴提供的融資安排。這些資金讓公司有能力提前部署算力，但部分融資與股權承諾仍取決於交付進度及其他條件。

未來展望方面，Anthropic 預期營收仍將成長，但成長率會隨規模擴大逐漸放緩。公司目前仍面臨算力供給不足，因此必須提前 12～18 個月預訂產能，甚至以更高價格採購短期算力。隨著新一批大型算力設備上線，相關成本可能先於營收出現，導致營業利益率階段性下降。

text:
Anthropic 的 S-1，让AI看了下结论是: 长期确实是一家非常牛逼的公司，但短期资本市场可能过于乐观了

财务数据确实惊人：

2025 年营收 $4.6B，2026 年仅上半年就达到 $16.3B。Q2 单季度营收 $11.6B，甚至已经实现接近 $1B 的 GAAP 经营利润。

企业大客户数量爆发，80% 的收入来自按 Token 使用量付费。但对于投资者来说，重要的不只是增长有多快，而是增长还能持续多久。Q3 营收 $16.8B，环比增长 45%，表面上依然非常亮眼。

管理层自己写明的风险：

1.明确预期增速将下降，"可能比我们预期的更显著、更快"，并承认"过去难以准确预测收入"。
2.80% 按量计费，大客户多数无长约或可随时缩减，有些大客户合同带灵活终止条款。
3.5–7% 的收入来自违反使用政策的客户（9 个月口径），8–9 月加强了封禁，会拖累后续增速。
4.季节性被高增长掩盖：2025 年底假期两周消费下降约 20%，增速放缓后会显现。

另外但从月度趋势来看，增长动能已经明显放缓。7 月底的 Revenue Run Rate 已经超过 $65B，而整个 Q3 的收入年化也只有 $67.2B。分月份的收入可能已经走平，甚至出现回落。

与此同时，Anthropic 在 S-1 中披露了数千亿美元的长期算力采购及租赁承诺。这些成本具有很强的刚性，一旦收入增长不及预期，经营杠杆也可能反噬

所以我认为 Q4 的数据非常关键。如果 Q4 能继续大幅增长，说明 AI Agent 的需求仍然在快速释放；但如果收入增速明显下台阶，市场就不得不重新审视对未来几年的增长预期。

我长期非常看好 AI，也相信 AI Agent 会创造巨大的经济价值。但长期看好AI和是否在高估值梭哈一家公司是两回事。

在 $2T 的估值预期下，我觉得市场可能已经提前透支了未来几年的高速增长。

text:
Anthropic just filed for its IPO and some of these numbers are absolutely insane.

The company generated $16.3 billion in revenue during the first half of 2026, compared to just $1.1 billion during the same period last year. That's incredible growth but what I find even more interesting is how much money Anthropic is spending to sustain it. Anthropic reportedly lost $80.7 billion during the first six months of 2026, although roughly $72 billion came from non cash accounting charges related to convertible financing. So the actual cash burn is nowhere near that headline number. However, the company still spent nearly $9 billion on compute and infrastructure during that period and has at least $518 billion in longer term infrastructure commitments.

And now we have Anthropic reportedly agreeing to spend up to $120.5 billion on computing capacity from SpaceX through 2029, with payments potentially reaching $3.1 billion per month once all the capacity is delivered. We're talking about a company spending billions every single month just to secure enough compute to remain competitive. Meanwhile, Anthropic is expanding its revolving credit commitments from $3.3 billion to $15 billion and increasing its minimum liquidity requirement from $500 million to $5 billion. Essentially, the company is securing access to significantly more financing while making sure it has enough cash available to support these enormous commitments. Another interesting detail is that Anthropic's seven co-founders will retain 50.1% of the voting power through a special Class F share that carries no economic rights. So even after going public, the founders will maintain control over major corporate decisions regardless of how much outside investors contribute.

Personally, I think Anthropic is an incredible business, but I've also been saying for a while now that frontier AI labs are being valued way too aggressively. Growing revenue at this pace is impressive, but eventually investors are going to want to see how much of that revenue actually turns into profits after paying for all this infrastructure. And this is exactly why I continue to prefer the infrastructure side of AI. Whether Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX, or another frontier lab comes out ahead, they all need compute, memory, networking, and power to keep scaling. The AI labs are spending hundreds of billions competing against each other, and the infrastructure companies are the ones collecting those checks.

text:
China Robotics Today 

If general models can generate robot actions, what remains for robotics companies to build?

A discussion from @YorkYang5050 on rednote:

1. The challenge reaches beyond planning.

He separates System 2 reasoning/planning, System 1 feedback-driven action, and System 0 low-level control. General models now reach into action generation.

2. Generating an action is only part of the deployment question.

His concern is timely response: chunking and asynchronous execution help, but changing environments still require adjustments.

NVIDIA reports 18.56 seconds per inference call for Direct Policy EEF on RoboLab-120, averaged over successful episodes and including network delay. The simulation pauses during inference. That is a narrow experimental result, not a demonstration of real-time physical control.

3. A smaller model still has to perform the task.

Smaller models must retain useful capabilities. His team's Qwen experience illustrates the tradeoff; it isn't a general benchmark.

NVIDIA's model comparison reports Astra at 72.7%, Sol at 33.3%, and Luna at 2.0%: 30 tasks and 150 episodes total per model. This compares deployed models; it does not test distillation or establish what a carefully distilled model could achieve. The evaluation uses simulated pick-and-place, excluding contact-rich insertion and assembly.

4. The two development paths could meet.

He sees potential convergence: frontier labs shrink capable models; robotics teams strengthen smaller policies. Both need robot data and training.

5. Onboard compute follows different constraints.

Robots face power, cooling, battery, space, weight and upgrade-cycle constraints. He invokes his Caper experience to question optimistic timelines.

For scale, NVIDIA specifies configurable 40–130 W power for Jetson AGX Thor. That is a module specification, not the robot's total power consumption or a guarantee that a particular model fits and runs well.

6. Network reliability needs its own discussion.

Coverage, roaming, interference and customer networks complicate deployment. Starlink doesn't directly solve indoor connectivity.

7. There is a constructive architecture here.

His proposed architecture combines general-model reasoning, memory and planning with a fast local policy that generalizes and responds to feedback.

8. Better models also improve how robot systems are developed.

General models also help labeling, failure analysis, recovery and data curation. Using the resulting data effectively still matters.

9. The physical product still has to work.

Touch, force feedback, sensors, control, manufacturing, delivery and service remain. He concludes stronger models can expand robotics opportunities without eliminating companies' value.

quoted_text:
@anandmahindra @Mahindra_Auto

LONG STORY SHORT
I bought a Mahindra Bolero B8 for my staff from Utkal Automobiles Pvt. Ltd., Barbil (Odisha) and paid ₹10,91,000 in full. The dealership kept saying "all fine, take delivery." The PDI report was never shared with me, yet the vehicle was registered. When I inspected it myself, I found a misaligned bonnet and then far more. A 14-point independent PDI inspection followed.

After my complaints, paint and body correction on a brand-new car came up. Each follow-up got me a new complaint number, and one was closed without my consent. Then the dealership offered ₹75,000 as "goodwill", refundable only at delivery of this same vehicle.

I offered to pay ₹75,000 EXTRA for a fresh unit. 206 days after my first payment, the vehicle is still in the showroom, undelivered.

THE NUMBERS
- ₹10,91,000 paid in full
- 206 days since first payment (27 March 2026) / 168 days since full payment (4 May 2026)
- 24+ emails from my side, plus calls to customer care and senior officials
- 3 complaint numbers: CF2700048215 → CF2700051620 (closed without my consent) → CF2700205465
- PDI report: never shared
- Resolution: zero

THE TWO TESTS THAT MATTER
Both were done at the Utkal Automobiles showroom, Barbil, in the presence of dealership representatives, on my vehicle and on another Bolero at the same showroom.
- AC: tested indoors and outdoors, 4 times. The other Bolero kept cooling. Mine starts cooling, stops within minutes and the cabin temperature climbs back up after ~13°C. It points to a compressor or compressor-switch fault. Recorded on video.
- Paint: same instrument, same inspector, same day. The other Bolero measured above 100 microns. Mine measured 63.3 to 85 microns, against a Mahindra standard of 100 to 150.

KEY FINDINGS (from the 14-point independent PDI inspection)

PAINT & BODY
1. Paint thickness 63.3–85 microns, below the 100–150 standard
2. Chipped paint, colour removal and scratches in 5 places: passenger rear door (near inside lock), bonnet driver side, bonnet passenger side (near hinge), front bumper, tailgate
3. Multiple sand spots in the paint
4. Pimples and dimples across body panels (Mahindra later acknowledged rectifying paint pimples under the bonnet)
5. Robotic punching marks on the skirting, abnormally prominent compared with the other Bolero

AIR CONDITIONING
6. AC stops cooling after ~13°C (details above)

GLASS
7. Rear quarter glass code mismatch: driver side E2G, passenger side E6

INTERIOR
8. Steering cover near the key area not fixed, with a visible gap
9. Pressed mark and misalignment on the dashboard airbag panel, a safety concern that needs formal certification
10. Roof lining not fitted properly, at the back corner

BODY ALIGNMENT & FINISH
11. Passenger door beading and bleeding issue not fixed
12. Rear bumper right side misaligned and bent
13. Rear door linings don't match on either side
14. Bonnet raised on one side, not flush, lining mismatched

ALSO FLAGGED IN MY EARLIER INSPECTIONS (13–21 May)
- Scrubbing and denting marks on the bonnet, which point to paint and body work done before delivery
- Passenger-side B-pillar bottom lining damaged
- Scratches on the driver-side door sill/footrest and on the tailgate footrest

MY ASK
I'm not asking for a favour. I paid for a brand-new vehicle, and I want a brand-new one. I have told Mahindra on calls and in writing that I will pay ₹75,000 extra for a fresh Bolero B8.

After 206 days without a solution, I'm bound to post this on X. I asked for a solution multiple times and never got one.

I own an XUV700 AX7L with alignment issues too. I never complained about it. I bought this Bolero for my staff, I complained, and this is what 206 days got me.

More images and videos are in the replies below.
