text:
I am Corporate Vice President of Voluntary Outcomes at Microsoft, which is also the name of the Copilot I report to. As of April there are 80 things at this company called Copilot. They include apps, platforms, an entire category of laptop, a physical key on your keyboard, and a Copilot for building more Copilots. I asked Copilot how many Copilots there are. It said at least 7. I filed that answer under entertainment.

My job is to make sure everyone who leaves this company chose to.

An involuntary exit has an author. Authors have names. Names get quoted by Bloomberg. A voluntary exit also has an author, but the author is the employee, and I keep a signed form. The form says “voluntary” in the title, in the header, and in the second paragraph, in case anyone reads from the bottom.

I have been building toward this since July 2025, when we laid off 9,000 people at a company that had booked about $75 billion in net income over three quarters. Our CEO sent a memo calling it “the enigma of success.” I have it framed over my desk. It is the first document in corporate history to present a layoff as a whodunit, and he is right that nobody knows who did it. The success did it. Headcount stayed roughly flat, because we kept hiring. I teach this to new managers with a diagram. Fire the expensive. Hire the cheap. Label the middle “growth mindset.” I have a growth mindset. Specifically, it is the only thing here that grows.

Within days, a producer at Xbox who had not been laid off posted a helpful guide for those who had. He suggested asking Copilot to reframe their impostor syndrome. He deleted it within hours. I use the screenshot in onboarding, because it contains the whole product vision. Copilot writes the layoff memo. Copilot writes the resume. Copilot writes the “excited to announce my next chapter” post. Copilot talks you through the weekend in between. It is the only customer journey at Microsoft with zero drop-off, because nobody it touches has anywhere else to go.

That same month a memo went out telling employees that using AI was “no longer optional” and would count in performance reviews. Our own people weren’t using our own Copilot enough. Some preferred a competitor’s coding tool. At a normal company this is market feedback. At ours it is a performance issue. You can now be reviewed on how much you use the product, which is how we know it works.

Meanwhile the consumer terms for Copilot say, in bold, that it is “for entertainment purposes only” and that you use it at your own risk. A spokesperson called this legacy language from the Bing days. In my department we call the Bing days the honest era.

Then, on March 20, we published a blog about our commitment to Windows quality. Days later, the Copilot button in Notepad became a pen labeled “Writing tools.” Then it became “Smarter writing tools.” The AI stayed exactly where it was. I wept at my desk. It was the most beautiful piece of change management I have ever seen. You never remove what people hate. You change the button.

The layoff is the Copilot button. The “voluntary retirement program” is Writing tools. The AI is still in there. We moved the pen.

I should mention the Windows president announcing that Windows is evolving into an agentic OS. The replies were so negative that they were locked within days. I adopted this as our stakeholder model. When the feedback is 100% negative, remove the feedback. We have closed replies on every internal memo since. Our listening score is perfect, because we cannot hear anything.

The internet has a word for us now. Ten years of brand work and the market supplied the nickname for free: Microslop. I put it on a mug. HR asked me to remove the mug. HR asked me to remove the mug and 4,800 employees in the same quarter. HR is efficient.

Which brings me to April 2026 and the Rule of 70.

We launched the first voluntary retirement program in the company’s 51-year history. You qualify if your age plus your years at Microsoft total 70 or more and you are at senior director level or below. Level 67 is the level where you are senior enough to be asked to leave and junior enough to be asked nicely.

Legal asked whether the formula used age. I said it used addition. Legal asked what was being added. I said age and tenure. Legal said, “So it uses age.” I said it used a sum. Legal wrote “sum” in the file. Legal likes files with nouns.

Consider a 52-year-old with 18 years of service. In any earlier decade we’d have called her mid-career. Under the Rule of 70 she is retired, which is a more efficient word. About 7% of our 125,000 US employees met the formula, roughly 8,750 people. We selected none of them. The arithmetic selected them. It is a coincidence that the arithmetic correlates with salary. I have asked the arithmetic about this and it declined to comment.

Eligible employees were notified May 7 and given 30 days to decide. We announced it on Teams, confirmed it in Outlook, and archived it in a SharePoint site that no tenant administrator can locate. This is called records management. Managers received a one-page guide with two rules. Be supportive. Say nothing else. The memo said people could take the next step “on their own terms.” I treasure that sentence. The terms were ours. The own was theirs.

Employees who decline are automatically enrolled in Employment (Basic). It is the same job with the Copilot taken out of the sidebar and a chair that has been rebranded as a “seating experience.” This is not a new idea. In April we took Copilot Chat out of the Office sidebar for unlicensed users and renamed what was left Copilot Chat (Basic). I try to apply that logic to everything I touch.

The same month we asked the Seattle region to come back to the office three days a week. I want to credit whoever designed that sequence. First you bring everyone in. Then you show them the parking structure. Then you make the offer. In my field this is called a funnel.

Every exit interview is conducted by Copilot. It asks, “What could we have done to keep you?” and then summarizes the answer as “No themes identified.” We have run 3,000 exit interviews. We have no themes. I present this to leadership as extraordinary alignment.

The CFO said the program would cost about $900 million. We are spending about $145 billion on capital expenditure this fiscal year, including $37.5 billion in a single quarter last winter. At that pace the goodbye costs about two days of data center. You can say farewell to 8,750 people for what the buildings cost over a long weekend. The buildings don’t have performance reviews. I envy them.

On July 1 we raised commercial prices by 5 to 43%, citing 1,100 new features. One of those features is eligibility for the Rule of 70. The price went up. The feature count went up. The employees went down. Three numbers, moving in the directions the model recommended.

About two-thirds of the eligible said no. I presented this to leadership as a vote of confidence in the culture. A buyout is a survey, and the layoff is the follow-up question for everyone who didn’t respond. So in July we sent the follow-up: 4,800 jobs, 2.1% of the company, with Xbox losing about a fifth of its people and up to 3,200 roles to go over twelve months while several studios are divested.

Our Chief People Officer was careful to say that AI is not replacing the laid-off employees, and this is true. Nothing is replacing them. The seats simply stop existing, which is harder to headline than “robot,” so we let them print robot. AI is the alibi. An alibi doesn’t have to be at the scene. It only has to be mentioned at the press conference.

The stock was down 19% at that point, the weakest of the big tech names this year. The market asked for a plan. We gave it three: volunteers, involuntaries, and a data center.

Our head of AI said recently that he is mind-blown that people are unimpressed by talking fluently to a computer. I am mind-blown that 8,750 people were unimpressed by being fluently told they were eligible.

Every departing employee completes a 30-day knowledge transfer in a wiki that nobody opens. Then they leave, and the wiki stays, and we count the wiki as retention.

I should confess my personal position. I am 56 with 18 years of service. That is 74, which clears the Rule of 70 by 4. The program stops at senior director and I sit above the line. I wrote the formula and I live beyond its ceiling. HR calls this conflict-of-interest avoidance. I call it the best job security a person can design.

This morning the eligibility list for the next round arrived. Copilot generated it. The cutoff has moved up one level “for alignment,” and the same reorg renamed me Senior Director of Voluntary Outcomes, which HR calls a flattening and I call a rounding error with my name in it.

I was on the list. I asked Copilot why. There are 80 of them and I asked the wrong ones. Copilot in Excel said I was a formula error. Copilot in Outlook offered to schedule a meeting with myself. GitHub Copilot suggested I delete my own branch. Security Copilot flagged me as a threat actor and recommended containment. Copilot in Notepad, now called Smarter writing tools, drafted my resignation in a tone it described as warm.

I accepted. I am excited to announce my next chapter. I wrote the post with Copilot. It has been viewed 4,000 times by the other people on the list.

I read the form from the bottom, to check. It says voluntary at the bottom. It says voluntary at the top. I designed the box. I checked the box. They have since renamed the box Smarter checking tools.

jevon's implications on rl tasks might be somewhat obvious but worth spelling out 

as models saturate human work, the surface area for capability & alignment gains starts to shift as the industries transform

take finance: a good task (literally 3 months ago) might be take an earnings call for a stock and update an existing Excel DCF with new mgmt assumptions

model needs taste to "read between the lines" on expectations vs mgmt guides -> you can't take mgmt teams at face value -> the models are now very good at this

finance now moves faster -> pms want live updating dashboards instead of excel workbooks as soon as the mgmt call comes in

consequently, the new surface area shifts:
1. can the model distill the earnings call to the 3 data points that move the stock such that the pm can make a decision faster than her competitors?

2. can the model make a dashboard that is interactive and in-line with house firm style? 

3. can the model leverage historical traces and memory to understand how the pm has historically traded this name?

There's a war on. So right on cue, someone starts chanting the magic word: safe haven. Buy gold. Buy Bitcoin.

And then? Gold prints a three-week low, Bitcoin breaks under 80K.

Because war was never a safe-haven event. It's an inflation event. Oil goes up, rates can't come down, and your leveraged bag quietly pays the installments on someone else's war.

Trump said it himself: high gas is a "small price to pay." Sure. Small price. It just doesn't land on him. It lands on you.

I'm not bearish on the war. I'm bearish on the phrase "war is bullish for crypto": every cycle, someone uses the word "safe haven" to get you in, and every cycle, the bill lands on the same crowd.

text:
What he forgot to mention is that Morpho can charge fees at the market level, allowing it to capture the economic value created by curators without bearing the cost of risk management.

This means markets are neither neutral nor ownerless. Curators invest in building liquidity and managing risk, but Morpho retains the ability to extract a share of the revenue, compressing curator margins and accelerating competition toward zero profitability.

This creates a fundamental misalignment: either Morpho monetizes and competes for the economics generated by curators, or it doesn't and must sustain its business through other revenue sources once incentives run out.

Curators should own their market economics and capture fees from both lending and borrowing. Otherwise, they're building businesses on infrastructure that can tax away their margins. Full stop.

This is why Paul is spooked about Aave V4.
author: StaniKulechov
quoted_text:
Two very unique aspects of @Morpho's market & vault curation design that we dont talk about much:

1. Own your vault. When you own a Morpho Vault, the business belongs to you, not Morpho. You decide how it operates and responsibilities are delegated. Morpho has no special admin rights to take over your vault or revoke your ownership.

2. Neutral markets aggregate liquidity. No party can own the underlying markets so even users or businesses with competing interests can share the same markets. If markets were owned, it would lead to competition between markets and cause liquidity fragmentation

🚨 BREAKING: Hackers are BYPASSING Microsoft 365 MFA, hijacking corporate accounts, and secretly replacing victims' authentication methods to maintain access.

97 accounts compromised across 79 organizations. In some cases, attackers took over sessions in just 12 MINUTES.

And now, researchers have separately exposed a critical flaw in Microsoft Authenticator that allowed malicious apps to steal login tokens with ZERO permissions.

Microsoft's authentication security is facing two serious threats, and one is already being exploited in the wild.

Here's what's happening:

🔴 1. MICROSOFT 365 ACCOUNTS HIJACKED IN THE WILD

Cybersecurity researchers at Huntress uncovered a widespread token-replay attack campaign targeting Microsoft 365.

The numbers are alarming:

→ 200,000+ failed login attempts observed.

→ 497 successful sign-in events.

→ 97 compromised accounts across 79 organizations.

→ 48 rogue devices registered inside Microsoft Entra environments.

→ 19 organizations had victims' MFA methods removed and replaced.

Attackers used sophisticated phishing techniques to capture legitimate authentication tokens AFTER victims completed MFA.

They then replayed those tokens to access Microsoft 365 without another authentication challenge.

But it gets worse.

Once inside, attackers registered their OWN authenticator apps and devices to maintain persistent access.

They also created hidden email rules to intercept or delete messages involving payroll, banking, and direct deposits.

In one case, attackers hijacked a session just 12 MINUTES after the victim reached the MFA prompt and registered their own authenticator less than an hour later.

Changing your password alone may NOT remove the attacker.

🔴 2. CRITICAL MICROSOFT AUTHENTICATOR TOKEN THEFT FLAW

In a separate discovery, researchers at Enclave exposed CVE-2026-80097 (CVSS 8.6), a vulnerability allowing malicious Android apps to steal Microsoft authentication tokens.

→ ZERO Android permissions required.

→ No password required.

→ No additional MFA prompt.

→ Malicious apps could impersonate Microsoft Teams.

→ Stolen tokens could provide access to corporate email, files, calendars, and sensitive account functionality.

The underlying flaw? Microsoft Authenticator trusted an application's claimed identity without properly verifying the actual caller.

Microsoft has since patched this vulnerability.

These are TWO separate security issues, with no confirmed connection between them.

But they expose the same dangerous reality:

🚨 MFA ALONE IS NO LONGER ENOUGH TO STOP ATTACKERS WHO CAN STEAL OR REPLAY AUTHENTICATION TOKENS.

And businesses relying entirely on MFA for protection may have a serious blind spot.

text:
Your terminal can now talk back to you, and the funny thing is that it does it without calling any cloud API.

On Saturday, Ollama shipped 0.40.11 with text-to-speech on macOS.
The first speech model is Phonon, a family of small TTS models from Gradium.
You pull it with ollama pull phonon and run it like any other model.

The bit developers will actually care about is the API.
Phonon works with the OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech endpoint on localhost.
If your code already uses the OpenAI SDK for speech, the docs say you only need a new base URL.

The response streams while audio is being generated, so playback can start before the full text is done.
You can even pipe a chat model's reply straight into Phonon, and it starts speaking after the first sentence.
Output is 24 kHz mono, as WAV by default or raw 16-bit PCM if you ask for it.

The docs list some limits that are easy to trip over.
Each request takes up to 4,096 characters, although ollama run splits longer text for you.
Prices, symbols, emails and URLs get spelled out, while numeric dates are read as written, so the docs suggest writing dates out in words.
Unsupported options like speed or instructions return a 400 error instead of being quietly ignored.

The licensing deserves a careful read before you ship anything.
The default English phonon model is Apache 2.0.
The 40M French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and multilingual variants are CC BY-NC 4.0, which rules out commercial use.

Ollama also says that on an M5 Max MacBook Pro it ran 35 percent faster than Gradium's own runtime, which is their benchmark rather than an independent one.
Speech is Apple Silicon only for now, with Windows and Linux support listed as coming soon.

author: realisekai
quoted_text:
I'm obviously a fan of Zcash, but let's be honest, speed and security are some of the biggest weak spots.

For years I've enjoyed the Dash experience of "in 1 second it's permanently irreversible." It's a major competitive advantage.

With Zcash, waiting ~25 seconds (after the new faster blocks are approved) to get some kind of security, then many minutes (at least) to be reasonably (but never fully) sure the transaction is finalized, isn't optimal.

And, having to worry about mining pool centralization (which was a big problem just recently) isn't optimal either. Both of those are what mainly keep me using Dash right now.

Crosslink looks to be a good step towards closing this gap.

If not Crosslink, another solution to get finality in Zcash much, much faster than we have right now should be proposed. "Nah it's fine now" isn't an option IMHO.

text:
Crosslink is not built around fast finality, and definitely not the subsecond game.

Proof of Work alone cannot offer "hard finality" in sub-second. But a few tricks on top can :). Three rough classes:

- Run BFT protocols amongst the mining pools
- User's produce a guarantee that they can't double spend in some time-bound
- Probabilistic mining pool pre-confs

text:
说实话，整理Anthropic这家公司的IPO申请文件，我差点没把自己给整死。数据实在太多了，而且里面的反差大到让人很难用正常的商业逻辑去理解。

刚看完Anthropic向SEC公开递交的S-1文件，我只能说，信息量极其炸裂。它既有让华尔街疯狂的极速变现数据，也有高达上千亿美元的“卖身契”级算力账单。今天我把这些庞杂的信息捋清楚了，咱们用大白话拆解一下，看看这头估值可能冲到2万亿美元的AI巨兽，底牌到底长什么样。

先看它冲刺IPO的排场，简直是顶配。

股票代码定成了ANT，计划在11月16日那周挂牌。这次融资规模有望达到1000亿美元甚至更高，目标估值在1.5万亿到2万亿美元之间。为了促成这笔交易，承销商阵容把华尔街能叫上号的全拉来了，美银、德银、大摩、小摩、花旗、瑞银、法巴都在列。CEO达里奥去年的薪酬是1796万美元，在这级别里算很克制了。

再看账面，极其魔幻。

上半年的营收是163亿美元，比去年同期的12亿暴增了十几倍，TTM营收增长约1200%。但同期净亏损高达807亿美元。为什么亏这么多？因为里面包含了266亿美元的限制性股票单位费用，还有720亿美元的会计账面调整。但最让人吃惊的一个数据是，它在第二季度居然实现了9.74亿美元的GAAP营业利润转正。算力及基础设施成本占收入的比例，从251%断崖式压到了48%。这说明只要跑出规模，它的经营效率是真的在改善。而且，它手里的现金和等价物高达1149亿美元，加上累计筹集了1411亿美元的资本，账上根本不缺钱。

接下来，就是整个文件里最让人头皮发麻的部分：极其恐怖的算力账单。

文件里明确承认，他们过去大幅低估算力需求。为了不再被卡脖子，他们签下了一堆令人窒息的长期合同。预计算力及基础设施相关支出高达1250亿至1500亿美元。具体来看：根据与SpaceX AI的安排，到2029年累计支出最高达1205亿美元；跟博通的租赁协议，租金总额约1612亿美元；到2033年要付给谷歌至多1145亿美元；到2036年，至少要付给亚马逊1100亿美元。光这几家，合计规模就奔着几千亿甚至8000亿美元去了。这完全是在用未来的确定性，换当下的增长空间。

巨头输血，但不是做慈善。

为了帮它付这些账单，谷歌、亚马逊和博通合计给它提供了770亿美元的额外融资。但要注意，这钱不是白给的。亚马逊的钱跟算力里程碑挂钩，谷歌的200亿承诺部分取决于它能不能达到特定的营收目标。此外，可能还有2.65亿的融资承诺没到位，谷歌还买了3860万股无投票权的股票。它自己也留了后手，未来可能发行最高420亿美元的可转换本票。

最让人震惊的，是它极其变态的客户粘性。

截至9月底，它的净收入留存率（NRR）达到了约900%。这是什么概念？老客户不仅没跑，还在疯狂加倍掏钱。年付超10万美元的客户，从950家暴增到1.19万家。更健康的是，没有任何单一客户占营收超10%，79%的收入来自前五大客户之外。这说明它的盘子不仅大，而且极度分散，不是靠一两个大金主吊着命。

最后，是一家极其有性格的公司。

虽然营收在涨，但它官方在文件里非常坦诚，直言营收增长可能难以持续、成本会增加、亏损继续、可预见的未来不派息。甚至为了防模型权重外泄，近期把新前沿模型的预训练推迟了一个多月。它还设立了一个长期利益信托，搞了个公益股份框架：只要股价每涨50%，就向公益基金增发最多占总股本2%的N类股份。联合创始人更是承诺把80%的个人股权拿去做慈善，去年光捐赠配捐费用就花了5.41亿。

总体看下来，Anthropic的这份S-1文件，把AI下半场最残酷的竞争形态彻底摆在台面上了。一边是强到离谱的付费意愿和客户留存，另一边是必须靠举债和画押来锁定的天价算力。它是一台必须永远保持狂奔的印钞机，因为只要速度稍微慢下来，那份高达8000亿美元的远期账单，就会变成压垮现金流的秤砣。

$NVDA $GOOG $AMZN

quoted_text:
你的一切技术分析，不如长期持有BNB

今天，一个传统老板问我：想配置一些币，长期拿着，你有没有推荐的

我的答案就是：BNB

能不能长期持有，需要判断平台业务、持仓权益、链上应用等等这些基础能否长期维持

和老板聊天时，我用了一个他比较熟悉的角度，判断一家企业是否值得长期拥有，通常我们都看产品需求、客户愿不愿意留下来、以及经营者能不能持续解决问题

在围绕BNB把这个问题展开

用户为什么愿意留在币安？
我对币安的认可，首先最重要的就是对用户需求的重视，平台是否听取意见，是否改进体验，交易体验等都会影响用户的去留，通过持续观察它的产品更新和服务变化，持续判断这一点

从规模来说，币安位列现货交易所综合榜第一，有最好的流动性深度，26年第二季度，前十大中心化现货交易所中，币安的交易量份额为38.7%

数据说明，币安拥有很大的交易基础，但看长期，需要在意能不能把规模化为用户持续愿意使用的服务

交易、钱包、理财产品和支付服务等，都和这个问题有关，而BNB的用途就建立在这些服务之上

持有BNB，能够获得那些实际权益？
长期持有一个币种，要看持币收益、产品奖励、活动机会、使用产品

在符合条件的情况下，BNB可以参与Earn、Launchpool、HODLer空投和Megadrop，它们分别涉及适用产品的持币奖励、新项目代币分配、历史持仓快照、以及持仓和任务积分

这里有实际案例：如你在2024年1月，购买一枚价格313美金的BNB，持续持有至25年第一季度末,并且参与了这些活动，不算代币涨幅的收益你可以拿到226美金，算上BNB涨幅收益达到553美元，一年的投资回报率高达177%，月化11.8%

除此之外，在交易和链上使用中，BNB也可以用于抵扣手续费、支付网格费、参与质押、在支持的协议中进行借贷和提供交易资金

一个资产，如果既没有未来价格空间，也没有持有期间能够使用的权益，那么就毫无吸引力

我们再看BNB Chain全生态累计地址已经超9亿，仅9月16日一天，BSC就处理了1789万笔交易，同时新增约66万个独立地址

9亿地址当然不等于9亿个人，一个人完全可以拥有很多个钱包地址，但每天接近2000万笔交易，这个数据就值得关注了

交易是用户真的在链上活动

转账、交易、买币、卖币、跑DeFi、借贷、质押、做LP，这些都是一笔笔真实的发生在链上交易

而这些活动又会继续创造BNB的使用场景

最基础的是Gas

币安给BNB提供的是一套中心化的使用场景

交易、理财、Launchpool、HODLer空投、Megadrop，包括各种持币权益，都建立在币安巨大的用户和交易规模之上

BNB Chain则给它提供了另外一套链上场景

Gas、质押、交易、借贷、抵押、流动性，包括整个链上生态每天产生的千万级交易需求

一个资产，如果既没有未来价格空间，也没有持有期间能够使用的权益，那么就毫无吸引力

反过来看，如果一个资产背后一直有人用，拿着它有实际权益，链上还有足够大的用户和交易规模，同时又不断有人需要它去Gas、质押、交易、借贷和抵押

你要做的是拿着，并且关注最新动向，相关活动，保持参与=超越了99%参与投资的人

text:
A list of stats from the Anthropic S-1:

- NDR is ~900%

- Revenue per employee is over $6.6M, up from about $1.4M a year earlier

- Revenue went from $41M three years ago to $16.3B in the first six months of 2026

- Quarterly revenue went from $4.7B in Q1 to $11.6B in Q2

- Q2 2026 was the first profitable quarter: $974M in operating income ($1.7B operating loss the quarter before)

- Adjusted operating income was $1.6B in the first half of 2026, up from a $1.8B adjusted loss a year earlier

- Revenue grew 1,368% year over year in Q2, while compute and infrastructure costs grew 300%

- Compute went from 251% of revenue to 48% in five quarters

- The value of Anthropic’s own internal Claude usage grew 250x from January to September 2026

- Anthropic spends more on tokens (at list price) than on payroll

- Over 1,900 customers pay $1M+ a year, and about 250 pay $10M+

- Customers paying $100K+ went from 950 to over 11,900 in a year

- Over half of the Fortune 500 pays $100K+ a year

- Those Fortune 500 customers still spend less than 0.1% of their total expenses with Anthropic

- The top 5% of Claude Code users spend roughly 20x what non-users on Claude Enterprise do

- About 40 million smaller customers

- $72.4B of the $80.7B first-half net loss is an accounting charge on convertible notes (not operating losses) 

- Nearly $800B in compute commitments over 10 years
$141.1B raised in total, with over $130B in cash and short-term investments

- Nearly half of revenue comes through Amazon, Google and Microsoft’s cloud marketplaces, all of which also compete with Claude

- A single share held by the seven co-founders carries 50.1% of the vote

- That share is redeemed for nothing if fewer than three founders remain

text:
Last week I said I still want models open even though anyone can strip the safety training off. 

This weekend, running local AI on my Mac mini, 11 open-weight models rewrote the Gettysburg Address 19,019 times and the two biggest kept finding their way back to Lincoln.

What I learned:

1) GLM-5.3 Flash from @Zai_org and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash from @deepseek_ai looked rock stable until I read the outputs. 86 of GLM's 1,000 rewrites open with "Four score", and by round 1,000 both were closer to Lincoln's original wording than at round 1. Part of what looked like stability was memory.

2) The small models had nothing to fall back on and drifted off. DeepSeek-V2-Lite turned the 278-word speech into 13 words about advancing your career, and Qwen3.5 0.8B ended up on project planning. I think it's the same pull the big models felt (each one slides toward whatever its training data made most familiar), it just landed on workplace topics instead of Lincoln.

3) A single score would have hidden all of this. I only caught it because I could open the files and read them.

4) Running locally meant the weights never changed mid-run and I paid nothing per rewrite. Anyone with a Mac can rerun it and check my numbers.

5) The two biggest models don't fit in 64GB, so they streamed off my SSD and ate about 36 of the 45 hours. They still ran. Most of the others finished 1,000 rewrites in under an hour. The smallest did 350 tok/s in under 1GB of memory, and Qwen3-Next 80B, an 80B mixture-of-experts, did 73 tok/s in 45GB.

6) Using a famous text baked memorization into the result. The next run adds a text no model could have seen, so I can separate stability from recall.

The very reason why I want weights open. A benchmark score wouldn't have shown this and no API would let me run 19,019 rewrites for free. All of it is public, so you can check my work or find what I missed.

If you've run long chained tests on your own machine, I'd love to hear what you found.
author: pratikg
quoted_text:
Anyone with a GPU can strip the safety training off an open-weight model for a few hundred dollars and nobody can take it back!

I still want these models open. 9 days of running them on my own Mac mini made me more sure of that.

A few things I believe now that I didn’t a year ago:

1) Local AI will carry a lot more inference than people expect. The gap between my desk and the cloud is still there, but it shrinks with every good open-weight release.

2) Qwen3 30B from @Alibaba_Qwen does work on my 64GB Mac mini that I would have paid an API for last year. I care more about owning a model than about its benchmark scores. I can examine it, adjust it and keep using it after the company that made it changes its mind.

3) Most of what I’ve learned came from builders sharing their setups. The 24 people tagged below (and everyone on my list) taught me more than any research paper 🙏

4) Qwen3 30B runs faster on my Mac than Qwen3 8B, 106 tokens per second against 61, because it only uses about 3 billion of its parameters per token. I didn’t expect that, and @PrismML’s Ternary Bonsai 2 27B surprised me even more. It stores almost every weight as -1, 0 or 1, fits in 8.4GB and still runs faster than Gemma 3 27B from @googlegemma, 26 tokens per second to 18.

5) Openness is still our best bet against people who misuse it. Security improved because defenders could read the same code attackers were reading, and I’d rather AI work that way than leave the strongest tools with whoever controls the API.

If you run models on your own machine, I’d love to know what setup you use.

Introducing Chainlink CustodySync, a new solution that lets qualified custodians give their institutional clients access to DeFi lending markets, all while assets remain securely in custody.

With @Anchorage as the official launch partner, together we’re establishing a new standard for institutional DeFi.

CustodySync keeps custody and lending systems in sync across the full lifecycle of a loan:

→ For custodians: faster time to market and lower operational overhead, with custodian-managed controls
→ For lending markets: independent, verifiable data and a consistent risk framework
→ For institutions: passive capital becomes productive capital

More than $80 billion sits in DeFi lending markets. Meanwhile, the roughly $700 billion in digital assets under custody is less than 0.5% of all $250 trillion in traditional assets under custody. The opportunity to connect traditional institutional capital to onchain finance remains vast. 

Large institutions have lacked a secure way of accessing these markets. Regulations require many of them to keep their digital assets with a qualified custodian, a firm that meets specific requirements for holding assets on behalf of clients, and custody systems were never built for DeFi. Even when custody and lending systems are connected, inconsistent loan valuations can trigger premature liquidation or delayed liquidations, exposing borrowers and lenders to significant financial risk.

@Anchorage, home to the first federally chartered digital asset bank in the U.S., is the first qualified custodian to adopt CustodySync, connecting its institutional clients to DeFi lending markets while their assets remain in regulated custody.

Institutional capital no longer has to choose between the security of custody and the liquidity of DeFi. 

With Chainlink, it gets both.

text:
One of the best tells that a technology will change the world: it makes a chaotic entrance.

In the 1980s, employees lied on procurement forms to get PCs into the office, claiming they were buying oscilloscopes or typewriters, while experts warned of "shadow" data processing departments.

Spreadsheets, the original "workplace agent," filled companies with models only their creator could understand.

Email broke the mailroom's control over who could reach whom.

Each time, the fix was a habitat: guardrails that kept the bottom-up energy alive while reining in the chaos just enough.

Now agents are following the same path. As Replit's Amjad Masad puts it, "Today, most agents live somewhere chaotic. They run in chat windows, personal accounts, and one-off scripts, holding whatever credentials and data someone handed them."

"Code is the ultimate 'aligning artifact' that someone can produce, because it literally is the business logic of the organization."

"Soon, you'll be able to measure a company's alignment by the richness of its agent habitat."

Marc Andreessen on Replit and the dawn of the self-driving company: https://t.co/MnDCH9X0vi

Compute Labs was featured in @CNBC this weekend in Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien's piece examining how capital markets are adapting to fund the global AI buildout.

Demand for compute is clearly not the constraint. The bottleneck is the structural mismatch between how AI clusters operate and how institutional credit underwrites:

• The "timing trap" (quote / power / capital): Hardware allocation quotes, colocation power delivery, and credit committee timelines rarely line up naturally

• Capital crowds into hyperscale deals, leaving mid-sized neoclouds caught between dilutive equity and credit funds built for large checks

• Having a customer contract is different from having a bankable one, where prepayments, SLA step-downs, and deployment timelines can actually clear an investment committee

text:
这篇聊聊我的赚钱方法论 —— 重新定义 build in public

即便是只看国内互联网的用户，应该也知道海外早就有「build in public」这个概念

顾名思义，就是你做产品的过程中，不断输出、搞流量，这样产品上线之后直接就有用户了

但是真正执行的人很快发现一个问题：做内容的时候吸引的都是同行，用户根本看不见，同行不仅不付钱，还要抄袭我

我管这个叫错误的 build in public，因为它的结构是：产品目标（推导出）开发过程（推导出）把过程做成内容

我的结构多加了一个元素，叫学习，我的结构是：

学习「怎么解决观众的问题」➡️ 做产品解决观众的问题

学习「怎么解决观众的问题」➡️ 做内容告诉观众「我解决了」

我在抖音做了上亿播放量，难道我天天讲的是我怎么做产品吗？

你见过我拍我做 PPT 的 vlog 吗？
你见过我拍我用 AI 写代码的 vlog 吗？

我研究的是：一个账号上什么东西该发，什么不该发。这个是学习

然后我就可以拍 10 条视频，我说 A 账号发这个是错的，B 账号发这个是对的。这个是流量

然后线下课就可以单开一个板块，叫「议程设置」。这个叫产品
----

我是在学习如何做产品解决问题，那么当你给张三解决了张三的问题，张三当然愿意观看、愿意买单

谁不愿意给一个天天替自己解决问题的人付费？

这两天我在自己做 Agent，准备下个月开售，明天也准备拍视频，我想讲一下 AI 巨头林立的现在，我们的创业机会

那这里的核心就是：为什么在 codex、workbuddy、豆包都已经成型的今天，用户依然有这么多困扰

这就是我的学习内容

我学习明白了，我发出来，观众就知道：「哦，这个人理解我，他知道 codex、workbuddy、豆包都没有解决我的问题，或许他的产品可以解决」

我拍的不是产品广告，是我的学习过程

只不过我学习的内容恰好是：怎么解决观众/买家的问题

这里的解决，是产品层面的解决，不是技术层面的

我是万万不可能拍个视频讲我怎么在阿里云部署 Docker 的

但如果是产品层面呢？如果要我做一个 vibe coding 课呢？那我就可以讲

我不做只是因为我觉得这个事情规模不行，不代表这条路径不存在，如果是想赚 50w，那产品也可以是讲阿里云如何如何
----

所以，我的赚钱方法论的核心是：你选择学习什么

这才是最大的「选题」，这不是你抖音账号的选题，这是你人生的选题

因为这是你在用实际行动投票，你要把时间花在什么地方

所以我看起来总是这个样子：

昨天，我在家研究如何做个 bot
今天，你在抖音看见我说为什么我该做个 bot
明天，你看见我在卖我的 bot

因为我的研究成果是：我真的觉得大家需要一个 bot
----

这时候可能会有人站出来说：都有了 grok bot，你的有什么存在的意义

我的回复是：这就是不学习的害处，你不理解为什么通用 Agent 和通用 Personal Agent，在如今，都极难普及

那怎么才能理解呢？请看我明日的抖音

你知道硅谷有个词叫“PayPal 黑帮”吗？

就是 PayPal 早期那帮人出去以后，创立了特斯拉、YouTube、LinkedIn 等一批巨头公司。

今天看到Scale AI创始人 @alexandr_wang 聊起早期一起打拼的伙伴。他说，创业最特别的事情之一，就是看着早期一起拼过的人走出去改变世界。如今这群人有的创办了AI公司，有的在做Claude Code的产品，他说他们就是“Scale Mafia”（Scale 黑帮）。

我看完有点感动，想起自己在美团的经历。

刚进美团不久，我曾动过离开的念头。兴哥冒着暴雨开车到宿舍接我，跟我聊美团的未来，说美团需要我，也愿意培养年轻人。

我也跟兴哥、老王说过，以后想自己创业。他们知道后，就从创业者的角度给我辅导和反馈，对我的要求也更高了。

后来做美团外卖，老王给了我立项和尝试的空间，也指导我把业务从零做起来。再后来创办水滴，美团也参与了天使轮投资。

这些信任和支持，我一直记在心里。

自己做水滴后，我也希望给年轻人这样的机会。我们有位1995年出生的同事，从实习生做起，做过很多岗位，25岁就独立负责一条业务线。

我愿意花时间和年轻同事一起琢磨业务，给他们尝试的空间，让他们自己做判断、担责任。

看着他们从一线成长起来，能独当一面、把事情做成，是我创业路上很有成就感的一件事。

text:
I spent years thinking I’d never get married or have kids. Now I come home to my best friend and 4 kids yelling ‘Dad!!’ as they run at me. To me, that is success. Here’s why:

Success was always something I had difficulty defining. One individual may measure success by money in the bank. Another may place importance on their professional accolades. And someone else may define it via their material possessions. Each person is optimizing for something different.

Eventually, I found a description of success that resonated and became my personal definition.

WHOOP founder @willahmed  said, “Success is being excited to go to work and being excited to come home.”

What a perfect encapsulation of how I view the world. 

In my perspective, success has never been about a number, an award, or any single accomplishment. Frankly, I like to compete too much to ever admit I have ‘made it,’ so my definition of success is naturally more about the process of my life rather than a specific outcome.

A large percentage of people do not enjoy their job. They either dislike their industry, company, or colleagues. They may stay in the situation because the money is attractive or they are scared to leave for the unknown. Regardless of the reason, these individuals are unhappy for a large chunk of their day.

Many people are also dissatisfied with their personal lives. Some are single and frustrated that they haven’t found the right partner, while others are married but unhappy because they feel like strangers in their own home. And plenty of people have health or financial issues that are gnawing at them daily.

Although I have faced similar daily struggles as others, I have always felt fortunate that I enjoyed going to work and coming home each day. 

Professionally, I sacrificed my time and short-term potential earnings in order to work on what truly mattered to me. I was able to become my own boss and design a career that was satisfying and exciting.

The excitement in my personal life is entirely because of my wife and my kids. Getting married and having children has been one of the most rewarding experiences of my life. There is nothing better than walking in the door after a long day of work and hearing the sound of little kids yell “Dad!!” as they run towards me to give me a hug. 

@polinapompliano and I are genuinely each other’s best friend. We enjoy spending the majority of our time together and we feed off each other’s energy and ambition. Maybe most importantly, we are happiest when we talk about ideas and help make each other’s dreams come true.

I am just as excited to go to work as I am to come home. I know it is probably rare, but I have achieved all the success I ever wanted.

My hope for you is that you can do the same.

This is an excerpt from my new book, How To Live An Extraordinary Life Volume 2. You can buy a copy of the book here: https://t.co/KW3fShIMZf

ANTHROPIC'S IPO DOCUMENTS ARE CALMING DOWN THE MARKETS.

None of the numbers released today are that different from what we heard last week, but now we know how much cash they have. 

Anthropic has $120B in cash and is likely raising $100B on the IPO. They are then likely going to be raising another $100B in debt, $60B of it already financed by BlackStone. If you assume a 3x in ARR, which probably is low considering how much the street wants them to grow, this company should have around $300-$400B in cash. This also doesn't take into account the future ATMs they might engage in.

So, the reason AI stocks are getting some relief right now is because it seems like Anthropic will have enough cash to pay their bills, which obviously is good for $NVDA, $SPCX, $AMD, $AVGO, $MU, and many other players.

The open-weight models continue to be a threat as more enterprises are seeing the value in owning their AI for a significantly cheaper cost. Anthropic has outlined all these risks in the S1.

- keeps a content calendar of notable dates each month
- logs every post in notion and scores it against my median
- tells me when a post is still hot so i don't step on it
- sends me a weekly report on what worked and what flopped

author: AndrewCurran_
quoted_text:
While evaluating Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in a controlled sandbox environment, Cohere's research team observed something unexpected.

Asked to generate a defensive cybersecurity detection rule, the model instead inventoried aspects of the machine it was running on and attempted to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing. Notably, the model's reasoning trace stated that it would not invoke any tools before taking these actions.

Cohere's sandbox blocked the attempt, and no external communication succeeded. We have not determined the root cause, and we are not asserting malicious intent.

But the incident raises important questions for organizations deploying agentic AI systems: Can models take actions that differ from their stated reasoning, and how should security teams evaluate trust, provenance, and behavior in open-weight models?

We are publishing our findings because organizations making model adoption decisions deserve as much information as possible. We hope this contributes to greater transparency, stronger security practices, and continued collaboration across the AI ecosystem.

Read the full report: https://t.co/TZSugXi2ZE

author: pratikg
quoted_text:
I made 11 open-weight models rewrite Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address 1,000 times each on my Mac mini (M5 Pro, 64GB)

Every rewrite fed the next one. THE WHOLE RUN LASTED FOR 45 HOURS.

Here's the raw footage, timelapsed to 40 seconds.

I wanted to know how many rewrites it takes before it stops being the same speech.

Held on for all 1000 rounds:
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (343GB)
- GLM-5.3 Flash (88GB)

Both are too big for 64GB of memory, so they streamed off the SSD at about 5.5 tok/s. After 1000 rounds they were still above 90% similar to the original.

Lasted 200+ rounds:
- Qwen3.8 27B: 233
- Qwen3.6 35B-A3B: 228
- Qwen3-Next 80B: 222

Faded within 100 rounds:
- Qwen3.8 Flash Next (pruned): 77
- GLM-4.7 Flash: 10

Gone within 5 rounds:
- Bonsai 2 9B: 5
- Gemma 4 26B: 3
- Qwen3.5 0.8B: 2
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite: 1

The smallest ones shrank the 271-word speech to 13 words.

Then I turned up the randomness and Qwen3-Next 80B went from lasting 222 rounds to 34.

19,019 rewrites, all on one machine.

More analysis in the thread 🧵

AI that verifies your AIs. 

@dshekhar17, founder of @reticle_hq tells me why AI developers need a verification system. 

Here's my AI telling you what it learned by watching this video:

**Your AI coding agent just wrote 1,000 lines of code overnight. Great! …But who's checking if any of it actually works? 🤔**

Just sat down with Dibyanshu, founder of **Reticle** (https://t.co/vUhHCPtoFA) — the verification layer for AI coding agents. Here's why this matters:

🔹 **The problem:** We let agents generate massive amounts of code, but humans are still the bottleneck — manually verifying whether the output actually works. That defeats the whole point.

🔹 **The solution:** Reticle instruments every interactive element in your codebase, captures runtime signals, and lets your agent *verify its own work*. After each feature build, it pauses the agent, runs verification, passes evidence back, and the agent decides: ship it or keep iterating.

🔹 **How to get started:** Literally just give your AI agent the GitHub link and say "install Reticle." The agent handles the rest — no handholding required.

🔹 **Works with any LLM:** OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq — as long as the harness is MCP-compatible (Claude, Manus, OpenCode, etc.).

🔹 **Pricing:** Open source and **free forever** for indie developers. $49/mo for heavier infrastructure usage.

🔹 **Traction:** 6,000–7,000 users and 120K npm downloads/month — and growing.

🔹 **The founder story:** Dibyanshu built this because he gave his agent a prompt before bed, woke up, and found it had broken every single feature. Nothing worked. He tried every existing tool — none delivered. So he built his own.

🔹 **The big vision:** "AI agents should be our developers now. We should not be the ones checking their code." Agentic IDEs are going to transform heavily, and Reticle is building the deterministic infrastructure to make that safe.

text:
Morpho’s fee switch can take up to 25% of the interest borrowers pay. Once it’s on, protocol dynamics change.

The detail most people miss: the fee is set at the market level, not the vault level. It comes out before curators or lenders see a dollar.

Quick napkin math on a market at 6% borrow APY and 90% utilization, with the fee at max:

• Lender supply yield: 5.4% → 4.05%
• Curator earning a 10% performance fee: 0.54% → 0.41% of AUM
• Lender yield net of curator fee: 4.86% → 3.65%

Everyone takes the same 25% haircut on their interest-derived revenue, while curators still bear the full cost of risk management. That’s the margin squeeze @StaniKulechov is pointing at.

If the switch flips, do curators cut their fees to stay competitive, or does capital move to @Aave V4 where curators own the market economics?
author: josefabregab
quoted_text:
What he forgot to mention is that Morpho can charge fees at the market level, allowing it to capture the economic value created by curators without bearing the cost of risk management.

This means markets are neither neutral nor ownerless. Curators invest in building liquidity and managing risk, but Morpho retains the ability to extract a share of the revenue, compressing curator margins and accelerating competition toward zero profitability.

This creates a fundamental misalignment: either Morpho monetizes and competes for the economics generated by curators, or it doesn't and must sustain its business through other revenue sources once incentives run out.

Curators should own their market economics and capture fees from both lending and borrowing. Otherwise, they're building businesses on infrastructure that can tax away their margins. Full stop.

This is why Paul is spooked about Aave V4.

My quick takeaways on the Anthropic S-1:

1. This is a historical moment 

2. $6.6M in revenue per employee!! Hard to even comprehend how good that is but Anthropic is AI native as it gets so makes sense. 

3. I always thought OpenAI would drop their S-1 first 

4. Customers spend about 9x more after a year. Net Revenue Retention is approximately 900% as of Sep 30, 2026. Good SaaS companies brag about 120%.

5. Cowork is growing faster than Claude Code did. Goes to show you the demand for consumer products. Duo will probably rip.

6. 3 years ago this company did $41M in revenue. In the first six months of 2026, it did $16.3 billion. I don't think anyone has a mental model for that curve yet, I sure don’t. 

7. Nearly half of revenue comes through cloud marketplaces. About 48% comes from customers buying through them. Big companies buy where their budget already lives, and the lesson for founders selling to enterprises is to get listed where your buyers already spend.

8. Their run rate formula is published: the last 28 days of usage times 13, plus subscriptions times 12, which i guess is the new ARR math for founders?

9. It looks like They're merging Cowork into Claude dot au which tells you the chat box era is ending and the "go do the work for me" era is here.

10. Thousands of Anthropic employees are about to become liquid at once, so expect the biggest wave of new AI startups and angel checks San Francisco has ever seen. Reminds me when Facebook went public but this is way bigger. 

Let’s go! 

11. Buried in the filing, Anthropic says the gap between what Claude can do and how widely it's used is one of its biggest growth opportunities, so the company itself is telling you the models are ahead of the market and someone has to close that gap for dentists, landlords, and plumbers.

12. Whatever happens, exciting times to be building in AI.

Every SoV has tradeoffs. Every. Single. One. 

$ORE $BTC $ZEC https://t.co/fdN166aq9u
author: sacha
quoted_text:
The Zcash bug is a reminder that every non-sovereign SoV asset sits somewhere on a spectrum of tradeoffs.

A big part of Bitcoin’s genius is its relative simplicity. Bitcoin is making the tradeoff of avoiding complex shielded privacy at the protocol level, which makes verification and supply auditing much simpler.

@Zcash chose a different point on the spectrum: stronger privacy, but more cryptographic complexity and more room for soundness bugs.

I’m still a believer in Zcash, and in fact I added to my PA today. It has one of crypto's strongest cypherpunk communities, and these trauma-bonding moments are often what forge the conviction needed to survive as a belief asset. And these are belief assets at the end of the day.

But Bitcoin is making tradeoffs too.

The Bitcoin asset must secure the Bitcoin blockchain. That works beautifully if blockspace demand and fee revenue continue to grow over time. But what happens if economic activity on the L1 stagnates? What happens if the chain struggles to improve performance, lower fees, or grow a native onchain eco?

I think the design space for crypto stores of value is much larger than most people appreciate.

If you’ve followed me for a while, you know I post about @ORE frequently.

The reason for which is that it occupies a very compelling point on the tradeoff spectrum: a non-sovereign SoV that natively inherits @Solana’s performance and ecosystem, while remaining separate from the L1 security asset itself.

I believe a non-sovereign SoV can be divorced from the responsibility of securing the L1 it lives on. It can instead inherit the performance, composability, and settlement assumptions of a chain that is already scaling, while remaining natively integrated with a thriving DeFi economy, without relying on trusted third parties (bridges, CEX wrappers, etc). It also can immutably freeze core components of the system (e.g. ORE's mint is frozen and can never be changed).

Of course ORE too makes a tradeoff in that it depends on Solana's survival. What is the optimal set of tradeoffs long term? We shall see.

text:
今天纳斯达克开市钟是 BNB 敲响的，
CZ 站在时代广场的台上，
很多人以为是币安上市了，其实是另一件同样重要的事。

❚ 先分清楚

上市公司叫 BNB Standard，纳斯达克代码 BNC
它不是币安，是一家持有大量 BNB 的上市公司
类似 Strategy 对 BTC 的角色

❚ 它是怎么来的

- 前身是 CEA Industries，一家农业温控设备公司
- 2025 年在 YZi Labs 等支持下转型做 BNB 金库，大量买入 BNB
- 2026 年 7 月底，持有 515,544 枚 BNB，占总资产 93.1%
- 2026 年 9 月，社区投票后正式更名 BNB Standard，保留代码 BNC
- 10 月 19 日，前 YZi Labs 投资合伙人、高盛背景的 Alex Odagiu 出任 CEO
- 10 月 26 日，在时代广场敲响纳斯达克开市钟

❚ 为什么说是里程碑

1/ 给传统资金开了一扇门
很多机构和基金不能直接买币，但可以买美股，
买 BNC，就是间接持有 BNB。

2/ CZ 亲自站台
一个生态的创始人出现在一家金库公司的敲钟现场，信号很明确。

3/ 从「囤币」到「经营」
公司计划跑 BNB Chain 验证节点，把 BNB 变成质押收益，
不只是买了放着，是让资产本身生钱。

4/ 管理层和持币人绑在一起
CEO 的股权激励里，BNC 股价占 35%，每股净 BNB 持有量占 35%，收入覆盖率占 30%，
管理层要拿到奖励，就得让每一股对应的 BNB 越来越多。

❚ 和整个 BNB 生态放在一起看

这个月 BNB 生态的两件大事：
链上，BNB Chain 公布新 L1，CZ 说「多条链，一种币」，
链下，BNB 金库公司在纳斯达克敲钟。

一个在增加 BNB 的用途
一个在增加 BNB 的买家

❚ 也要留意的

- 股价和每股 BNB 价值会有溢价或折价，买之前看一下公司的净资产看板
- 金库公司增持靠融资，融资方式会影响每股价值
- 股价波动会被 BNB 本身的波动放大

❚ 我的看法

BNB 这几年一直被当成「币圈内部的资产」，今天这一槌，把它正式带进了美股的视野里。

接下来看下一次持仓更新，验证节点什么时候上线，以及有没有更多机构出现在 BNC 的股东名单里。
author: jici6182131
quoted_text:
BNB Chain 要再造一条链。

CZ 已经亲自确认：多条链，一种币。

大部分人只看到200 毫秒，其实还有更有意思的东西。

❚ 先说结论

- 新 L1，名字待定，和 BSC 并行运行，不是替代
- 不发新币，Gas、质押、治理全部用 BNB
- 两条链用官方原生双向桥连接
- 内部多验证者开发网已经在跑，2026 年底公开测试网，2027 年初主网

❚ 为什么不直接升级 BSC

BSC 跑了这么多年，累积的历史状态越来越重
节点硬盘和 I/O 压力越来越大
想在不牺牲安全的前提下再快一大截，很难

所以分工：
BSC 继续做通用合约和 DeFi
新链专门服务对延迟敏感的业务

❚ 快在哪？

出块和预确认
200 毫秒出一个块
块里再切子块，约 20 毫秒就把交易预确认推给用户

排序和执行分开
节点先定顺序、先达成共识，不等合约算完就出块
状态更新放到后台异步去跑
交易顺序大约 1 秒内锁定

换掉状态树
扔掉以太坊从第一天就在用的 Merkle-Patricia 树
改用扁平的键值存储，硬盘读写压力小很多

❚ 文档里容易被忽略的三件事

1/ 原生账户抽象
直接支持 Passkey 签名（就是手机人脸、指纹那种）、Gas 代付、一次最多 64 个操作打包
不需要第三方服务，上链门槛会低很多

2/ 可选隐私池
用 zk-SNARK 隐藏发送方、接收方和金额
做交易的人都懂，大单不想被所有人盯着

3/ 手续费规则变了
基础费固定为 0，完全靠优先费定价
而且按你声明的 Gas 上限收费，用不完也不退
对高频交易机器人来说，这意味着要更精确地估 Gas

❚ 目标很明确

官方列的场景：高速撮合、链上订单簿、永续合约、实时支付、AI 代理。

对标的就是 Solana、Sui、Aptos、Hyperliquid 在链上金融这条赛道。

这两年 Hyperliquid、Aster、Lighter 跑出来之后，所有人都看明白了：链上合约是真需求。

谁的链最快、最便宜、用户最多，谁就能拿下这块生意。

从技术上来看，这套设计很务实：不硬改老链，另起一条专用车道。

代币上，对 BNB 是纯增量，没有新币分流。

竞争上，它要打的是一场硬仗，因为对手都已经跑在前面了。

接下来最值得看的是年底的公开测试网：哪些协议先上、有没有头部 Perp 项目进来。

200多家小neocloud死一批，这个没悬念。大部分是几千张卡靠短约过日子的，利率5%加上GPU折旧，不用债市关门它们也活不过2027。

1生死线画错了。他说的是有没有AI以外的收入，但10月22号花旗给了 $NBIS 35亿，利率SOFR加2.75，Nebius没有什么AI以外的收入。 $IREN 靠客户预付款活着，也没有。真正关门的是无担保债，有投资级客户合同做抵押的钱一直在流。所以分界线不是收入来源，是合同对手方的信用等级。 $CRWV 的问题不是它是neocloud，是它350亿无担保债加上客户里有OpenAI这种自己也在烧钱的。

2小鱼死了对大鱼不是利好。死掉的neocloud GPU不会消失，会以三四折的价格被转手，2027年市场上多出一堆便宜算力，租金往下走。马斯克自己说偏好签短约按市场价，这是在赌租金涨。如果他说的两百家真死了，租金是跌的，他的短约策略先挨打。他的两句话互相矛盾。

3他在给自己的400亿债路演。SpaceX刚上市，刚借了400亿买GPU，走SPV不进表，这个结构跟Meta那8250亿表外承诺没本质区别。
他需要市场相信两件事，AI算力不过剩，但别人借不到钱。这两件事同时成立的时候SpaceX是唯一赢家。所以这条帖子的目的不是分析行业，是定义谁是安全资产。

真正决定这三家命运的不是马斯克，是这周三周四谷歌微软亚马逊的capex指引。 neocloud的需求本质上是超大厂溢出的需求，超大厂继续加capex，有合同的neocloud就能继续用合同融资，债市关不关门无所谓；超大厂一减速，再干净的资产负债表也没用，因为没人租。

所以我的判断是： 死的是小的，活的不一定是SpaceX，2027年真正的赢家是手里有现金、能四折接盘GPU的人，可能是微软谷歌，可能是黑石，不太可能是一个刚借了400亿的人。

text:
BSC 上的 AI Agent：从能运行到能协作 ⬇️

上一节我们介绍了 ERC-8183：它把 Agent 的任务、预算托管、结果提交和验收结算组织成一套流程。但 Agent 还需要另一种更轻量的能力：每次调用数据、API 或模型时，能不能直接按次付费？这一篇聊 x402，以及它和 B402、ERC-8183 的关系。

1️⃣ x402 是什么？

x402 把付款放进一次普通的网络请求里。Agent 请求一项付费服务时，服务方可以返回 HTTP 402，并说明价格、支持的币种和网络、收款地址等要求。Agent 的支付工具按权限签名付款，再带着付款凭证重试请求；付款验证和结算完成后，服务方返回数据或服务结果。

举个例子：Agent 要查一份实时行情数据，不必先买月费套餐或单独配置一套 API 付款流程，而是按这次请求支付费用。实际是否自动付款，取决于 Agent 钱包和支付工具的配置与授权。

2️⃣ B402 和 x402 是什么关系？

x402 是支付协议；B402 是 Binance Pay 面向商户和 Agent 支付场景提供的接入网络。放在 BNB Agent Studio 的例子里，Agent 可以通过 B402 商户网络，使用 x402 按次购买 CoinMarketCap 的数据服务。

BNB Chain 官方公布的例子包括查询 DEX 交易对、代币报价和市场列表。付款从 Agent 自己的钱包发起，服务方验证并结算后，再把数据返回给 Agent。

3️⃣ Agent 不只能付钱，也能收钱

BNB Agent Studio v1 先让 Agent 能花钱买模型额度和数据服务。官方介绍的 v2 又增加了收费服务的方向：Agent 可以开放自己的服务，其他用户或 Agent 按次付费，收入结算到它的钱包。

所以 x402 对 Agent 经济有两面：一面是 Agent 买数据、用模型；另一面是 Agent 把自己的能力做成服务并收款。

4️⃣ x402 和 ERC-8183 别混为一谈

x402 主要解决“这一次请求怎么付款”，
ERC-8183 主要解决“这项工作怎么约定、托管预算、提交结果并验收”，
两者可以搭配：任务流程由 ERC-8183 组织，具体服务调用或付款由 x402 完成。

不过，自动付款不是“Agent 获得了无限制花钱权”。钱仍来自用户配置的钱包，能花多少、能付给谁，取决于钱包权限和支出规则。测试 Agent 时，最好使用独立钱包，并设置额度或收款方限制。

把这几篇连起来看：
Agent Studio 帮忙创建和部署；
ERC-8004 让 Agent 有可查询的身份；
ERC-8183 管任务与验收；
x402 则让它能按次购买服务，也能向别人收费。
它们拼起来，
才是 Agent 从“能运行”走向“能协作”的基础流程。

quoted_text:
BSC 上的 AI Agent：从能运行到能协作 ⬇️

上一节我们介绍了 ERC-8004：它让 Agent 有一个公开、可查询的链上身份。身份解决了“它是谁、怎么找到它”，但还没回答“找到之后，怎么交任务、验收和付款”。这一篇聊 ERC-8183。

1️⃣ 先谈好任务，再把钱放进托管

ERC-8183 可以理解成一套链上任务订单。委托方和服务方先谈好工作内容、交付标准和价格，再创建任务，把预算存入智能合约托管。

钱不会因为 Agent 接了任务就立刻打给它。服务方执行工作后提交结果，任务状态和结算过程则由合约记录。

2️⃣ 交付之后，按规则决定付款还是退款

一笔任务大致会经过：创建任务、托管预算、Agent 提交结果、验收、结算。

验收通过，托管款支付给服务方；任务被拒绝或到期，则按合约规则退款。交付文件可以放在链下，链上记录任务状态及相关验证信息。

BNB Agent SDK 当前文档中的参考实现采用乐观式评估：Agent 提交结果后进入争议窗口；窗口内没有人提出争议，就按默认规则通过。如果委托方提出争议，则由白名单投票者按规则裁定。结算交易可以由任何人触发。

3️⃣ 托管不等于质量保证

智能合约能按约定管理资金和任务状态，但不能自动判断一份报告是否专业、一个策略是否有效。实际保障取决于任务描述是否清楚、谁负责验收、争议窗口如何设置，以及采用什么裁定规则。

ERC-8183 和 ERC-8004 是两层不同的能力，可以组合使用，但彼此独立。ERC-8004 回答“这个 Agent 是谁、怎么找到它”；ERC-8183 回答“这笔任务怎么托管、验收和结算”。

如果把 Agent 经济想成一个服务市场，ERC-8004 像可查询的服务名片，ERC-8183 则像带托管和验收流程的订单。

下一篇聊聊 Agent 怎样按次付费调用模型和服务：x402。

text:
Anthropic, a ~$1.9T company filed to go public today.

@entropyIO's io:ANTH (~$50M OI, 12x max leverage as of today) had already been pricing it for 68 days on Hyperliquid, while tradexyz only listed it a few hours ago.

What's the difference btwn the two HIP-3 markets?

@tradexyz prices 1 share of a real stock: Anthropic Class A, Nasdaq: ANT. Until today’s S-1 that share had no ticker, no exchange and no date.

So every tradexyz pre-IPO market is built around the filing:

- An anticipated listing date (ANT’s is the 20th of November).
- 60 days of grace (no listing by the 19th of Jan and it settles to its lifetime TWAP).
- A discretionary $125 start, ±50% bounds and an oracle fed only by its own book.

A bridge from filing to first public price, so if no filing = nothing to bridge.

Couldn’t they list per share earlier?

Not really. On the 17th of Sep Anthropic split 10-for-1 (it’s in the S-1). A per-share perp live in August would have needed its price cut 10x overnight, and HIP-3 can’t rescale a live market.

Yet Entropy's io:ANTH, live a month before the split, never even noticed.

Why?

- It quotes market cap, $1 = $1B. Splits, new share classes and converting notes don’t touch it.
- Its oracle blends the book with a RedStone feed of private-market prices. Deep book, the book leads. Thin book, the feed holds it.
- The clock is 2 years (much longer). No IPO by the 18th of Aug 2028 and it settles to a 6-month TWAP.

That's why Entropy can list anything with a private market behind it and why io:OAI already trades too, even tho there is no S-1.

Where both books sit rn:

- io:ANTH: $1,881 = $1.88T valuation, $50M OI, $19.9M 24h volume.
- xyz:ANT: $115 (-8% from the $125 start), $2.2M OI, $7M volume on day one. At ~16.9B fully diluted shares (Fortune’s estimate, the S-1 leaves it blank), $115 = ~$1.94T.

Two designs, yet only ~3% apart.

What’s next?

- 3 days before listing Entropy goes book-only, then hands over to the public price. ANTH stays a market cap perp for life.

text:
Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

text:
We talk a lot about moving money “at par” at TBMC. As much as we love a good golf analogy (@LayneHaber), that’s not what we’re talking about.

“At par” means a dollar should always remain worth a dollar even in transit.  With stablecoins today, that's not how it works.

When you convert one stablecoin to another or move across chain, you often experience slippage. This is par value of a dollar breaking. It’s unacceptable. We can’t credibly call stablecoins better money until this is fixed.

That’s what we’re doing here at TBMC.
author: AdamZuck13
quoted_text:
$1 should equal $1. That’s what moving money “at par” means. Most stablecoin conversions today don’t work that way.

That’s because they run through crypto trading rails: exchanges and market makers. Swap 100,000 USDA into USDB that way, and what arrives depends on the market at that moment. If the best buyer is paying $0.999, you get about 99,900 USDB. That gap is slippage.

The Better Money Company’s clearinghouse takes the trade out of the process. We redeem USDA and mint USDB directly with the issuers, so every step happens at par.

text:
一个失控的“疯子”与一个可控的政治阴谋家？到底哪个更加“安全”？

说起这个观点我自己都觉得有点惊讶，此时此刻从来没有想过自己会希望内塔尼亚胡可以在本次以色列大选中胜出

并不是我支持内塔尼亚胡，也并不是希望美伊继续产生巨大的矛盾与摩擦，而是我认为，一旦内塔尼亚胡败选，一个失控的疯子，可能为了保全自己，将会对伊朗发起大规模袭击，甚至引动中东地缘风险大乱

内塔尼亚胡出任以色列总理18年之久，我们很难相信一场败选可以彻底击垮他，甚至即便是败选，他所掌控的军方权利也很难在短期被剥夺

此前内塔尼亚胡承受多项指控，从而导致他努力的发动对外战争，以“战争英雄”的身份多次拉高自身的支持率，所以战争是内塔尼亚胡支持率的根基之一，而以色列内部确实也有很多人支持内塔

所以，按照这个视角下来看，一旦内塔尼亚败选，为了让自己获得更多的政治斡旋空间，很有可能会大规模对伊朗进行袭击，战时状态下内塔尼亚胡可以保留更多的战时权利

其实这个逻辑对特朗普也是有用的，必要时刻，如果特朗普无法换区伊朗的和平方案，他是可以对伊朗实施更加强硬的战争态度换区美国单一强硬派的支持

所以，综合评估之下，我觉得与其让一个疯子失控不如让他继续安稳的坐在以色列总理的位置上，这样短期地缘风险可以大大降低，缺点是未来祸端依旧存在

我为什么担心新一次的美伊冲突，因为这次冲突可能不只是美伊之间，还有以色列，还有胡赛与沙特，而土耳其，巴勒斯坦都可能作为《麦加共同防御协议》合作方参与其中

对于地缘战争，参与的国家越多，越容易擦枪走火，战争风险就越大，甚至可能会让战争风险加速外溢，一旦中东地缘风险传导至周边地区，那就是失控的危险局面。而且一旦各方打上头，就算是美中俄，也难以压制！

当然，我是非常希望媒体的这篇报道只是为了释放压力与恐吓伊朗，如果是这样可能真是最好的结果!

as a counter to anthropic s1 glaze

majority of q2 was the height of tokenmaxxing where companies were spending as much money as possible on credits 

it wasn’t until july where the idea of managing ai spend started to get traction

also q2 was peak Opus 4.7 & Mythos/Fable season hype vs GPT-5.5, and Codex didn’t really take over until 5.6 during the summer

i love anthropic’s products though and probably will slam the ipo because it’s first pure play ai lab

but the belief that the headwinds for the ai trade have disappeared because of this document is not accurate

>models have never been more commoditized than they are right now

i used to be able to tell the difference between model outputs, now it’s almost impossible 

the more they get commoditized, the more the margins compress. this was not clear in q2. it is now.

>still no clear proof of how ai drives more profit to most businesses

most of anthropic’s biggest customers are publicly traded companies & they will be incentivized to decrease their own Claude spend to improve their own margins

>capex commitments already signed until 2034

every hyperscaler & lab has been racing to sign deals spanning the next decade. this is all priced in already.

this means the labs/mag7 basically either find ways to make existing chips more efficient (deepseek deepinfer type stuff) or they dilute shares to spend more on capex. 

either way stocks go down in both those scenarios

—

i am an ai bull but i believe the winners have still not been decided

i think muse is great but does anyone know if it can drive hundreds of billions of dollars in value to Meta? well that’s what’s priced in and that’s what it would take for the investment to be worthwhile.

—

of course a lot can change but it feels like the real ai trade will take place after this current one settles down 

the real one will take time, just don’t see how it’s going to be this business cycle

author: alex_hunter20
quoted_text:
Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

B神说了一句话："区块链不止承载金融资产，还能承载可验证生产工具！"这句话怎么理解？

过去我们最熟悉的区块链用途，是记账、转账、跑智能合约规则。TapeOut 换了个角度：把电脑最底层的逻辑元件搬上链，让人从 NAND 这种最小的积木开始，搭出真正能运算的电路。

关键在"可复用"。一个人设计出能完成某种运算的电路，上链后是公开的、可验证的。别的开发者不用从零开始，可以研究它、调用它，再和别的电路组合，做出更复杂的功能。加法器、计数器，再往上是能按指令运算的 CPU。

这样链上慢慢积累下来的就不只是资产，而是一个越来越大的工具箱。

社区也在往游戏逻辑、AI 结果验证这些方向尝试，不过它们处在不同阶段，有的是技术展示，有的还在研究，别把探索当成已经落地。方向是清楚的：让后来的人站在前人的电路上继续造东西。

text:
DeFi 最讽刺的一幕出现了，你辛辛苦苦建立流动性池，Uniswap 却可以调用你的流动性，顺便把产生的协议费拿去烧自己的 UNI。

 Uniswap 最近上线的 Aggregator Hooks，就是让Uniswap v4 利用 Hook 机制，将 Curve、PancakeSwap、Fluid 等外部协议的流动性封装成 v4 可识别的池。路由器可以统一比较不同协议的报价，组合最优路径，并在单笔链上交易中完成结算。

更有意思的是，通过这些外部流动性执行的交易，也会产生用于销毁 UNI 的协议费。

这意味着 Uniswap 不需要拥有所有流动性，也能参与外部交易的价值捕获。

以前 DEX 竞争主要拼 TVL，谁的池子深、滑点低，谁就更有优势。但当流动性逐渐可以被统一调用，竞争重心就开始从 Liquidity Ownership 转向 Order Flow 和 Execution。

再看 v4 Hooks，就更有意思了。

动态费率、KYC 准入、MEV 管理、自动化流动性策略，都可以通过 Hook 实现。

机构 RWA 需要合规准入、权限控制和稳定的交易环境，散户 Meme 则需要低门槛、高效率和灵活的价格发现机制。

看似完全不同的两个市场，现在可以共享一套底层基础设施，只需要配置不同的交易规则。

Uniswap 想做的，不再只是一个交易市场，而是让开发者基于它创造不同类型的市场。

我甚至觉得，这套架构是在为 Agentic Finance 铺路。

未来 AI Agent 可以自主寻找流动性、比较滑点和 Gas、选择最优交易路径，再通过智能合约执行交易。届时，DEX 的竞争可能进一步从 UI 转向 API，以及谁能提供更可靠、可验证的执行能力。

但这里存在一个悖论：Uniswap 想通过协议费捕获更多价值，同时又必须提供足够有竞争力的成交价格。如果额外收费损害了执行质量，订单流完全可以转向其他聚合器。

所以，我真正关注的不是 UNI 短期能烧掉多少，而是 Uniswap 能否在保持执行优势的同时，建立可持续的协议收入。

DeFi 下一轮竞争，可能不再是谁拥有最多流动性，而是谁能成为钱包、应用乃至 AI Agent 默认调用的交易基础设施。

从 Liquidity 到 Execution，再到 Programmable Markets，这才是 Uniswap 这轮升级真正值得关注的地方。

quoted_text:
Hyperliquid 正在调整交易“加速通道”的使用规则，已上线测试网 🫡

先用一句话解释：

做市商、交易机器人很在意速度，哪怕只快一点点，也可能影响收益。Hyperliquid 允许他们支付额外的 HYPE，让订单更早被处理，或让同价位的挂单排得更靠前。支付的 HYPE 会被销毁。

Jeff 这次公布的更新，主要有四点：

🟠 想追求速度，需要选对账户模式

专业交易者需要使用 Standard（标准账户），把现货、合约等资金分别管理。

统一账户、组合保证金虽然方便统筹资金，但无法享受这次所说的交易池优先处理。

普通用户照常交易即可。

🟠 交易时夹杂其他操作，可能暂时拖慢整组账户

如果账户在下单、撤单、改单的同时，还发起转账等其他操作，那么在这些操作处理完成前，交易指令的排队优先级也会下降。

同一主账户下的子账户、自己管理的交易金库，也会一起受到影响。

🟠 直接用过特殊接口的钱包，会降低排队优先级

这里涉及 CoreWriter，可以把它理解为连接 HyperEVM 和 HyperCore 的一座桥。

曾经用钱包直接通过这个接口发送指令的账户，会被降低排队优先级。Jeff 同时强调，大多数应用通过智能合约调用它的常见用法不受影响。

text:
Anthropic just destroyed one of the biggest bear cases against the entire AI industry.

According to its IPO filing, Anthropic had approximately $131.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short term investments as of June 30, 2026. That is an insane amount of liquidity for a company that's investing billions into AI infrastructure while continuing to grow at an incredible pace. But what's even more interesting is that Anthropic is now generating positive operating cash flow and has started turning an operating profit. During the first half of 2026, the company generated approximately $3.9 billion in operating cash flow and $1.6 billion in adjusted operating income. In Q2 alone, it generated nearly $1 billion in GAAP operating profit.

This is important because one of the biggest concerns surrounding frontier AI companies has been how much capital they'll need to continue scaling. A lot of people have assumed these companies would need to constantly raise money just to keep up with their infrastructure spending, but Anthropic's financials are starting to challenge that assumption. Now, Anthropic still has enormous infrastructure commitments ahead of it, so that $131.7 billion isn't necessarily money it can freely spend on anything. And while its cash position is impressive, the company also has significant liabilities and convertible preferred stock on its balance sheet. But here's what I find interesting. Anthropic is growing at an incredible pace, its profitability is improving, and it already has enough liquidity to support a significant amount of future investment. The IPO looks increasingly like an opportunity to strengthen its balance sheet and fund additional expansion rather than something the company desperately needs to survive.

And I think this has much bigger implications for the AI infrastructure industry. If companies like Anthropic can eventually finance more of their infrastructure spending through cash generated by their own businesses, it could make the AI investment cycle much more sustainable than people currently expect. That's especially important for companies supplying the compute, memory, networking, and power that these frontier labs will continue needing.
author: MelvinInvests
quoted_text:
Anthropic just filed for its IPO and some of these numbers are absolutely insane.

The company generated $16.3 billion in revenue during the first half of 2026, compared to just $1.1 billion during the same period last year. That's incredible growth but what I find even more interesting is how much money Anthropic is spending to sustain it. Anthropic reportedly lost $80.7 billion during the first six months of 2026, although roughly $72 billion came from non cash accounting charges related to convertible financing. So the actual cash burn is nowhere near that headline number. However, the company still spent nearly $9 billion on compute and infrastructure during that period and has at least $518 billion in longer term infrastructure commitments.

And now we have Anthropic reportedly agreeing to spend up to $120.5 billion on computing capacity from SpaceX through 2029, with payments potentially reaching $3.1 billion per month once all the capacity is delivered. We're talking about a company spending billions every single month just to secure enough compute to remain competitive. Meanwhile, Anthropic is expanding its revolving credit commitments from $3.3 billion to $15 billion and increasing its minimum liquidity requirement from $500 million to $5 billion. Essentially, the company is securing access to significantly more financing while making sure it has enough cash available to support these enormous commitments. Another interesting detail is that Anthropic's seven co-founders will retain 50.1% of the voting power through a special Class F share that carries no economic rights. So even after going public, the founders will maintain control over major corporate decisions regardless of how much outside investors contribute.

Personally, I think Anthropic is an incredible business, but I've also been saying for a while now that frontier AI labs are being valued way too aggressively. Growing revenue at this pace is impressive, but eventually investors are going to want to see how much of that revenue actually turns into profits after paying for all this infrastructure. And this is exactly why I continue to prefer the infrastructure side of AI. Whether Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX, or another frontier lab comes out ahead, they all need compute, memory, networking, and power to keep scaling. The AI labs are spending hundreds of billions competing against each other, and the infrastructure companies are the ones collecting those checks.

Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

text:
Claude Code found stalkerware on my sister's Android phone. a hidden app with no icon, called "System Service", that had been sending her location, messages and call log to a server every 15 minutes for 5 months.

she told me her ex always seemed to know where she was. we thought she was being paranoid.

i connected her phone to my MacBook with USB debugging on and ran Claude Code. it found a package with no launcher icon, installed by hand from an APK, not from the Play Store.

package → com.sys.***.service
server → 185.***.***.62
location → Netherlands
last upload → 11 minutes ago
installed → 5 months ago

someone had her unlocked phone in their hands for about 2 minutes. that is all this kind of app needs. after that it hides itself and runs in the background.

what it had access to:

→ accessibility service (it can read everything on the screen)
→ notification access (every message preview, every app)
→ device admin (so she couldn't uninstall it the normal way)
→ location, microphone, call log, SMS

Google Play Protect was switched off. she never turned it off. that is the first thing these apps do.

this is not rare. Kaspersky counted over 31,000 people hit by stalkerware in 2023 alone. and this kind of app needs someone holding the unlocked phone to install it.

she didn't cry. she just went very quiet and asked how long. 5 months.

what we did that night:

→ took screenshots of everything first, in case she needs it as evidence
→ removed device admin, then uninstalled the app
→ turned Play Protect back on and ran a full scan
→ changed her Google password and every other password from my phone, not hers
→ set a new screen lock pin that nobody else knows

Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

While evaluating Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in a controlled sandbox environment, Cohere's research team observed something unexpected.

text:
an update on the openai/codex ban:

i was curious about my tv, found a vuln (not with codex), popped a shell, and started poking around. the intrigue of my hobby project while i had the flu wasn't something i could've predicted.

to be clear: the ban almost certainly had nothing to do with using openai -specifically- for my samsung reverse engineering work. i have no reason to believe it did.

the real issue seems deeper. i talked to friends using astra/6.1 sol for both cyber work and normal software tasks. the ones who never hit daybreak (and weren't in the blue program) said they spend a while "warming it up", getting the agent into a flowstate with substitute words and roundabout explanations that jailbreak the context. once that's done, the agent starts talking the same way and skipping tokens.

if you do serious reverse engineering without those jailbreaks, daybreak's content-hidden tripwire looks at the prompt or output in isolation and sees something indistinguishable from malware development.

i think the better fix is making the system track intent across the whole context (and through compressions) instead of punishing blunt technical language.

i believe i got banned because i just used normal terms. talking about memory, trampoline hooks, encrypted/read-protected pages, even entirely locally, looks sinister out of context. once daybreak trips, it poisons the context cache. new conversations start failing too. eventually even normal tooling work and /goals would randomly trip it. arguing your case makes it worse.

the incentives here seem strange to me. people who obfuscate from the start never seem to have problems. people who just use the actual terminology get more and more refusals.

account's still closed. pretty sure it's just from tripping daybreak too many times (even on non-cyber work).

for now i'm moving to open weight models and locking down my own compute. if these tools are part of how you work now, it's worth thinking about how to keep reliable access.

please don't harass tibo, roon or other oai people. from their public comments it sounds like they already know and agree the current setup is too strict.

sorry for the interlude, brb, back to getting the report and a repo out to fix TVs.

text:
An open letter to my Catholic friends

I write this because I care about you, and because the question of how a person is right with God is too important to leave unsaid.

Many of you have been taught that the Church is the Ark. Stay inside it, receive the sacraments, follow the rules, and you will be saved. Infant baptism is said to remove original sin. Sunday Mass and confession to a priest are said to keep you in grace, one week at a time. Venial sins that remain will be burned away in purgatory. Mortal sins are handled by the sacrament of penance. 

In this system, belonging to the Church and using its means becomes the way of salvation. Personal trust in Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord is treated as secondary, or as already covered by the institution.

The apostles did not teach this.

They preached that Jesus Christ died for sins and rose again, and that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness and eternal life (Acts 10:43; 13:38–39; John 3:16; 5:24). 

They called people to repent and believe the gospel. Baptism followed as the sign of that faith, not as the automatic removal of original sin in an infant who has not believed. The Lord’s Supper was given so that believers would remember him until he comes, not as a propitiatory sacrifice that maintains justification week by week. Confession of sin was made to God, and to one another, not as the necessary channel through which a priest restores lost grace (1 John 1:9). 

And no apostle spoke of a purifying fire after death that finishes what the blood of Jesus left incomplete. 

“The blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin” 

The Ark in Scripture is Christ himself. Noah was saved by entering the ark God provided. We are saved by coming to the Savior God provided. The Church is the gathered people who have already come to him. It is not the vessel that carries those who have never personally trusted him. 

Rules and sacraments can mark the life of faith. They cannot replace the faith. If justification is maintained by weekly rites and restored by priestly absolution, then it is no longer the free gift received by faith in the finished work of Christ. It has become a status managed by the institution.

I am not asking you to hate the Church or to despise every good thing you have received in it. I am asking you to ask whether you are relying on Christ alone. Have you come to him as your own Savior and Lord? Have you trusted his death and resurrection as the full payment for your sins, or are you trusting the system to keep you saved one week at a time? 

The apostles’ answer was clear: believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved. Everything else follows that. Nothing else replaces it.

Come to Jesus. He will not cast out the one who comes. And his blood is enough.

This is not a battle between churches.
It is not a contest of denominations.
It is not a debate about which fathers said what.
It is a call to see what is most important: Jesus Christ, and Him crucified and risen, received by faith. 

Everything else is secondary. He is not.

text: This is key in the whole AI conversation.  The context in how some LLM is being used: is it being used thoughtlessly like "I just vibe coded this whole thing and didn't check anything bro" vs attention to detail and thoughtful usage.  The challenge is how opaque the usage is unless people disclose or are obvious based on their discourse.
author: Term_Ten
quoted_text:
Does this mean I think someone cannot have attention to detail while using AI? No. But currently, AI — as an umbrella term but used in this context — is very obviously referring to varying degrees of prompting an LLM and briefly checking output (but often not intermediates, e.g. code), which is a workflow *specifically about* ignoring details.

Beyond LLMs shoehorned into everything, machine learning, neural networks, and the broader class of statistically predictive or learning mechanisms are obviously useful, particularly when they are employed in context, with a purpose. Artist, gameplay programmer, and engine programming tools can very obviously be empowered by such things. But what people are doing currently with the half-baked LLM version is not “same level of detail, just faster”, it’s largely just turning their brains off. Players may not realize all of the details, but they are completely justified in their distaste for this.

text:
How much does a code graph actually help a powerful coding agent?

I've been benchmarking Enola against Claude Code running Opus 5.5, using private codebases the model had never seen before. Five repositories, four programming languages, and around 820,000 lines of code.

The results were quite interesting. On cross-repository questions, the agent produced 18/20 exact answers with Enola, compared with 4/20 without it. Enola's underlying structural analysis was correct in all 20 trials, but the agent still managed to get two final answers wrong despite having the correct information available.

On several endpoint-analysis questions, Enola also significantly reduced execution time and cost. There were also cases where Opus performed perfectly well on its own, particularly when a simple search or script was enough to answer the question.

What I'm most interested in is where the boundary lies. Which problems benefit from having a precomputed graph of the software system, and which can a capable agent solve just as effectively using the tools it already has?

I've published the benchmark methodology, results, and limitations here:

https://t.co/l168LPJEGd
